[182] The Chief of Defence's principled view of the Armed Forces' needs and development

[183] The Government's renewal program for state activities - current guidelines for NATO's defense planning - special studies and analyses

[184] In addition to this, the Defence Study has been included as important background material when assessing the defence trade-offs

[185] The report provides a status report on the implementation of the main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities during the period 1984-88. The main guidelines presented for the five-year period 1989-93 are influenced by the country's difficult economic situation

[186] In this respect, significant changes have occurred in the Defence Commission's view of the assumed economic development

[187] This is described in the message

[188] The prospects for developments in both the economic and security policy situations make it necessary to plan the Armed Forces' future activities under great uncertainty

[189] Alternative lines of development must be considered

[190] Through the planning system, political authorities must be able to overview the consequences of the budgetary choices they must make when presenting the annual defense budgets

[191] The long-term plan must provide the opportunity to make rational and well-thought-out adjustments to varying economic framework conditions

[192] With this White Paper, the Government is laying the foundation for the further development of the Armed Forces

[193] The goal is a credible, effective and enduring defense

[194] Activities must be aligned with resource availability in an optimal manner with the aim of achieving the highest possible defense capability

[195] Given the size, complexity and scope of the Armed Forces, it is neither desirable nor practically possible to make dramatic changes within such a short timeframe as five years, but it is important that the changes that are necessary take place within long-term overall planning

[196] The resources that can be made available for defense purposes during the period will, under any circumstances, not be sufficient to meet all needs

[197] It is therefore necessary to strictly prioritize tasks and resource use, and to continuously analyze organizational forms and measures that can counteract registered weaknesses

[198] The Chief of Defence's principled view of the Armed Forces' needs and development is set out in Appendix 1 to this report

[199] Unless otherwise stated, all krone amounts in this White Paper are stated in 1988 price levels

[200] The 1985 Defense Study is included as an unprinted appendix to the Storting's Defense Committee in graded and ungraded versions

[201] Main guidelines for the activities of the Armed Forces

[202] The main task of the Armed Forces in peacetime is to act as a deterrent to war, and to defend national independence with military means if Norway were to be attacked

[203] However, security policy encompasses more than purely military measures

[204] The defense measures are part of a broad register of security policy instruments that collectively aim to provide the country with the greatest possible security

[205] Allied defense cooperation is a cornerstone of Norwegian security policy

[206] This gives Norway a level of security that our resources alone cannot provide

[207] The joint defense system acts as a deterrent to attacks in that Norway's defense capabilities cannot be seen in isolation

[208] As a NATO member, Norway is also committed to the Alliance's equal goals of defense and détente

[209] Norwegian security policy is still based on measures of both a deterrent and reassuring nature

[210] The Norwegian security concept, which is based on a balance between deterrence and reassurance, remains firm

[211] Measures to promote Norwegian security interests in relation to new challenges are being continuously assessed

[212] Within the framework of alliance cooperation, Norway actively supports measures that can contribute to increased mutual trust between East and West at the lowest possible force level

[213] NATO's strategy of flexible response and defense in forward areas is shaped by the view that a credible deterrent capability depends on flexibility in choosing alternatives to meet an attack

[214] In Norway's view, it is important that NATO reduces its dependence on nuclear weapons, especially the early use of such weapons

[215] At the same time, the ongoing disarmament process in the wake of the INF Treaty must be continued

[216] Emphasis must be placed on a holistic approach, while it is important to avoid blocking links between further disarmament negotiations related to conventional forces, chemical weapons and tactical nuclear weapons

[217] It is necessary to continue to base NATO's strategy on an appropriate mix of sufficient and effective nuclear and conventional forces, updated where deemed necessary

[218] Furthermore, a ban on the production and stockpiling of chemical weapons must be aimed at

[219] Furthermore, negotiations must be carried out with the aim of ensuring conventional stability throughout Europe at the lowest possible force level

[220] When it comes to nuclear weapons, these must be seen in the context of the conventional balance of power

[221] Particular emphasis must be placed on reducing the number of nuclear battlefield weapons, as these can exert dangerous pressure for early use

[222] Land-based short-range missiles should be reduced to the same level

[223] The Norwegian side has high hopes for the ongoing START negotiations

[224] A possible agreement on 50 percent reductions in the superpowers' strategic nuclear weapons arsenals could have direct effects on Norwegian security to the extent that they influence the design of the superpowers' future strategic force structure

[225] With our exposed strategic location, it is important for Norway to maintain close connections with the rest of Europe

[226] Isolation and special status are always a danger for smaller countries in vulnerable positions

[227] To counter the danger, it is, among other things, an important task for Norway to emphasize the broader security policy significance of developments in the High North for Western Europe and to ensure Western European involvement in these developments

[228] From the Norwegian side, it will be a key task during the planning period to follow developments within the EC/EPS and WEU with particular attention

[229] Developments in Western Europe could pose major challenges for Norway in the years ahead

[230] Transatlantic relations will remain fundamental to Western security

[231] The United States will remain Norway's foremost military guarantor

[232] The defense of Norway must be seen in a European context, and Norway's strategic position in an Atlantic, and increasingly in an Arctic context

[233] Norwegian security policy will continue to be shaped primarily in light of our NATO participation

[234] Within the North Atlantic framework, Norwegian security interests are linked to the stated guarantee of Allied reinforcements and Allied defense of Norwegian territory

[235] Within the Western European framework, Norway must orient itself in relation to a greater Western European will to develop a stronger European pillar in the Alliance and to promote general Western European interests with which Norway wishes to identify

[236] Cooperation in the Alliance may change during the planning period

[237] There may be certain changes and adjustments regarding the distribution of tasks and responsibilities between NATO's North American and European member states

[238] A possible change in burden sharing and new forums for defense cooperation among member countries in the Alliance could present Norway with new challenges

[239] NATO consists of states that are linked by the sea

[240] The naval forces of NATO states consequently have a different role than those of the Warsaw Pact states

[241] It is necessary for NATO to have and operate naval forces that can secure the necessary maritime communication lines between the various Western states

[242] Because several of the alliance's member states, including Norway, are located in forward areas, Western naval power plays a significant role in their defense

[243] NATO's naval forces are one of the most important sources of reinforcement for Norway

[244] It is important that they practice their ability to operate in northern waters to make their commitment to come to Norway's rescue credible

[245] This is also necessary to motivate the mutual restraint that is a prerequisite for continued low voltage in the sensitive northern areas

[246] The development of the Soviet fleet and the new weapons systems that partly operate in new areas and waters in the north have made it more necessary for Norway to cooperate with other NATO states to ensure the ability to control the sea areas off Northern Norway

[247] This will also raise the defense threshold in the region

[248] The ability to ensure rapid Allied naval presence off Northern Norway is an important link in the forward protection of supply lines across the Atlantic, the defense of Norway, the British Isles and the continent

[249] A large Norwegian territory will be defended by a small population

[250] This places great demands on the Armed Forces' mobility and ability to rapidly redeploy

[251] It will not be possible to prioritize all tasks as highly as desired

[252] Resources must be deployed where they are believed to have the greatest defensive effect

[253] Norway on its own has no opportunity to balance the military force that could be deployed against us

[254] Our defense must be seen in light of NATO's combined strength

[255] Our defense planning assumes that an attack on Norway triggers the solidarity obligation in NATO

[256] The ability to mobilize quickly is a prerequisite for our success in solving the defense task

[257] This in turn depends on correct and timely political and military decisions

[258] Of particular importance is that we request allied reinforcements in a timely manner

[259] If handled correctly, this will act as a deterrent to attacks

[260] Strategic developments have given Northern Europe increased importance

[261] This is primarily due to the fact that the Soviet Union has established itself as a great power at sea

[262] Northern Norway and Southern Norway flank the outlets to the world's oceans for two of the Soviet Union's four fleets

[263] Control of the outlets is of crucial importance to the Soviet Union in both offensive and defensive contexts

[264] Southern Norway also forms an important flank position for operations in the Central European sector

[265] It is a clear goal in Norwegian security policy that defense capabilities should be maintained and that all parts of the country should be defended

[266] The goal of the defense structure is that the organization and force composition should make it possible to solve war prevention and war aversion tasks

[267] With the term "defense capability" we understand our capabilities to solve defense tasks

[268] Defence capability depends on the economic framework conditions, the personnel and material resources that society makes available, and the way in which these resources are utilized

[269] This forms the basis for the structural composition and for the combat capability that our national forces can produce

[270] However, our country is part of a defense alliance

[271] The scope and value of our own defense efforts must therefore be assessed in the context of the alliance

[272] Defense capability must be assessed on the basis of a realistic perception of the challenges that the defense may face in war

[273] It is difficult to imagine an isolated attack on Norway alone

[274] However, both Northern Norway and Southern Norway could conceivably be attacked as part of an attack on Western Europe, especially if control over Norway is considered important for the final outcome of a potential conflict

[275] Assessments of the effectiveness of the Norwegian and allied force buildup will largely determine the strategic goals an attacker can set

[276] If it is successful to neutralize the ports and airports that are central in this regard, the defense could soon find itself in a critical situation

[277] A number of factors mean that Northern Norway would likely play an important strategic role in a major war

[278] The region will continue to be prioritized in a defense context

[279] Since the resource base is limited, a defense threshold must be established even in peacetime that can hold until national and allied reinforcements arrive

[280] It is assumed that the standing Soviet forces in the north have sufficient capacity to carry out an isolated and limited attack against the northeasternmost parts of Norway without us having any preparation time of practical importance

[281] However, such an operation could trigger a widespread conflict

[282] Under the current circumstances, the risk is hardly proportionate to the possible strategic gains

[283] A more extensive attack in the north, deeper into Norwegian territory, requires larger combat-ready forces than those that are, for example, usually stationed on the Kola Peninsula

[284] Such an attack is hardly conceivable without the initiator being prepared for a major war

[285] The build-up of forces can hardly take place in secret

[286] This should give us strategic warning

[287] In the rest of the country, there is uncertainty about the factors that could influence the extent, time and location of a possible invasion

[288] It is therefore considerably more difficult to determine what should influence the choice of structure and level of ambition for the Armed Forces

[289] In Southern Norway we find the majority of the country's resources and governing bodies

[290] The region is of crucial importance for our overall defense capability, and for creating and maintaining a defense situation in the north

[291] Southern Norway is also important for the defense of the Baltic Sea outlets, and for maintaining control over the North Sea

[292] The forces that can theoretically be deployed against Southern Norway are very extensive

[293] However, the investment options are highly situational dependent

[294] Invasion seems unlikely as long as Denmark and Schleswig-Holstein are in Allied hands

[295] The scope and timing of an attack will depend heavily on the course of the conflict and the need for forces on the continent

[296] The goal for the defense in Southern Norway will initially be to secure the exercise of authority and important societal functions, and to ensure that the region's defense resources can be fully utilized

[297] The Armed Forces must ensure reception and operational capabilities for allied reinforcements

[298] The Armed Forces must also be able to support the defense struggle in Northern Norway

[299] Conditions must be prepared to support Allied operations in Northern Germany and Denmark

[300] Furthermore, the Armed Forces must be structured so that it can provide effective resistance to operations that could conceivably be launched while the conflict over the Danish straits and belts is still ongoing

[301] If the defense of the Baltic Sea outlets were to collapse, a major invasion of southern Norway could conceivably be launched after some time

[302] Our defense capability against such an attack will be limited, especially if the situation arises at the same time as we are engaged in decisive battles in Northern Norway

[303] The armed forces would then be faced with very difficult tasks

[304] Such a major attack against southern Norway could only be repelled through coordinated operations by Norwegian forces, and with significant efforts by allied combat forces

[305] The prospects for the development of the country's economy are characterized by great uncertainty

[306] In the area of security policy, we must be prepared to meet changing framework conditions

[307] The future activities of the Armed Forces must therefore be planned with the aim of being able to meet uncertainty

[308] The Government believes it is right that the Armed Forces contribute to the necessary restructuring in the period 1989-93 to correct the difficult economic situation in which the country finds itself

[309] The Armed Forces must therefore adapt to lower budget growth than has been the case in the two previous five-year periods

[310] The main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities in the coming five-year period are based on maintaining defense capabilities

[311] This is assumed to occur with total real budget growth of approximately NOK 5.6 billion, which corresponds to average annual real budget growth of two percent

[312] However, growth may vary from year to year and will need to be assessed in relation to the economic situation, among other things

[313] Defense capability must also be assessed in relation to security policy developments, especially in our immediate vicinity

[314] In addition, defense capability must be ensured through productivity growth and savings on the operating budget

[315] There will therefore be a strong focus on rationalization measures

[316] By restructuring the peace organization, it should be possible to reduce the consumption of man-years by an average of one percent per year

[317] This will, based on the 1988 level of 27,500, reduce the man-year consumption in 1993 by 1,350 to 26,150 and will result in total savings over the five-year period of just over 4,000 man-years

[318] This corresponds to an accumulated savings on salary budgets of about one billion kroner

[319] The war structure will mainly be maintained with the aim of optimal adaptation to tasks and resources

[320] The Armed Forces shall also provide support to civil society to the extent that it is compatible with its other tasks

[321] For many years, there has been a lack of balance between the level of ambition and access to resources in the Armed Forces

[322] This is the result of several circumstances that go back many years

[323] A particularly important reason is that neither the budget level nor structural objectives were adjusted in connection with the cessation of arms aid at the end of the sixties

[324] Secondly, efforts to restore balance through rationalization and efficiency have not yielded sufficient results

[325] The peace organization is too large and its operating methods too expensive

[326] Therefore, operating expenses become so high that the investment level becomes too low

[327] A fundamental review is now needed

[328] In addition, the Armed Forces have been given expanded tasks without the framework having been significantly changed

[329] This is a problem that has not only arisen in recent years

[330] It has been recurring

[331] A fundamental review of the Armed Forces would be necessary regardless of whether the proposed average growth target was 3 percent or 2 percent

[332] The difference between these targets for the period 1989-93 is NOK 2.9 billion, or 2.9 percent of the total defense spending that this report estimates

[333] Thus, the difference between these alternatives lies in the need for austerity and adjustments, but not fundamental changes

[334] The challenge is greater, however, because the current structure cannot be continued with 3 percent average annual real growth

[335] The great uncertainty associated with economic development makes it necessary to be able to plan under uncertainty

[336] The planning methods that were developed for the long period of relatively steady economic growth are not suitable for the new situation

[337] Therefore, the planning system in the Armed Forces must also be adjusted to be able to handle uncertainty and variations in resource availability to a greater extent

[338] The need for a main course in the first five-year period must be taken into account, but when the long-term course is to be set, there must be a certain range of variation between upper and lower alternatives in order to be able to handle the uncertainties

[339] One cannot steer development towards several alternatives at the same time, but long-term planning work must not be tied to a main course that cannot be adjusted over a longer period of time, when circumstances make this necessary

[340] Long-term planning is not about making unrealistic plans in a long-term perspective, but about investigating alternative development lines that can be followed if the main plan cannot be followed

[341] Long-term planning is therefore not about making decisions as early as possible, but about making them possible as late as possible

[342] In accordance with established practice, the notification is limited to a five-year period

[343] This is the last five-year period of the time period studied by the Defence Commission

[344] The report, like St report no. 94 (1978-79) and St report no. 74 (1982-83), does not indicate specific growth assumptions beyond the period studied by the Defence Commission

[345] The Ministry assumes that decisions will be made on how the development of the Armed Forces after 1993 will be examined early in the planning period

[346] The Government proposes to base the Armed Forces' activities in the period 1989-93 on the plan to restore balance in the Norwegian economy and is not intended to provide guidance for long-term development into the next century

[347] This must be investigated in the same thorough manner as the Defence Commission of 1974 investigated developments for the period

[348] A key task will be to secure sufficiently qualified personnel

[349] Measures that will strengthen gender equality in the Armed Forces will be given priority

[350] During this period, the Ministry will take a closer look at the service conditions and career opportunities of civilian employees

[351] The situation of conscripts will be followed up and assessed with the aim of ensuring good conditions

[352] The length of service will be maintained

[353] The combat capability of all branches of defense will increase

[354] The defense priority of Northern Norway will be maintained

[355] Defense resources will primarily be directed towards departments and units that are located, or planned to be transferred, to our northernmost part of the country

[356] This leads to relatively less emphasis on the defense of other parts of the country

[357] The standing army units will be strengthened and reorganized

[358] The mobilization departments will receive variable equipment, depending on their task and disposition

[359] The army's strength goals (number of brigades) and the departmental structure itself will be considered

[360] There will be a greater difference in the degree of updating between brigades that are planned to be deployed in the most vulnerable areas and those that will defend other parts of the country

[361] The Navy's numerical strength will largely be maintained

[362] The submarine program is being completed, and the modernization of the escort vessels will be carried out

[363] The MTB fleet renewal program continues, but the scope is being assessed

[364] Construction of new mine clearance vessels is about to begin

[365] The coastal artillery defense is still being strengthened, but the overall plan is under review

[366] Within the Air Force, air defense of airports and key installations will be strengthened

[367] A modern missile defense system is being established at airports in Northern Norway and Central Norway

[368] Land defense will be strengthened at all air stations

[369] The organization and scope of the rescue service will be assessed

[370] The F-5 aircraft will reach the end of their service life during the period

[371] The update of the control and warning system will continue

[372] The Home Guard's capacity and activity level will largely be maintained

[373] The development will be characterized by the supply of surplus equipment from the Army and the strengthening of armor protection

[374] The work to strengthen the UN's apparatus for conflict resolution, crisis management and peaceful settlement of disputes has been a high priority area in Norwegian foreign policy since

[375] With the lack of stability and danger of new conflicts that exist in several areas of the Third World, this task will not become less important in the years to come

[376] Given the danger of great power participation and the risk of the spread of such conflicts, this work will also have great security policy significance

[377] In the reform work underway at the UN, we, from the Norwegian side, have strongly supported the measures that have been taken to strengthen the Secretary-General's apparatus for early warning of international situations that could develop into armed conflicts

[378] The UN does not have its own forces available for peacekeeping operations

[379] It is the member states that provide forces

[380] The security policy goal of contributing to peaceful development in the world is safeguarded, among other things, by the Armed Forces earmarking and training a special emergency force that can be made available to the UN at short notice

[381] The Armed Forces will contribute to maintaining and developing technological environments for defense equipment and participate in international collaborative projects

[382] The Armed Forces will participate to a greater extent in the development of products that will meet specific Norwegian requirements

[383] Emphasis will continue to be placed on suitable high technology in future procurements

[384] Investment needs in construction are large

[385] Projects that have a direct impact on the Armed Forces' combat capability will be given priority, including ammunition depots, but emphasis will also be placed on measures that promote well-being such as welfare buildings, barracks and messes for officers and privates, and housing

[386] The jointly financed projects mainly include measures for the reception and support of allied forces and the updating and renewal of systems for warning, communication, command, control and information

[387] In connection with the planning and implementation of the Armed Forces' construction projects, emphasis will be placed on ensuring that the information in necessary discussions with affected landowners, municipalities, counties and interest organizations is sufficiently comprehensive and available in a timely manner

[388] Through advance storage of heavier equipment for allied forces that are likely to be deployed in Norway, the dependence on sea transport for the transfer of reinforcement forces has been reduced

[389] Personnel and light equipment can be transferred by air

[390] The storage measures also promote stability

[391] The transfer of allied air forces to Norway will be crucial to maintaining dominance in Norwegian airspace

[392] Within the framework of the COB program, an agreement has been signed to store equipment for American air reinforcements at eight Norwegian airports

[393] The storage program is well underway

[394] The COB program does not mean that the aircraft squadrons are exclusively earmarked for operations in Norway

[395] However, the large number of reinforcement options means that an attacker will face a highly uncertain situation

[396] This in itself will have a war-preventing effect

[397] In 1981, an agreement was signed between Norway and the United States regarding the advance storage of equipment for a US naval expeditionary brigade

[398] The storage takes place within the framework of NATO's collective defense

[399] A British-Dutch amphibious force has Norway as its first deployment option after command of the force was transferred from SACLANT to SACEUR

[400] This involves only a small amount of advance storage, but the force exercises regularly in Norway and can be transferred at short notice

[401] The work to find a suitable replacement for the Canadian brigade that was earmarked for operations in Northern Norway is expected to lead to clarification during

[402] Canada is participating with a battalion group in NATO's mobile force, which can be deployed on the Northern Flank in Europe in a crisis situation

[403] Materiel for a Canadian battalion is stored in northern Norway

[404] The strength and equipment will not be affected by Canada ceasing its other obligations to earmark forces for operations in Norway

[405] Since the 1950s, materials, ammunition, fuel and equipment for Allied air and naval forces have been pre-stored in southern Norway

[406] The West German Navy has depots along the southern Norwegian coast, among other things

[407] Norway actively participates in the coordinated allied surveillance operations over the northern sea areas

[408] This provides Norwegian authorities with overview and warning as well as significant operational and technical insight

[409] The development of military technology has major consequences both for the security challenge we face and for the development of our own defense

[410] The cost trend for advanced defense equipment is disturbingly high

[411] Small countries are particularly affected by this development

[412] It will be an important task to select and utilize those parts of the technological development potential that provide the greatest defense capability for our forces as a whole and within the resource framework that is determined

[413] All parts of society are obligated to take part in the defense of Norway

[414] This requires close cooperation between civilian and military authorities through a total defense concept

[415] In the event of war, the Armed Forces can requisition supplies, transport support, materiel, maintenance services, buildings and facilities from civilian society

[416] Cooperation arrangements at local, regional and central levels will be maintained and further developed, primarily through daily cooperation and through exercises of both an allied and national nature

[417] Particular emphasis will be placed on practicing crisis management skills, the emergency preparedness system and the emergency preparedness cadres established for war within all levels of total defense

[418] The government's renewal program, productivity growth and rationalization will be very important in the work of implementing the main guidelines, including through a shift to more pronounced financial management and results orientation through the annual budgets

[419] Particular emphasis will be placed on greater local discretion and freedom of action

[420] An action plan for this has been prepared

[421] Furthermore, work is being done on simplifying regulations as an important part of the efficiency improvement efforts

[422] Business plans will be prepared for all units by 1990, and in conjunction with these, efficiency improvement plans with specific savings targets for each year will be drawn up

[423] The rationalization effort will be strengthened so that it makes a significant contribution to creating a necessary renewal process

[424] There will be great demands placed on long-term planning in the Armed Forces

[425] With the aim of achieving an optimal structural composition, both quantitatively and qualitatively, a number of defense sector-specific analyses have been initiated

[426] A more comprehensive analysis of the overall defense structure will be carried out

[427] It must be assumed that this work may lead to changes in the structural composition outlined in this report

[428] The planning methodology will be further developed

[429] It is desirable to loosen the constraints in the budget to increase flexibility in the use of resources

[430] This will improve the freedom of action and the possibilities for managing the Armed Forces' activities

[431] In future planning, emphasis will also be placed on highlighting alternative development lines under different framework conditions with the aim of achieving the highest possible defense capability in the short and long term

[432] Uncertainty about economic developments, and the possibility of changes in the security policy framework as a result of negotiations on arms control and disarmament, also indicate that emphasis is placed on alternative planning

[433] The implementation of the Main Guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities in the period 1984-88 INTRODUCTION

[434] This section provides a brief account of the implementation and status of the main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities in the period 1984-88, which were submitted to the Storting with St meld no

[435] The presentation includes the development of appropriations, organization, personnel, education and exercises, materiel and supplies, and buildings and structures

[436] More detailed information about each of these areas is provided in Annexes 2a-d to this report

[437] St report no. 74 for 1982-83 addressed the lack of balance that existed between the Armed Forces' activities and the resources that were made available

[438] This would be corrected through rationalization measures, reprioritization and reductions

[439] Reductions could be necessary to create a better balance between operations and investments

[440] Through the Storting's consideration of St. prp. no. 1 for the following years, some such reductions have been adopted and implemented

[441] The Chief of Defence has stated in the 1985 Defence Study that some of the goals and assumptions in Parliamentary Report No. 74 were difficult to reconcile, neither in general nor within the given resource framework

[442] When it comes to rationalization measures, the study points out that developments in recent years have dampened hopes of significant operational reductions due to increased demands on operating assets, primarily as a result of our general social development

[443] The Chief of Defence also states, as his view, that it is very difficult to gain traction with the decision-making authorities for significant savings through restructuring and removal of activities that do not produce combat capability

[444] It is now clear that significant interim goals in Parliamentary Report No. 74 cannot be implemented during the period

[445] This applies, for example, to the Army, where the goal was, among other things, three brigades of 90 standard by 1988, and for the Navy, the construction of prototypes for new mine clearance vessels and the start of modification of Storm-class MTBs

[446] Fewer flight hours and sailing days have also been produced than expected

[447] The reasons have included a shortage of pilots and technicians and the fact that more vessels than normal have had to be laid up due to a tight operating budget throughout the period

[448] In other areas, development has been closer to the target

[449] Prioritized brigades in the Army have been provided with modern air defense, mobility has been improved for several departments, and the anti-tank sector and ammunition situation have been improved

[450] In the Navy, three modern coastal forts are under completion, six new UVBs are being built and six old ones are being modernized

[451] In addition, the escort vessels are being updated

[452] The Air Force has acquired modern air defense for six important airports, the new fighter structure has been established with F-16 and F-5 aircraft, new transport helicopters have been acquired and are being introduced, and silo radars have been put into service or are under construction

[453] In two areas of the Armed Forces' activities, developments have not gone as planned, and new problems have arisen

[454] This applies to the personnel sector, where the departure of special categories of personnel has been particularly high, and it concerns the implementation of rationalization measures that have not yielded the intended savings

[455] In Part IV, the Ministry returns to these problems, and measures that can improve and streamline efforts are discussed

[456] The defense's involvement in environmental and resource issues is also briefly discussed, and an international comparison of defense spending has been prepared

[457] Preparations for the reception of allied reinforcements are an important part of the Armed Forces' tasks

[458] The construction of warehouses for a US naval expeditionary brigade and the advance storage of equipment for aircraft in connection with the COB agreement are significant improvements in this area

[459] Canada's decision to cancel the earmarking of two air squadrons and a brigade for deployment in Norway must be considered a deterioration of the overall defense capability in the Northern region

[460] NATO is now working to find a replacement for the Canadian forces

[461] During the planning period, propositions and reports have been submitted to the Storting on a number of major issues, including some issues that were not mentioned in the Storting report

[462] The annual budget proposals and proposals on NATO's infrastructure program have been the most important parliamentary documents in the planning context

[463] Appendix 3 provides an overview of all propositions and reports that the Ministry of Defence has submitted to the Storting from 1983-84 and later

[464] BUDGET DEVELOPMENT Parliamentary report no. 74 for 1982-83 projected annual real budget growth of 3.5 percent during the period

[465] Subsequent calculations show that real growth for the years 1984-1987 will be approximately 3.3 percent on average per year

[466] During the period, great emphasis has been placed on increasing investments and limiting operational growth

[467] As a guideline, St meld 74 proposed a material investment share of 25 percent of the budget in 1988, excluding the Coast Guard, while operating expenses were assumed not to increase in real terms by more than one percent annually

[468] The subsequent calculations for 1984, 1985, 1986, 1987 and estimates for 1988 show that operating expenses will have an average real growth of just over 1.5 percent during the period

[469] The fact that the increase has been somewhat larger than expected is primarily due to difficulties in limiting growth in non-wage operations

[470] A significant reason for this is the introduction of new equipment that is expensive to maintain

[471] At the same time, it has proven difficult to close down, or reduce, existing operations

[472] The salary budget showed a relatively strong reduction in the first years of the period, due to, among other things, a greater than expected causal departure of officers

[473] But the departure of certain categories of civilian personnel that it would have been desirable to retain also contributed to reducing salary costs

[474] Increased use of temporary personnel, and efforts to improve the personnel situation, have led to an increase in wage costs at the end of the period

[475] During the period, investments in equipment have had an average real growth of approximately six percent

[476] The objective of a 25 percent material investment share of the budget in 1988, excluding the Coast Guard, will most likely be met

[477] In addition, through the infrastructure program, there have been material investments of approximately 1.5 percent of the budget

[478] Construction and civil engineering investments have increased significantly for both the national and jointly financed parts

[479] The increase in volume for the nationally financed projects is primarily a consequence of increased material investments, of which Norwegian Adapted Hawk (NOAH) air defense missiles, turret guns for the Coastal Artillery, Brig 90 and ULA class submarines are the largest

[480] The increase in the jointly financed program is particularly related to work in connection with allied reinforcements for efforts in Norway in times of crisis and war

[481] Organization For the Army, the period 1984-1988 has been characterized by organizational restructuring that has resulted in fewer and larger units with a consequent redistribution of personnel

[482] Regional supply commands have been established at each DK/DIV

[483] The structure of the naval districts has not changed during the period, but measures to save personnel are being considered

[484] A one-year command school for the Navy (BSMA) was established

[485] Due to new and better equipment, including new transmission systems, two of the Air Force's radar stations have been closed and given mobilization status

[486] At six of the air stations, NOAH air defense batteries are now being set up

[487] In accordance with the conclusion in Recommendation S No. 250 for 1983-84, the division of work and responsibility between the administrations, the Ministry of Education and Culture and the Ministry of Education and Culture remains unchanged

[488] However, these questions are under investigation

[489] The peacekeeping headquarters of the Defence Command Southern Norway (FKS) was moved from Oslo to Stavanger in the spring of 1987 as planned

[490] The conscription service is expected to be reorganized and the name has been temporarily changed to the Norwegian Conscription Agency (NVA

[492] In order to achieve more efficient and rational operations, the Norwegian Armed Forces Data Center (FDS) and the Norwegian Armed Forces Joint Communications (FFSB) have been merged to form the Norwegian Armed Forces Telecommunications and Data Service (FTD

[494] The departure of personnel at the end of the period was greater than expected

[614] DEFENCE COMMITMENT

[615] As part of the follow-up to the report from the World Commission on Environment and Development, work has been initiated to clarify in which areas the Armed Forces can contribute to the follow-up to the report

[616] Among other things, the need for training and information on environmental and resource issues, energy efficiency measures, measures against environmental pollutants, the relationship to reindeer herding and outdoor resources in areas where the armed forces conduct exercises, etc. will be examined in more detail

[617] In support of the World Commission on Environment and Development, the Ministry of Defence organized an international expert conference on the topic of SECURITY AND THE ENVIRONMENT in

[618] The report from the conference was printed and published in the autumn

[619] During the conference, it was pointed out that the concept of national security has changed its content

[620] Nations can no longer achieve security at the expense of each other

[621] They must work together to face common dangers and seek security together

[622] Environmental degradation undermines national and international security and is detrimental to all states

[623] The limitations of nation states as decision-making bodies have become clear, even as nations are eager to protect and assert their own sovereignty

[624] The environmental challenge goes beyond the borders of the nation-state and cannot be handled by institutions with a narrow national mandate

[625] The Ministry will, as a follow-up to the World Commission on Environment and Development's report, continue to work on these issues in the planning period 1989-93. **7. [644] THE CONSEQUENCES OF THE DEVELOPMENT FOR THE DEFENCE CAPABILITY** From the previous sections it is clear that the budget development during the period has been close to the target of 3.5 percent real budget growth per year and the material investment share in 1988 also appears to have reached the target of 25 percent

[645] Considerable efforts have been made to limit annual increases in operating expenses to one percent, but the increase has been just over 1.5 percent

[646] On the personnel side, the Armed Forces have problems retaining certain categories of officers and technically well-qualified personnel in competition with the private sector

[647] There are also recruitment problems for technically well-qualified personnel

[648] During this period, the defense has received a lot of new material and equipment

[649] Education and training have been extensive

[650] In sum, this has led to increased combat capability

[651] In some areas, however, tight operating budgets and other capacity problems have led to lower levels of preparedness and training for some defense elements

[652] The strengthening of combat capability has therefore not reached the full extent recommended by the commission

[653] The Defense Commission wanted a defense that, in cooperation with our allies, had such a defense capability that an attack on all or part of the country would entail unacceptable risk to the attacker

[654] In Northern Norway, the main goal was to build up a defense with sufficient strength to hold out long enough for reinforcements to be brought in from other parts of the country and from outside

[655] For Southern Norway, the commission believed that we needed to be able to prevent attacks to a greater extent by maintaining a defense based essentially on mobilization forces

[656] The Commission's recommendation regarding the defense structure in Northern Norway has been quantitatively achieved, although the pace of force modernization is somewhat lower than expected

[657] Combat capability has increased during the period

[658] The defense in Southern Norway has also been strengthened in some sectors, but in general it has not succeeded in achieving the commission's recommendation

[659] On the other hand, planning and arrangements for Allied reinforcements have taken on a significantly greater scope than the commission anticipated

[660] This applies particularly to air combat forces (COB agreements), but also to land combat forces (MEB

[661] The measures taken in this field significantly strengthen the Norwegian Armed Forces' deterrence capability

[662] Overall, the combat capability of the national forces in Southern Norway has increased during the period, but somewhat less than anticipated by the Defence Commission

[663] The region is no longer considered to be as vulnerable to a major attack, especially in an early phase of a conflict

[664] In the context of the alliance, the defence capability is therefore considered to have been maintained during the period. **IV Main guidelines for the activities of the Armed Forces in the period

[665] This section presents proposals for main guidelines that will apply to the activities of the Armed Forces during the period

[666] This five-year period is the last of three covered by the Defence Commission's proposal for a 15-year perspective plan

[667] The basic goals of Norwegian security policy will be described

[668] Likewise, NATO's goals and strategy, and Norway's self-imposed commitments on defense measures within the framework of alliance membership

[669] Furthermore, the détente tendencies in East/West relations and the relationship between the superpowers will be discussed

[670] Developments in Western European cooperation and the relationship between the United States and Western Europe in terms of defense and security policy will be discussed

[671] A description will be given of the military situation between NATO and the Warsaw Pact, and of developments and issues in the area of ​​arms control and disarmament

[672] Norway's strategic position will be specifically discussed

[673] An assessment of military technical developments and a description of the total defense concept will be provided

[674] The structural objectives for the period 1989-93 will be described on the basis of the main tasks assigned to the armed forces, defense related assessments and trade-offs, allied cooperation, and framework conditions for finances and personnel

[675] The main guidelines are designed by Defense Branch for the areas of personnel, organization, education, exercises, and for materiel and buildings and facilities

[676] The section also contains guidelines for implementing the Government's renewal program in the Armed Forces, productivity growth and rationalization, and how the Armed Forces, in addition to its primary tasks, contribute to supporting civil society

[677] Finally, an overview will be given of the overall defence planning and how the measures in the main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities in the period 1989-93 are intended to be organised and implemented. **1.1 The specialist military recommendations** The report to the Storting has been prepared in close collaboration with the specialist military authorities

[678] In Appendix 1, the Chief of Defence has given his principled view of the Armed Forces' needs and development in the years ahead

[679] The statement is based on the Defense Study

[680] This was prepared by the Norwegian Armed Forces High Command, and has been the basis for the High Command's internal long-term planning

[681] The defense study, which follows the report, has not been approved by the political authorities

[682] It concludes that an average annual real growth rate of six to seven percent over a 15-year period is needed to maintain a balanced and strong national defense

[683] It also describes adjustments that must be made to the defense structure if budget growth remains at the same level as in recent years, i.e. approximately three percent in real terms annually

[684] The government has placed great emphasis on the professional military perspective in the overall political considerations that have been made

[725] Security policy goals The fundamental goals for Norwegian security policy are (cf. St meld no. 74 (1982-83) and Innsst S no

[726] to prevent war in our region - to secure our sovereignty and freedom of action as well as our right to shape our own society - to contribute to peaceful development in the rest of the world

[727] In a world of sovereign states and without an accepted superior authority that can ensure that states refrain from the use of violence and other forms of abuse, states must take measures themselves to protect themselves

[728] This must, as far as possible, happen in such a way that it does not create mutual fear and uncertainty

[729] The armaments can lead to uncertainty that reinforces and consolidates political contradictions

[730] On the other hand, military weakness can also lead to insecurity

[731] Nations are woven together in a comprehensive relationship of interdependence

[732] Therefore, security policy must include a balance between security and reassurance considerations

[733] In the age of nuclear weapons, no nation can achieve security at the expense of other nations

[734] They must therefore instead seek security together

[735] Yet international politics is largely characterized by unilateral measures and a lack of mutual restraint

[736] It has also proven difficult to translate the notion of shared security into agreed and coordinated measures

[737] The agreement to eliminate all intermediate-range missiles (INF Treaty) and progress in negotiations on a comprehensive reduction of strategic nuclear forces now give reason for optimism

[738] Only negotiations, mutual restraint and confidence-building measures can create real and lasting security

[739] Norway is located in an important and sensitive military strategic area

[740] Such a position also entails responsibility for viewing national security policy in an international perspective

[741] A fixed course helps prevent thrust and pressure

[742] By combining the ability and will to defend and by doing its part to promote mutual restraint, Norway contributes important prerequisites for continued low tension

[743] The main task of the Armed Forces is to act as a deterrent to war in peacetime, and to defend national independence with military means if Norway were to be attacked

[744] However, security policy encompasses more than purely military measures

[745] The defense measures are part of a broad register of security policy instruments that collectively aim to provide the country with the greatest possible security

[746] Norway actively participates in international efforts for arms control, disarmament and conflict resolution by peaceful means

[747] Behind this international commitment lies the recognition that nations' different security interests interfere with each other

[748] Cross-border cooperation and mutual restraint in the use of military force are required

[749] In accordance with this view, the implementation of Norwegian security policy is based on both reassuring and deterrent considerations

[750] Consistent implementation of a policy based on both of these elements helps to give credibility to Norway's intentions

[751] Our desire for peaceful cooperation between nations is signaled at the same time as our willingness to defend the country with the means at our disposal, should it become necessary

[752] Norwegian authorities have limited opportunities to control developments in our local areas

[753] It is therefore necessary to pursue a security policy that is adapted to the reality that we face at all times

[754] The geographical area of which Norway is a part now has, through political, military and technological development, a far greater strategic importance than a few decades ago

[755] This makes it necessary to take a position on political and military strategic issues that extend far beyond securing the country's borders alone

[756] In order for there to be no doubt about Norway's security policy goals, there must be consistency and continuity in our relationship with these external framework conditions

[757] Allied defense cooperation is a cornerstone of Norwegian security policy

[758] This gives Norway a level of security that our resources alone cannot provide

[759] Through its goals and its defense structure, NATO helps to secure the foundation for peaceful development, despite ideological and power-political contradictions between East and West

[760] Norway's security interests in the international community will, for the foreseeable future, be best served through Norwegian membership in NATO

[761] As part of a comprehensive Norwegian security policy, Norway has practiced certain self-imposed commitments of a reassuring nature

[762] They aim to convince surrounding nations of Norway's peaceful intentions and the defensive goals of alliance membership

[763] The most important commitments concern the nonstationing of foreign military forces on Norwegian soil in peacetime (the base policy), and the non-stationing or storage of nuclear weapons and chemical weapons as well as refraining from preparing for the use of such weapons (the nuclear weapons policy, the chemical weapons policy

[764] Within the framework of alliance cooperation, Norway actively supports measures that can contribute to increased mutual trust and security policy stability between East and West, at the lowest possible force level

[765] The UN is a cornerstone of Norwegian foreign policy

[766] In the UN's work for peace and security, peacekeeping operations are an important conflict-reducing instrument, and one of the UN's most successful initiatives

[767] In recent years, and in most international conflicts, there has been a clearer recognition of the necessity of negotiating solutions

[768] The need for UN observers and forces is therefore increasing

[769] One of the tasks of the Norwegian Armed Forces is to provide contingents for UN peacekeeping operations

[770] With this, Norway can make a major contribution to maintaining international peace and security

[771] This effort therefore also has significant national security policy value. NATO is a defense alliance between sovereign and equal states whose purpose is to ensure the security of its member states in freedom

[772] The Alliance's primary task is to prevent war and ensure a lasting and stable peace

[773] NATO advances its goal, among other things, by maintaining adequate military preparedness

[774] The fundamental principle of NATO defense is the collective guarantee of the security of its members

[775] An attack against one or more member states is considered an attack against them all

[776] Participation in the Allied joint defense contributes to preventing an isolated attack on Norwegian territory

[777] A potential attacker will have to take into account the allied defense potential and the allied reactions

[778] The Norwegian Armed Forces' ability to ward off attacks is strengthened by making concrete preparations in peacetime for the reception of allied reinforcements at short notice

[779] In parallel with maintaining an effective and credible defense, the Alliance aims to work for real improvements in international relations and promote détente between East and West

[780] These two pillars of the Alliance's overall policy for peace and security were established in the Harmel Report from 1967, which still forms the basis of NATO's policy towards the Warsaw Pact countries today

[781] In the Declaration from the Brussels Heads of Government Meeting in March 1988, NATO countries stated that none of the Alliance's weapons will ever be used except in response to attack

[782] They have further made it clear that the Alliance respects the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of other states, and have appealed to the Soviet Union to similarly respect the legitimate security interests of Western countries

[783] In NATO bodies, all decisions are made by consensus after prior political consultations

[784] In addition to discussions on purely military issues, regular political consultations also take place

[785] Central to these consultations are the biannual meetings at ministerial level

[786] The North Atlantic Council, the Defence Planning Committee (DPC) and the Nuclear Planning Group (NPG) meet at Permanent Representatives level between ministerial meetings

[787] In addition, a number of committees under the Council and the DPC continuously address issues of common interest

[788] NATO also serves as a forum for expert-level consultations on issues ranging from disarmament and arms control to environmental protection and scientific activities

[789] Consultations within the Alliance are of particular importance when it comes to negotiations on arms control and disarmament

[790] In multilateral negotiation forums, alliance partners coordinate their views in order to develop the best possible basis for safeguarding the interests of all member states

[791] In bilateral negotiations between the Soviet Union and the United States, consultations within NATO give the other allies the opportunity to influence the negotiation processes

[792] From the Norwegian side, political consultations are highly valued both because they provide an opportunity to promote one's own interests and views, and because the consultations provide insight and access to information of significant importance for the formulation of Norwegian defense and security policy

[793] NATO's strategy In 1967, NATO's strategy was changed from "massive nuclear retaliation" to "forward defense and flexible response

[794] The primary purpose of both the strategy itself and the design of the Alliance's military forces to support it is to deter any attack — both conventional and nuclear

[795] A potential attacker should not be able to pre-calculate the consequences of an attack

[796] The member states' will for unity, and their force structure, are in this context means of making it clear to a potential attacker that an attack against one or more alliance countries will be met with all appropriate means, and that such a situation could also result in the use of nuclear weapons with unpredictable consequences for all parties

[797] In other words, the most important function of nuclear weapons in the Alliance's strategy is to prevent war

[798] It's not about weapons that can win a war

[799] NATO countries have declared that the Alliance's weapons will never be used except in response to attack

[800] Credible deterrence requires a credible ability to meet any attack at the level and with the means necessary to stop the attack and repel it

[801] The flexible response strategy is based on a combination of defense at the level under attack with the ability to escalate the use of military force in a controlled manner

[802] This means that the first use of nuclear weapons by the Alliance is not ruled out as a possible option

[803] But the current strategy does not prescribe the first use of nuclear weapons either

[804] In Norway's view, it is important that NATO reduces its dependence on nuclear weapons, especially the early use of such weapons

[805] Reliance on early use may increase pressure for preemptive attacks and thereby increase the risk of unintentional escalation

[806] It can be paralyzing in a crisis situation

[807] Norway will therefore, in accordance with what is stated in the

[808] Norway will therefore, in accordance with what is stated in the actively contribute to the Alliance being able to work away from a strategy that includes the possible first use of nuclear weapons, in parallel with greater emphasis being placed on conventional defense

[809] A possible mutual reduction of conventional forces to approximately the same level would reduce the possibility of a conventional attack, and thereby reduce dependence on nuclear weapons

[810] If deterrence fails, it follows from NATO's strategy that defense must be designed in such a way that the attacker is persuaded to abort the attack and withdraw his forces

[811] The Alliance has therefore designed a balanced “triad” of defense assets — conventional forces, tactical nuclear forces, and strategic nuclear forces — that complement each other and must be seen in context

[812] At the same time, each individual element must constitute a credible means of defense

[813] The alliance will preferably meet a conventional attack with conventional defense

[814] In order to make conventional defense credible, and thereby reduce dependence on nuclear weapons, NATO countries place great emphasis on reducing the imbalance in the conventional balance of power in Europe

[815] This is sought to be achieved both through arms control agreements and by improving conventional defense

[816] Forward defense involves stationing Allied defense forces so far forward that both the eastern parts of the Alliance's territory and the flank areas can be defended if one or more NATO countries are attacked

[817] The principle reflects both geographical and political realities

[818] This applies, for example, to a significant part of the Federal Republic of Germany, where several densely populated industrial areas are located close to the central German border

[819] Although a defense in depth here could be militarily advantageous, a defense strategy that involves giving up parts of allied territory in advance would be politically unacceptable

[820] Even a conventional war with today's weapons could cause enormous destruction to the affected areas

[821] It is therefore not a sufficient deterrent to try to convince an adversary that a war fought on the territory of another country cannot be won

[822] A potential attacker must not be led to believe that his own territory will be a safe haven if he attacks any NATO member state. **2.2.3 The policy of appeasement** Norway has taken into account the situation and assessments of neighboring countries in its defense policy dispositions

[823] Such considerations have been taken to emphasize the defensive nature of Norway's alliance membership, and to contribute to the lowest possible level of tension in Northern Europe

[824] This has been expressed in a number of unilateral, self-imposed commitments in our defense measures within the framework of alliance membership

[825] Norway has consistently asserted the right to determine the content of the measures that are at any time considered appropriate to safeguard Norwegian security interests. The following prerequisites were laid down for membership in the Alliance during the Norwegian deliberations prior to the formation of NATO in

[826] The Norwegian Government will not enter into any agreement with other states that entails obligations for Norway to open bases for the combat forces of foreign powers on Norwegian territory as long as Norway is not attacked or exposed to threats of attack

[827] This condition applies to the permanent stationing of foreign powers' combat forces on Norwegian territory

[828] The principles of the base policy have later been further specified and made concrete, including in connection with allied exercises and training activities in Norway

[829] In summary, the base policy is practiced in such a way that it does not prevent (cf. St prp no. 1 (1977-78)): - that Norway opens bases for allied combat forces in the event of an armed attack on the North Atlantic area, or at a time when the Norwegian authorities feel exposed to threats of attack and request allied combat forces to come to the country - that Norway, in prescribed constitutional forms, enters into conditional agreements with our allies with such a situation in mind - that Norway expands its military facilities according to such a pattern that they will be able to immediately receive and effectively maintain allied combat forces that are transferred to Norway to assist with the defense of the country - that Norway participates in allied joint exercises, or receives short-term visits by allied air and naval combat forces already in peacetime - that allied combat forces stay in Norway for training for short periods of time, or as part of allied exercises that aim to prepare for any possible allied efforts in Norway in a situation where Norwegian authorities request allied combat forces to come to the country - that facilities for command, control and communication, warning, etc. are established on Norwegian territory for allied combat forces - that stores of ammunition and equipment, supplies, etc. are established in Norway for allied combat forces - that Norway participates in integrated military cooperation within the Atlantic Treaty organization, enters into agreements on the transfer in prescribed constitutional forms of command authority over Norwegian forces to allied command, establishes allied headquarters on Norwegian territory or participates in the work thereof, or transfers Norwegian air defense units to allied operational command already in peacetime

[830] An example of measures that thus fall within the framework of the base policy is Norway's participation in NATO's airborne warning and control force, NAEW&amp;C, which in Norway uses Ørland Air Station as a base for missions in the high north

[831] All functions at the station in connection with this activity are carried out by Norwegian personnel, and the missions are subject to the same restrictions as other allied air operations in Norway

[832] Another example is the advance storage of supplies for allied air forces at Norwegian airports (the COB agreements), and the stores for allied reinforcement forces that have been established in several places in the country

[833] The framework for Norwegian base policy remains in place, and the measures that developments require to strengthen Norway's defense will be considered within this framework. Norwegian nuclear weapons policy will continue to be conducted within the framework that has been previously outlined
