[1851] CONTRIBUTIONS TO UN PEACEKEEPING OPERATIONS 3.1 UN Security Council

[1852] When the UN Charter was written in the final months of World War II, the role of world organizations in maintaining international peace and security was a major theme

[1853] The Charter's Chapter 5 on the role of the Security Council, Chapter 6 on the peaceful settlement of disputes, and Chapter 7 on measures against threats to the peace, breaches of the peace, and acts of aggression, contain guidelines for a collective security system that was intended "to save succeeding generations from the scourge of war, which twice in our lifetime has brought untold sorrow to mankind

[1854] The security system defined by the UN Charter was built on the premise that the five permanent members of the Security Council could agree to establish the arrangements for the use of military force provided for in the Charter's chapter

[1855] This assumption proved to be untrue in the first post-war years

[1856] In particular, the contradictions between the United States and the Soviet Union have prevented the Security Council from functioning according to its original assumptions

[1857] The UN and the Security Council have therefore been unable to play any executive role when it comes to East-West relations

[1858] The great power conflicts have also limited the Security Council's ability to act when it comes to conflicts in the Third World related to East/West relations

[1859] The greatest weaknesses of the system of collective security at the global level that has been established through the UN lie in the fact that the system does not have sufficient war-preventing capabilities

[1860] This has been seen, among other things, in the many armed conflicts in the Third World in the years after the Second World War

[1861] A number of these have also been discussed in the Security Council, but the Council has only exceptionally agreed on sanctions against countries that have committed breaches of the peace, or threats thereof

[1862] Those countries that had to consider armed action, for example against neighboring countries, have therefore been able to do so in the knowledge that the members of the Security Council would not agree on truly effective sanctions measures in response

[1863] The Security Council, on the other hand, has proven to be a far more valuable body for international crisis management, both in preventing vertical and horizontal escalation

[1864] This has been demonstrated, among other things, through the Middle East conflicts of

[1865] The Security Council, which can meet at one hour's notice, is in such contexts a standing emergency body that makes it possible to convene both major powers, other UN members and conflict parties within a very short period of time

[1866] The work to strengthen the UN's apparatus for conflict resolution, crisis management and peaceful settlement of disputes has been a high priority area in Norwegian foreign policy since

[1867] With the instability and danger of new conflicts that exist in several areas of the Third World, this task will not become less important in the years to come

[1868] Given the danger of great power participation and the risk of the spread of such conflicts, this work will also have great security policy significance

[1869] In the reform work underway at the UN, we, from the Norwegian side, have strongly supported the measures that have been taken to strengthen the Secretary-General's apparatus for early warning of international situations that may develop into armed conflicts, and the bodies that are continuously engaged in the work of bringing the parties to the conflict to the negotiating table, possibly through direct mediation by the Secretary-General

[1870] UN peacekeeping operations Peacekeeping operations are divided into two groups, forces equipped with lighter weapons and observer corps where the personnel are unarmed

[1871] Peacekeeping operations will in some situations be a very important tool for the Security Council in its efforts to limit international conflicts

[1872] This is also the area where the Norwegian and Nordic sides have been able to contribute most concretely to the UN's work to maintain international peace and security

[1873] From the Norwegian side, participation in UN peacekeeping operations has therefore had a dual objective

[1874] On the one hand, this effort has been an expression of the desire to strengthen the UN and the global apparatus for crisis management and conflict resolution; on the other hand, it has been a Norwegian contribution to reducing tension in the areas where the forces have been deployed

[1875] The concept for UN peacekeeping forces is based on the arrangement found in 1956 when the first UN force at Suez was established (UNEF I

[1876] This concept is based on the premise that the parties involved in the conflict should request or consent to the deployment of a UN force, and that the force's main task should be to monitor and maintain a ceasefire that has already been established pending a lasting peace solution

[1877] It has also been a prerequisite that a UN force should only be equipped with weapons for self-defense, and that conflicts should be resolved through a firm stance and negotiations, and not through offensive operations

[1878] Experience with UN peacekeeping operations is largely good

[1879] There is international agreement that these forces are perhaps the UN's most important innovation in terms of its work to maintain international peace and security

[1880] Experience has been best when UN forces have been deployed on the basis of a binding agreement entered into with the parties to the conflict themselves, which, for example, predefine the deployment area and other issues that are of significant importance for the forces to be able to fulfill their task

[1881] An example of this is the United Nations Observer Force on the Golan Heights between Syria and Israel (UNDOF

[1882] All parties perceive this strength as useful and important

[1883] In cases where such prior agreements do not exist, or when the parties are unable to enter into or comply with such agreements, UN forces have had a far more difficult task

[1884] This has been the situation for the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), among other things

[1885] In international crisis situations, however, there will not always be time to negotiate detailed agreements with the parties to the conflict

[1886] In such situations, it may be necessary to deploy and maintain UN forces to prevent further escalation of the conflict

[1887] UN forces do not maintain peace by virtue of their armed force, but by virtue of the authority inherent in their representation of the UN

[1888] They cannot, and should not, impose an external will on the parties

[1889] They shall not be a party or take part in the conflict that made the deployment necessary

[1890] The authority they have is also a result of the forces' reputation for impartiality

[1891] The forces can only complete their mission if the parties want to

[1892] Their presence makes it easier for parties who prefer a ceasefire but cannot agree on one, to adhere to an actual ceasefire

[1893] UN forces help create the trust that the parties cannot create themselves

[1894] There is always a possibility that UN forces contribute to freezing and preserving conflicts rather than resolving them because the risk of escalation is reduced

[1895] Therefore, it is important that peacekeeping operations also include deliberate attempts at mediation, negotiation and dispute resolution

[1896] Often, conflicts are so complicated that the parties lose control and are therefore unable to resolve them in an active manner

[1897] The UN forces then easily slip into the role of replacement authority

[1898] Local people look to them for protection and assistance

[1899] Therefore, one must always be prepared that a UN operation may be prolonged

[1900] Those countries that enter this with forces must be prepared to bear long-term responsibility

[1901] Threats of withdrawal may weaken the UN rather than exert pressure on conflict parties that lack the ability to comply with requests to assume control and who can easily respond to threats to remove UN forces by improving their positions

[1902] In addition to peacekeeping forces, the UN observer system has proven to be a valuable instrument in international conflicts

[1903] The main task of UN observers is to observe the actual situation in the area of ​​operation and to report on developments to the Secretary-General

[1904] UN observers have proven to be a very flexible, and relatively inexpensive, instrument that can be deployed at very short notice when the Security Council or the Secretary-General so decides

[1905] In this context, the UN Mission in the Middle East (UNTSO) has functioned as a standby force that can quickly deploy observers to other conflict areas

[1906] Many of the institutional problems associated with command relationships in UN forces have now been resolved

[1907] It has been established that the forces are under the command of the Secretary-General and not the Security Council, while the mandate and political issues related to the forces must be approved by the Security Council

[1908] The biggest outstanding problem in connection with the UN forces remains the financing arrangement

[1909] It is a major problem that large and important contributors are not paying the contributions to the UN forces' budget that they are obligated to make according to the UN Charter

[1910] The work of arriving at financing arrangements that can provide troop-contributing countries with better coverage for their expenses will be important in the years to come

[1911] However, it is clear that high-cost countries such as Norway can in any case expect to have only part of the total costs of UN participation covered through such schemes

[1954] The importance of UN involvement for the Armed Forces

[1955] Participation in UN peacekeeping operations is part of the Armed Forces' tasks and an important part of Norwegian security policy

[1956] The participation is an expression of the importance Norway attaches to the UN as an organization and the UN's role in the work to maintain international peace and security

[1957] This is a very special type of military operation

[1958] Our efforts in peacekeeping operations cannot therefore be assessed by the same standard that we use for our defense efforts in Norway

[1959] It is a national task that should not be weighed against or compared with the Armed Forces' ordinary activities in Norway

[1960] It comes as an add-on

[1961] However, participation in peacekeeping operations also has important bonus effects for Norway's defense capabilities

[1962] Peacekeeping operations reduce the risk of local conflicts spreading and becoming a threat to peace in our part of the world

[1963] Typical examples of this are the conflicts in the Middle East

[1964] If such conflicts are not limited, they can quickly and uncontrolledly lead to dangerous crises with direct effects also for Norway

[1965] This danger is especially present in strategically important areas such as those of which Norway is a part

[1966] In this sense, peacekeeping operations have a mitigating effect with security policy and war prevention significance for our country as well

[1967] Peacekeeping forces most often establish a buffer zone between warring parties

[1968] The force will therefore have an area of operations at the intersection between the parties

[1969] The environment is characterized by the political conflict, but also by military measures from the parties

[1970] A peacekeeping force operates in an environment that is more complex and realistic than what we can simulate during initial service and refresher exercises in Norway

[1971] This means that the personnel are faced with different military challenges and tests than during peacetime in Norway

[1972] This applies not only to technical disciplines, but also leadership at the team, platoon, company and battalion levels

[1973] Even though a peacekeeping force is deployed by agreement between and with the parties, great demands are placed on the UN force

[1974] Personnel must be able to use weapons for self-defense

[1975] Under certain circumstances, the force must be prepared to use limited armed force to accomplish its mission

[1976] This places high demands on individual military skills and on leadership at all levels

[1977] Feedback from UNIFIL shows that almost all participants believe that the service has great, sometimes very great, value for their own tasks in the Armed Forces

[1978] The personnel have been in an environment that is as close as one can get to the "demands of war" in peacetime

[1979] They have therefore gained an experience that we are unable to provide in other ways

[1980] The UN service therefore also contributes to sharpening the "pointy end" of the Armed Forces

[1981] It cannot, of course, replace training in larger units for the defense of Norway, and far from all military disciplines that are of importance to Norway are used during UN service

[1982] Through our involvement in UNIFIL, personnel gain valuable experience that will not least benefit the mobilization defense

[1983] Just as the personnel from the German Brigade provided the Armed Forces with a strong backbone in the years after the war, service in UNIFIL could have a similar effect for decades

[1984] After 1988, nearly 20,000 will have served in UNIFIL

[1985] This is a resource that we must ensure we use in the best possible way

[1986] Individual experiences will be captured by the Armed Forces as an institution, and reflected in the education and training directives

[1987] In order to systematize relevant experience, particularly with regard to leadership, the Inspector General of the Army will conduct a survey among all contingents that have served in UNIFIL

[1988] The UNIFIL commitment gives us the opportunity in certain fields for systematic study and testing activities in a more realistic environment than in Norway

[1989] This applies not only to improving old equipment, but also to developing and testing new ones

[1990] Similarly, technical skills and tactical procedures can also be tested and adjusted

[1991] The Norwegian units in UNIFIL have performed their duty in a manner that has earned respect in the area of operations

[1992] This suggests that the education in the Armed Forces is good, and provides a good basis for continuing the experiences that the individual service member and the Armed Forces as an institution gain in UNIFIL

[1993] UNIFIL participation does not only provide purely military experience

[1994] The UN service strengthens understanding of the Armed Forces, and it helps us to see our own defense in a broader international and peace-building context

[1995] The individual has experienced firsthand what values the Armed Forces are supposed to protect, and therefore gains a greater understanding of the importance of the Armed Forces

[1996] UN service is not only important for the individual participant

[1997] The service also has ripple effects

[1998] As UN service is voluntary, it results in a significant number of conscripts in the mobilization defense gaining military experience and further education that it would not be possible to give them through refresher exercises in Norway

[1999] MILITARY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENT

[2000] Over the past 15-20 years, military technical development has generally been very strong, but the pace of development has differed within the various areas

[2001] The development spans a wide spectrum of fundamental disciplines and translates into new and improved military equipment of a number of different categories

[2002] When it comes to more fundamental technical research, it is not possible to distinguish between a military and a civilian focus

[2003] However, it is clear that the need to produce more functional and effective military equipment is still a strong driving force in the technological development process in both the East and the West

[2004] There is still a significant difference in the level of knowledge and pace of development between NATO and Warsaw Pact countries

[2005] In general, the Western world still has a clear lead

[2006] This applies especially to the important areas of microelectronics and computer technology

[2007] In other fields, such as laser and particle beam weapons and materials technology, there is probably not a clear Western lead

[2008] The Soviet system has proven to have built-in significant limitations when it comes to translating basic technological knowledge into good products through an efficient and flexible industry

[2009] The most dominant feature in the technology landscape over the last 10-20 years has been the development of highly computationally powerful and compact computers

[2010] This has made it practically possible to build a large data capacity even into military equipment with very limited dimensions, which has provided the basis for a radical improvement in sensor systems, fire control equipment, communications and weapons, both in terms of efficiency and scope

[2011] In some contexts, developments have enabled the realization of new system concepts with fundamentally new properties

[2012] By combining better sensors with the use of new computer technology, a new generation of systems for surveillance, combat management and weapons control with significantly improved performance is being developed

[2013] Examples of products in this area include satellite-borne radars with very good resolution for all-weather area surveillance and autonomous, precision-guided weapons

[2014] The technological basis for developing such advanced systems also entails a greater range of possibilities for electronic countermeasures against surveillance and warning systems, communications systems and weapons

[2015] However, by consciously using the opportunities offered by technological development, it is possible to create systems with good resistance to such countermeasures

[2016] This competition between developing better systems and more effective countermeasures is a feature of the picture that is gaining increasing importance

[2017] There is a strong development of new and improved materials

[2018] This provides opportunities for aircraft and missiles with less weight and better performance, and for significantly increased protection of combat vehicles

[2019] Another important line of development is expected to lead to construction materials and construction principles that will significantly complicate radar detection of aircraft and missiles

[2020] In the field of ammunition, there is a development towards explosives that are significantly less sensitive to heat and mechanical stress

[2021] As such explosives are introduced into new weapons systems and ammunition stockpiles are modernized, the risk of catastrophic explosions in peacetime as well as in war will be greatly reduced

[2022] Laser technology is a relatively new area where strong development with a long-term perspective is underway

[2023] Portable, low-power laser weapons that can damage lenses, sensors, and eyes are already available

[2024] Work is underway to develop more powerful laser weapons for air defense systems

[2025] A number of practical problems still need to be solved, for example in connection with field power supply, before such weapons can be put into operational use

[2026] It is not known that new categories of chemical warfare agents are under development

[2027] The most important innovation consists of producing nerve gas in the form of two components that are individually harmless

[2028] This makes transport and handling significantly less risky

[2029] Suitable warning and protective equipment against chemical warfare agents has gradually become available

[2030] In this field, the biggest problems are related to prioritizing within narrow resource limits, and to finding operationally appropriate methods of use

[2031] Seen in a long-term perspective, military technical developments have very significant consequences for our security

[2032] The introduction of new and better weapons and support systems into Warsaw Pact forces could, within 15-20 years, significantly change the threat facing NATO and Norway

[2033] In the same time perspective, the military-technical development in the West gives us opportunities to meet this development and maintain the deterrent capability of the alliance's defence

[2034] It is not possible to credibly say anything in general about how technological developments will affect our defense capabilities, as financial and other resource constraints will also weigh heavily

[2035] The new technological possibilities that can be expected to become available will be able to be translated into new types of military equipment in significantly different ways, and to different extents in the East and the West

[2036] There is great uncertainty in this area

[2037] Even with a given assumption of the availability of new defense equipment on both sides, the specific consequences for our defense will depend strongly on how an armed conflict will unfold

[2038] Here too, there is a broad spectrum of possibilities and fundamental uncertainties

[2039] It is nevertheless possible to point to some main features of the development that can provide certain clues for an overall assessment of the possible consequences of how a possible future conventional war will unfold

[2040] As better surveillance and warning systems are put into use, it will become more difficult to conceal force movements and other necessary preparations for a war

[2041] Provided that such signals are interpreted correctly, this development will further reduce the risk of a surprise attack

[2042] Satellite-based radar systems for ocean surveillance will, in 15-20 years' time, mean that the parties in a possible major conflict will have a very good overview of each other's maritime surface forces and convoys

[2043] This will reduce the possibilities for strategic and tactical surprise over the sea and make surface operations more vulnerable

[2044] A similar development applies to a lesser extent to underwater monitoring

[2045] The importance of the role of submarines in a future conflict will therefore increase relatively

[2046] More effective weapons, and the ability to operate in darkness and poor visibility, provide the basis for a far greater intensity and dynamism in a possible future war

[2047] This does not necessarily mean that an armed conflict will be shorter

[2048] The duration of, and the time between, the intense periods of combat will be strongly dependent on the ability to support and lead such demanding combat operations

[2049] The course and outcome of conflicts will increasingly depend on the parties' ability to exploit the potential inherent in better weapons and equipment

[2050] In this context, the ability to resist the counterparty's electronic countermeasures, and to exploit corresponding opportunities yourself, will become an increasingly important factor

[2051] Command and control in a future war will be a very demanding task

[2052] Computer-based support systems for these functions will significantly contribute to easing work pressure and facilitating the basis for combat management at various levels

[2053] The demands for knowledge, experience and judgment in combat leadership will increase

[2054] The bulk of the consequences of military technical development are expressed in the form of significant, but not dramatic, equipment improvements in a wide range of fields, as resources allow the introduction of this equipment

[2055] The time constants in this process are long, and the development of new technology must most often be carried out based on uncertain assumptions about how the counterparty bets

[2056] This means that the contribution of technological development to the conventional balance of power can fluctuate somewhat, but in general it follows a fairly stable trend

[2057] Rarely does a breakthrough occur that changes the picture in a more fundamental way

[2058] This entails a major research and development effort to counteract the consequences

[2059] Examples of such breakthroughs that have taken place are the laser and new types of armor that provide significantly better protection against shaped charge weapons

[2060] With a major focus on military technical development, the possibility of such breakthroughs will always be present

[2061] When they occur, they could have significant consequences for the balance of power for a certain period of time

[2062] Such technological breakthroughs can very rarely be predicted with certainty

[2063] New technology provides us with the basis for developing more effective defense systems

[2064] However, the cost development for advanced defense equipment over the past 15-20 years has been disturbingly high in relation to the increase in NATO countries' defense budgets

[2065] Small nations in particular are already strongly affected by this development

[2066] From the perspective of Norwegian defense planning, it is therefore a very central objective to identify and utilize those elements in technological development that will enable increased defense capability within narrow resource limits

[2067] Balancing the performance level of the equipment and the number of units that the resources realistically allow for becomes a key point in this context

[2068] The tasks, position, status and development of the Armed Forces are assessed within the framework of the total defence concept on which our entire defence philosophy is based

[2069] Total defense consists of military defense and civil preparedness

[2070] The Government has the supreme leadership of the Total Defence Force

[2071] The tasks of military defense are set out in chapter

[2072] The main tasks of civil preparedness are to prepare civil society to cope with a war situation so that - the transition from peace to war can take place quickly and effectively while maintaining an organized society - the military defense is ensured the necessary civilian support - the civilian elements of the total defense and the population have their most important needs met - life and health are protected - a transition to the highest possible degree of self-sufficiency can be implemented

[2073] In peacetime, civil preparedness also has the task of enabling the country to overcome crises, disasters and major accidents with the least possible damage and disruption to social life

[2074] Each ministry is responsible for emergency preparedness within its area of expertise, including emergency planning in peacetime, and the executive authority during crises and in war

[2075] The Directorate for Civil Emergency Preparedness (DSB) under the Ministry of Justice has the overall management of the Civil Defence, and is responsible for the central coordination of civil emergency preparedness work

[2076] Utilization of civilian resources

[2077] The total defense concept is based on the fundamental assumption that we must be able to face a conflict on Norwegian soil

[2078] With the country's exposed military-strategic location and the low population in relation to the country's size and extent, we must rely on a total defense for resource reasons

[2079] The total defense concept makes it possible for the Armed Forces to concentrate the use of resources for purely military purposes that cannot be covered in any other way, while at the same time avoiding waste from a socio-economic perspective through the costly duplication of equipment that already exists and can be used in a crisis situation

[2080] This is in accordance with the Defence Commission's recommendations

[2081] By systematically utilizing civilian resources, the Armed Forces are exempt from investments in materiel and other services that can be obtained from civilian sources

[2082] Defense funds can be used to purchase specific military equipment and supplies

[2083] The practical possibility of utilizing civilian resources is found particularly in areas such as food and supplies, sanitation, fuel, transportation, communications, technical equipment, construction, and specialized maintenance and repairs

[2084] However, the geographical distribution of civilian resources does not correspond to the distribution dictated by defense tasks

[2085] In particular, there is an uneven distribution of resources between Northern and Southern Norway

[2086] In Northern Norway, the Armed Forces' units must therefore be made self-sustaining until materiel and supplies can be supplied from the south

[2087] In recent years, significant structural changes have taken place within several areas of business

[2088] Improved communications and faster turnover rates have reduced inventories in retail, while also leading to more centralized warehousing and longer transport lines

[2089] Especially within the oil companies' storage and distribution patterns, there is a concentration on larger and centralized facilities

[2090] This development weakens parts of our defense preparedness

[2091] The storage of fuel under state control that took place in 1987 has improved this to some extent

[2092] Modern society is in several areas more vulnerable to harmful influences than before

[2093] When it comes to electricity supply, our power stations are largely well protected in the mountains

[2094] More vulnerable are water reservoirs, transformer stations and power grids, but it is assumed that production and distribution can mainly be kept running by sharing or bypassing the power supply

[2095] A prerequisite is that a high level of repair readiness is maintained

[2096] However, in some areas there may be a shortage of transformers

[2097] Modern society is also heavily dependent on large computer systems, both local facilities and geographically distributed networks

[2098] Preparedness to address the consequences of extensive functional impairment is poor

[2099] In many contexts, rationalization gains do not seem to be balanced against vulnerability considerations when new computer systems are planned

[2100] For private facilities, there are no licensing schemes or other instruments that can ensure that the necessary consideration is given to society's vulnerability

[2101] For publicly owned facilities, it should be assessed whether the current directives are satisfactory in light of developments in recent years

[2102] The use of computer technology in telecommunications networks is increasing

[2103] The network exchanges will be programmable, monitored and controlled through geographically centralized operating systems

[2104] Very strict requirements must be imposed for protection against unauthorized interference in the control center's software and control functions

[2105] There has been a significant exodus from peripheral areas in Northern Norway

[2106] In Finnmark, for example, the population has decreased by about 4,000 people between 1978 and

[2107] Research, conducted under the auspices of the University of Tromsø, shows that 80% of the emigrants from Finnmark were in the age group of 20-40 years

[2108] Approximately the same percentage has an education and vocational training that is above the average for the county's population

[2109] The relocation has led to reduced mobilization potential for the Armed Forces, but the Civil Defence has also experienced problems in the form of reduced deployments in certain coastal municipalities

[2110] It is in the interests of the Armed Forces that the settlement in peripheral Norway is maintained based on emergency preparedness considerations

[2111] This applies not least to personnel for the mobilization forces, the coastal population's contribution with observations of foreign vessels, etc. The Armed Forces' opportunities to contribute to maintaining a balanced settlement pattern are largely the ripple effects that the presence of standing military units and staffs creates for the local community

[2112] The Ministry will closely monitor developments regarding settlement patterns in Northern Norway, and in collaboration with other ministries, take measures that can counteract a development towards weakened preparedness

[2113] The Armed Forces' transportation needs will be significant during emergency situations/ war

[2114] Military transport resources are not sufficient to meet this need and must therefore be covered to a large extent by the emergency response agencies for such transports

[2115] Vehicles worth an estimated NOK 15 billion will be requisitioned for military purposes. The national civil air transport capacity is significant

[2116] The Chief of Defence will be responsible for the management of the country's airlines during emergencies and war

[2117] The companies remain civilian bodies and are expected to serve the entire total defense

[2118] In addition, civilian aircraft and helicopters are requisitioned and organized into military departments

[2119] A total of 80-100 helicopters will be mobilized and organized into seven squadrons

[2120] In investment value, this represents NOK 7 billion

[2121] In an emergency situation, the Armed Forces will also utilize the civilian airports at the country's disposal

[2122] The civilian maritime transport resources that will be available are of considerable scope

[2123] The sharp decline in Western countries' merchant fleets has led to growing concern about how shipping preparedness within NATO can be maintained

[2124] For Norway, the establishment of the Norwegian International Ship Register (NIS) has reversed the negative trend

[2125] The flagging of Norwegian tonnage has almost stopped, and Norwegian ships registered under flags of convenience have been included in the NIS

[2126] In April 1988, there were 220 Norwegian-owned ships registered in the register, totaling 6.5 million gross tons

[2127] Ships registered in NIS fall under the Requisition Act of 1962 in line with other Norwegian-registered ships

[2128] They therefore also, in principle, fall under the merchant fleet's emergency response scheme

[2129] The "Working Group to Assess the Preparedness for Shipping" (Bruland Committee), which submitted its report in December 1987, has proposed certain modifications to the basic arrangement

[2130] The selection process has not yet been finalized

[2131] The cooperation arrangements practiced locally, regionally and centrally between the main elements within the Total Defence will be maintained and further developed

[2132] This happens through daily cooperation and through joint exercises of both an allied and national nature

[2133] Particular emphasis will be placed on practicing and testing crisis management skills and the emergency preparedness system

[2134] Particular attention will also be paid to "Naval Control of Shipping" with a view to optimal utilization of our merchant fleet in times of crisis and war

[2135] The Norwegian Defence University College will retain its central place as an educational institution for the Total Defence Force

[2136] The task of the Armed Forces is to contribute to the fulfilment of the security policy goals set by the Storting and the Government

[2137] The security policy goals are discussed above in subchapter

[2138] Politically and militarily, it is a prerequisite for the security policy benefits we can derive from NATO cooperation that they are combined with a strong national defense

[2139] The armed forces must be able to

[2140] to provide the strongest possible resistance to any form of attack - to assert sovereignty over Norwegian territory and be able to quickly repel, limit or defeat various forms of infringement - to implement an effective monitoring and warning service - to reinforce the current preparedness in vulnerable areas quickly and with appropriate means - to create the best possible conditions for the reception, protection and support of, as well as cooperation with, allied forces in a crisis situation - to provide support to UN peacekeeping operations by earmarking and training special preparedness forces and, if requested, providing Norwegian contingents - to assist with the exercise of authority in areas under Norwegian resource jurisdiction in the form of control and supervision of activities on the continental shelf and in the economic zone - to provide as extensive support to civil society in peace as is compatible with the other tasks

[2141] The tasks are not listed in order of priority

[2142] When designing the Armed Forces and organizing the Armed Forces' activities, the requirements imposed by the various tasks must be coordinated with the aim of achieving the greatest possible total defense effect

[2143] The tasks sometimes have competing demands and therefore trade-offs and choices must be made

[2144] There is broad political consensus in Norway about the desirability of having a defense force with strong roots in the population

[2145] It provides the basis for our conscription system and high mobilization potential

[2146] At full mobilization, Norway will be able to field over 300,000 men under arms, and a significant number of civil defense personnel

[2147] This is a relatively larger portion of the population than in any other NATO country

[2148] Together with the civilian resources that will be drawn into the defense of the country in a crisis situation, these forces constitute the main pillar of the total defense concept discussed earlier in the chapter

[2149] A potential attacker should know that the entire community is enabled to provide effective resistance

[2150] The entire country must be defended in a possible conflict

[2151] The defense of Norway is primarily a national responsibility

[2152] Military development and the increasing cost of weapons technology place significant demands on society's efforts to maintain a strong and credible defense

[2153] This development is expected to continue for the foreseeable future

[2154] Norway's defense efforts are not only of military importance, but are also crucial to our position as a credible alliance partner

[2155] This not only has an impact on the contribution to the Alliance's defense resources, but also on Norway's position within the Alliance

[2156] Our own defense capability is important for the common defense of Western Europe and for the Alliance's ability to reinforce the northern flank in an emergency

[2157] Maintaining a strong national defense will be a signal to the outside world of political will to bear the burdens required to ensure the country's freedom and territorial integrity

[2158] It also contributes to Norway's view being given weight in the context of alliance politics

[2159] In this respect too, the Armed Forces must be considered a significant security policy instrument

[2160] Tasks related to asserting sovereignty and exercising authority in areas under Norwegian jurisdiction require suitable departments both on land, at sea, and in the air

[2161] Border guard, coast guard, other naval vessels and various types of aircraft are elements used in this context

[2162] We must also have a management structure that is capable of managing and coordinating the activities

[2163] The tasks are handled by the usual military command bodies

[2164] The Armed Forces' surveillance and early warning service makes important contributions to maintaining an overview and creating the necessary basis for decision-making both in peace and in war

[2165] In cases where NATO's surveillance and warning assets operate from Norwegian territory (e.g. the NAEW system), agreements have been made that ensure cooperation and safeguard Norwegian interests

[2166] Alliance cooperation is a comprehensive and resource-intensive undertaking

[2167] This includes the staffing and operation of national elements at allied headquarters and other allied joint institutions, the national share of joint infrastructure projects, and a significant national effort in connection with preparations for the reception and support of allied reinforcements to Norway

[2168] It also includes support for allied training activities on land, in the air, or in Norwegian waters

[2169] These measures are important and necessary for our contribution to the alliance, and the alliance's support for us, to function effectively and securely under all conditions

[2170] In addition to military tasks in Norway, the Armed Forces provide

[2171] major contributions to various activities of social importance

[2172] Participation in disaster relief and rescue services, and in various major events and functions, is part of this

[2173] The Norwegian UN service has a relatively large scope, which requires significant resources

[2174] The effort is often of significant importance in preserving peace and maintaining order in war-torn areas

[2175] The Armed Forces thus make an important contribution to the UN's peacekeeping work

[2176] Although the service itself does not contribute directly to solving defense tasks in Norway, it is valuable in that commanders and crews receive realistic training under difficult conditions

[2177] The defense forces are thus provided with a significant base of experience that overall contributes to increasing our own defense capabilities

[2178] UN service is important for leadership development in the armed forces

[2179] Reference is made to Chapter 3, where the Armed Forces' involvement in UN service is discussed in more detail

[2180] DEFENSE ASSESSMENTS AND TRAITS

[2181] The military situation Norway's military situation is influenced by our geographical location

[2182] Its significance is largely a function of the power constellations in international politics and military-technical developments

[2183] Both factors contribute to giving Norway a central position

[2184] The military situation is further influenced by the military forces that are deployed in our immediate vicinity, or that have such an initial disposition and capacity that they can be deployed in our area

[2185] In this context, our close proximity to the Kola Peninsula is an important factor

[2186] Our situation is also affected by the fact that military units that operate, or are based in Norway's immediate vicinity, may also have tasks far from Norwegian territory

[2187] In this context, it is not a given that all the allied units and departments that exercise in our surrounding areas in peacetime will be available in war

[2188] The local topographical and climatic conditions are important factors in military operations

[2189] The conditions in our country are somewhat unique in this context

[2190] The areas where military operations can have a direct and immediate influence on Norwegian security (Norwegian area of interest) are the Arctic, the Barents Sea, the Greenland Sea, the Norwegian Sea, Iceland, the North Sea/Skagerrak, the Baltic Sea area, Denmark, the Scandinavian Peninsula, Finland and the Soviet Union's northern region

[2191] The strategic importance of Norway and its areas of interest is primarily determined by

[2192] the importance of naval power for the Soviet Union in a global perspective

[2193] Two of the Soviet Union's four fleets, the Northern Fleet and the Baltic Fleet, are stationed in our immediate vicinity

[2194] the strategic nuclear balance

[2195] A significant part of the Soviet Union's deterrence potential is submarine-based missiles

[2196] Strategic bombers with long-range cruise missiles and land-based ballistic missiles are also part of the nuclear balance

[2197] Parts of these forces have areas of operation in or near our area of ​​interest

[2198] Norway is geographically located in the flight line of land-based missiles between the North American continent and the Soviet Union

[2199] the strategic transport and supply lines

[2200] In a protracted conflict with conventional weapons between the Warsaw Pact and NATO, NATO needs supplies and reinforcements across the Atlantic

[2201] For the Soviet Union, breaking these lines may appear to be an important goal

[2202] Norway is important for keeping supply lines open

[2203] Allied need for defense of supply lines links the defense of Norway to the defense of Europe

[2204] The use of military force against Norway can be considered to be implemented on a scale from attacks with weapons of mass destruction to limited military demonstrations or incidents

[2205] An attack could theoretically be launched either as part of a major conflict between NATO and the Warsaw Pact, or as part of a limited conflict

[2206] Norwegian defense policy primarily aims to help prevent a major conflict by blocking the possibilities for a limited attack

[2207] Strategic warning is a notification that measures have been initiated that may be preparations for an attack

[2208] Warning period is the period from the time the warning is issued until the outbreak of war is expected to occur

[2209] New monitoring tools and methods will quickly provide an overview of developments in a crisis situation

[2210] This provides increased opportunities to react in a timely manner

[2211] At the same time, it will be just as important as before to interpret the signals correctly

[2212] In the worst case, strategic war preparations can be made over such a long period of time that vigilance is weakened

[2213] The signals can also be drowned in the amount of unclear and contradictory information

[2214] Purposeful escalation and de-escalation over a longer period of time may be a pattern of action that aims to achieve such an effect

[2215] The warning period one decides to use will influence the choice of combat readiness and the initial disposition of forces

[2216] A defense based on mobilization requires a longer warning period than a defense based on standing forces, not only because it takes longer to get the forces combat-ready, but also because the societal consequences of raising the readiness level are greater

[2217] The decision will thus become more difficult to make, and in addition to a longer notice period, will also require a more secure and unambiguous notice

[2218] The Warsaw Pact forces that are particularly important for Norwegian security include

[2219] the naval forces of the Northern Fleet and the Baltic Fleet - the army and air forces of the Leningrad and Baltic military districts - Soviet and other WP forces grouped in the northern parts of Poland and East Germany - other forces of the Soviet Union's Western Military Districts - forces in the strategic reserve

[2220] Forces in the Arkhangelsk Air Defense District, which is responsible for the air defense of large parts of the Leningrad Military District and adjacent areas, will also have to be taken into account

[2221] It is primarily the forces in the Leningrad Military District and the Northern Fleet's activities that can affect the situation in Northern Norway, Central Norway and our Arctic areas

[2222] The situation in southern Norway is most affected by forces in the northernmost parts of the Central European Front and the Baltic Military District

[2223] The allied forces that are particularly important for Norwegian security include

[2224] the allied amphibious, land and air defense forces that, according to the reinforcement plans, have Norway as a deployment option - the allied naval forces that are included in the plans for operations in our adjacent sea areas

[2225] The forces include, among other things, American aircraft carrier groups, submarines and maritime aircraft

[2226] A significant portion of the European NATO countries' navies are part of these allied naval forces

[2227] Allied naval forces under national command, including French naval forces, which can operate in the North Atlantic or the Norwegian Sea - Danish and West German land and air forces in Denmark and Northern Germany NATO's naval forces are mobile and have many other missions than operations in our immediate areas

[2228] It will depend on the situation to what extent they will operate so that they contribute directly to the defense of Norway

[2229] Norwegian defense planning cannot therefore be based on the efforts of allied naval forces, but must plan to enable us to cooperate with such forces to the extent that they become available

[2230] Neutral forces To the extent that Sweden and Finland are able to maintain armed neutrality in war, this helps to prevent Norway from being attacked over their territories

[2231] The situation in the High North

[2232] The military situation in the High North is dominated primarily by the Soviet Union's strategic forces and the naval capabilities of the Soviet Navy

[2233] The addition of modern aircraft, surface vessels and submarines, as well as cruise missiles and other types of remotely delivered weapons, has increased the Northern Fleet's combat power, and over the past fifteen years has enabled Soviet naval forces to operate gradually further south in the Norwegian Sea

[2234] The modernization of Western navies, and especially the modernization and reconstruction of the United States Navy throughout the 1980s, has helped to reduce the effects of Soviet naval buildup

[2235] The Soviet ground and air forces have also undergone a development and modernization process that has increased the forces' effectiveness and mobility

[2236] The introduction of attack and transport helicopters into the Soviet army formations has contributed to increasing the Soviet army's off-road mobility, and thus to reducing the advantages that Norwegian topography provides in a defense context

[2237] The attack helicopters also provide army forces with significantly increased firepower

[2238] New generations of fighter jets increase the range and penetration capabilities of the Soviet air forces

[2239] Despite the fact that extensive modernization has also taken place within Western air forces, NATO's technological lead has been reduced

[2240] Ground Forces Within the Leningrad Military District, there are 11 motorized infantry divisions with a peacetime configuration that means that they must be provided with mobilization reinforcements to varying degrees to reach full strength

[2241] Soviet army forces are divided into four categories

[2242] Category 1 divisions have approximately 90% peacetime manning, category 2 have approximately 50-75%, while category 3 have approximately 10-50% of war-ready forces in place in peacetime

[2243] The pure mobilization divisions (category 4) have a cadre staffing of up to 5%

[2244] Of the forces within the Leningrad Military District, none are believed to be of Category 1, three of Category 2, six of Category 3, while two of the 11 divisions are believed to be pure mobilization formations

[2245] In peacetime, two active motorized infantry divisions of category 2 and one mobilization division are stationed on the Kola Peninsula

[2246] It is assumed that the mobilization forces can partly be set up locally, and partly be supplied with personnel from outside

[2247] There is also a standing marine infantry brigade (category 1) on the Kola Peninsula and equipment for another one is stored

[2248] A standing airborne division (category 1) is stationed in the Leningrad region

[2249] There is also an airmobile brigade (BMD) and a corresponding battalion

[2250] The army forces are supported by, among other things, four tactical missile brigades (SS-1c

[2251] Within the military district, there is a missile brigade (SS-12/22) that is covered by the INF Treaty

[2252] Improved land communications with the Leningrad region and the large number of airfields on the Kola Peninsula make it possible to reinforce the existing fighting forces in the area relatively quickly

[2253] It is estimated that the transport capacity will be sufficient to transfer three motorized infantry divisions within four to five days

[2254] However, the transport lines are vulnerable

[2255] Large-scale transfers will also not be able to be carried out unnoticed

[2256] A large-scale force buildup on Kola in a conflict situation, or in a buildup phase, would be an important element of strategic alert

[2257] No full-scale exercises involving the transfer of divisions from the south to the Kola Peninsula have been observed

[2258] The Northern Fleet has a sufficient number of amphibious vessels for the Marine Infantry Brigade to carry out a full-scale landing operation, or alternatively several smaller landings

[2259] There is usually enough tonnage of merchant vessels in the ports of the Kola Peninsula and in local waters to allow two motorized infantry divisions to be moved at once

[2260] Such transport does not necessarily depend on the troops being unloaded at port

[2283] The Northern Fleet's vessels will be able to receive protection against air attacks in the sea areas outside Troms

[2284] Strategic aircraft are not permanently stationed in the highlands, but long-range bombers, including the BACKFIRE type, occasionally operate from the airports there

[2286] In the period 1989-93, the land combat forces on the Kola Peninsula are numerically far larger than ours

[2287] They have sufficient capacity to carry out a surprise attack against the northeasternmost parts of Northern Norway, but they must probably be seen primarily in the context of the need to secure the strategically important naval bases in the area

[2288] The Northern Fleet comprises a total of approximately 600 vessels

[2289] About 40 are submarines with strategic missiles

[2292] They are no longer dependent on long, vulnerable transfer routes through the Norwegian Sea and the passages between Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands to reach their launch areas in the Atlantic

[2293] As mentioned, this has led to increased use of Arctic sea areas as an area of operations

[2294] Here, the submarines are easier to protect, and the command and control arrangements can be made more secure and reliable

[2295] Submarines with medium-range strategic missiles (Y-class) have been withdrawn to the Norwegian Sea

[2296] From there they can reach targets in Europe

[2297] The stationing means that it will be more difficult to keep track of the submarines' movements

[2298] An important source of warning is being weakened for both Norway and the Alliance as a whole

[2314] Airports and other installations in Norway that are important for the battle for the Norwegian Sea could be particularly vulnerable

[2316] In building up the Soviet submarine fleet, the focus has traditionally been on quantity over quality

[2317] The Soviet Union therefore has more, but for example consistently noisier, submarines than the Western navies

[2318] This situation is about to change

[2319] Several of the newer Soviet submarine types can compete with Western submarines

[2320] At the same time, it is not assumed that Soviet shipyards will be able to produce new advanced submarines at the same rate as older vessels are withdrawn from service

[2321] The large number of submarines built in the 1960s and 1970s will probably have to be phased out in the next ten to fifteen years

[2322] Fewer, but more advanced submarines with a completely different armament, will be able to present NATO with different challenges than today

[2323] The Northern Fleet has about 90 larger and about 100 smaller surface combat vessels

[2324] Furthermore, several larger civilian ro-ro vessels are available; as well as special vessels that are independent of the quay (with barges on board) and a large number of auxiliary vessels

[2326] This suggests that the surface forces also have an important role in protecting the strategic submarines

[2327] A smaller number of the Northern Fleet's larger surface combat vessels are equipped with modern cruise missiles for use against ship targets, with ranges of around 500 km

[2328] Surface forces cannot operate over time in war without the cover of their own land-based or aircraft carrier-based air defense fighters

[2329] Kiev-class aircraft carriers also do not have the capacity to establish air superiority over their own forces within range of NATO land- or carrier-based air defense fighters

[2330] The Northern Fleet's surface vessels are therefore largely relegated to operating under the cover of their own land-based air defense fighters

[2331] There is a steady increase in the Northern Fleet's combat power through the introduction of new vessel types and weapons, and the modernization of old ones

[2332] The Northern Fleet's larger surface vessels, supported by supply ships, represent a potential for advancing Soviet interests in distant waters through the traditional use of sea power

[2333] The Northern Fleet's own air force consists of approximately 400 aircraft, including approximately 70 maritime attack aircraft, approximately 60 reconnaissance aircraft, approximately 25 light fighter-bombers for operations from aircraft carriers, approximately 80 anti-submarine (ASW) aircraft, 70 ASW helicopters and approximately 70 transport aircraft and helicopters

[2334] The navy's air force is also built up with a strong anti-submarine capability, and is tasked with supporting the navy's operations against invading Western submarines

[2335] The maritime attack aircraft have attacks on NATO or US aircraft carrier forces as their main task

[2336] They are supported in this task by submarines and surface vessels with long-range cruise missiles

[2337] A possible attack on Northern Norway would probably have to take place as a coordinated operation by army, navy and air forces

[2338] The limited capacity of vulnerable supply lines overland, and the emphasis that an attacker will therefore have to place on sea transport of forces, materiel and supplies, makes sea control in the Norwegian Sea a key factor in the battle for Northern Norway

[2339] The buildup and modernization of all branches of defense on the Kola Peninsula, together with the ability to reinforce the area with forces from more southern parts of the Leningrad Military District, has in sum strengthened the Soviet Union's military potential in our immediate vicinity

[2340] But development has not stood still on the western side either

[2341] At sea, the development of advanced anti-ship missiles such as HARPOON, EXOCET, and perhaps especially TOMAHAWK, has contributed to NATO's naval forces significantly strengthening their combat power in an area where the Soviet Navy was dominant for many years

[2342] TOMAHAWK has high target flexibility in that new targets can be programmed before launch, and in that the missile can be adapted to a number of platforms

[2343] The weapon is available in both a naval and a land-based version

[2345] Until the parties’ develop a sufficient ability to provide target data from satellite, the party with air superiority will have an advantage

[2346] The political and strategic consequences of the introduction of long-range cruise missiles at sea on both sides are discussed in more detail in the report's chapter

[2347] The update of the Norwegian forces described elsewhere in the report, together with the completion of the advance storage programs for own and allied forces, will help increase the firepower and mobility of these forces and their ability to be in place quickly if necessary

[2348] Allied exercises in our nearby sea areas in recent years demonstrate the will and, not least, the ability to carry out complex coordinated operations under marginal conditions

[2349] This development has, in sum, helped to offset some of the impact of the Soviet military buildup in our area of interest

[2350] The situation in the Baltic Sea area

[2351] While the military threat to Norway from the north is mainly linked to the Kola Peninsula, the Warsaw Pact forces in the Baltic Sea area constitute the possible threat from the south

[2352] NATO must view these forces from both a northern flank and a central sector perspective

[2353] The Baltic Fleet has not been expanded to the same extent as the Northern Fleet, but still has considerable striking power and equipment of consistently high quality

[2354] Some of the Soviet Union's most important shipyards and a number of naval bases are located on the Baltic Sea

[2355] The land forces in the Baltic Military District and the northern parts of Poland and East Germany include approximately 30 infantry and tank divisions (of which about half are assumed to be Category 1 and the rest Category 3), two airborne divisions (one is assumed to be Category 1 and the other Category 3), one marine infantry brigade, one marine brigade, one airmobile brigade, a large number of support divisions, and some tactical missile divisions

[2356] It is expected that only parts of this force will be able to be deployed in an attack against Danish and northern German territory

[2357] The Soviet tactical air forces in East Germany consist of approximately 1,100 fighter aircraft and helicopters, while in Poland, among other things, 220 long-range attack aircraft (Fencer) are stationed

[2358] The proportion of these air forces that can be made available in the Baltic Sea area at any time during a potential conflict will depend on the situation on the other front lines

[2359] The Baltic Fleet consists of approximately 500 vessels, of which approximately 30 are operational submarines, approximately 45 larger combat vessels and approximately 50 landing craft

[2360] The Baltic Fleet has sufficient amphibious capacity to allow the Marine Infantry Brigade and the Marine Landing Brigade to be deployed on a full scale in operations against NATO's area in the Baltic Sea and in straits and belts

[2361] The Baltic Fleet has its own air force

[2362] The Polish and East German navies consist of approximately 120 and approximately 130 combat vessels, respectively

[2363] A number of auxiliary vessels are also available

[2364] The merchant fleets of the Warsaw Pact countries in the Baltic Sea also have a significant capacity to transport troops and material from the rear areas and into ports in the combat zone, behind their own lines

[2365] The strength of the Baltic Fleet is considered by the West to exceed the Soviet Union's defense needs in the area

[2366] The large amphibious capacity poses a challenge to NATO's defense of the Baltic Sea outlets

[2367] The organization and training plans for the combat forces in the Baltics and the rest of the Baltic Sea region indicate that the forces may have an important task of controlling straits and belts in a conflict

[2368] Soviet domination of the Baltic Sea outlets and associated Danish and West German territory would pose a significant threat both to NATO's central sector and to southern Norway

[2369] NATO forces in West Germany and Denmark therefore play a direct role in the defense of Southern Norway

[2370] For NATO, it will be an overarching task to prevent the Soviet Baltic Fleet from reaching the North Sea and the Norwegian Sea, where it can, among other things, cooperate with units from the Northern Fleet

[2371] The possibilities for preventing air attacks against southern Norway will depend on the airspace between NATO's Northern and Central Commands being under Allied control

[2372] It is therefore of vital importance for the defense of Southern Norway that Danish and Northern German territory is held

[2373] It is also a prerequisite for preventing Norway from being cut off from the Allied forces on the continent

[2374] The Danish defense can take advantage of the natural barriers located in the shallow waters and narrow straits and belts

[2375] The country's military forces are specifically geared towards exploiting these advantages

[2376] However, northern German and Danish landmasses offer few natural obstacles to an attacker

[2377] The defense of the Baltic Sea outlets is significantly dependent on West German and other allied efforts

[2378] The West German defense has significant resources in the area

[2379] The West German Navy's main task, together with the Danish one, is to control straits and belts

[2380] Sailing out of the Baltic Sea is not only conditioned by securing straits and belts, but also requires control over the coast of Southern Norway

[2381] An attack against Southern Norway may come after the situation is locked in on the central front

[2382] The general purpose would be to create movement

[2383] By breaking through on the flank in Denmark and northern Germany and then turning north, one could advance into southern Norway with the aim of exerting pressure on the transatlantic supply lines from there

[2384] An operation against southern Norway could thus help lay the groundwork for victory in the rest of Central Europe

[2385] Also, a possible attack on southern Norway would probably have to take place as a coordinated operation of army, navy and air forces, including naval infantry and parachute or airborne units

[2386] The operation could only be carried out after the West German/Danish front had been broken through and the forces there defeated

[2387] The short distance between Jutland and Southern Norway facilitates the transfer of army forces by helicopters on a large scale

[2388] If it is to succeed in building up larger forces and supply lines with the capacity to carry out a campaign with the aim of permanently conquering southern Norway, it would require naval control in the Skagerrak and parts of the North Sea as well as air superiority in the same area

[2389] An attack on southern Norway could also be carried out through Sweden

[2390] Such an attack could be carried out regardless of whether the Danish straits and belts were open

[2391] It could therefore be deployed early in a conflict, and among other things, have the aim of opening the Baltic Sea outlets by exerting pressure on them from two sides

[2392] The Swedish defense capability helps to keep the threshold for such operations high, i.e. the resource requirements can be so great that the possibilities of winning on more central front sections are weakened

[2393] Southern Norway is a backward area both in relation to Northern Norway and in relation to Denmark/Northern Germany

[2394] The events in Denmark/Northern Germany, but also in Northern Norway, which may have preceded an attack on Southern Norway, may also have led to the mobilization of Allied forces in the region

[2395] Southern Norway is also within reach of airports in Great Britain, and several major Allied naval bases are located along the North Sea

[2396] The negative consequences for the Alliance of Soviet control over southern Norway and the adjacent sea areas and airspace would be very great

[2397] Nuclear and chemical weapons The Soviet Union possesses a significant number of strategic, medium- and short-range missiles that can reach targets on Norwegian territory

[2398] In our immediate area, it is the land forces' mobile tactical missile systems that primarily threaten our area

[2399] Most types of artillery are believed to have nuclear delivery capability

[2400] All of Norway is today within range of medium-range missiles

[2412] Developments on the military side in the years ahead

[2413] If weapons technology development is not controlled or limited by arms control or disarmament agreements, the general consequence of developments within the Soviet forces in our area of interest in the years ahead could take the following form

[2414] The Northern Fleet's combat capability will likely increase through continued strengthening of the surface, submarine and air forces

[2415] The development of a new class of aircraft carrier in the Soviet Navy has come a long way

[2416] It is not known where the vessels will be stationed, but their introduction will significantly increase the Soviet Union's naval capabilities

[2417] The Soviet Navy is nevertheless not expected to be able to develop a traditional aircraft carrier capability, in the Western sense of the term, in the coming years

[2418] The new airborne warning and control system (Il-76 MAINSTAY) will streamline flight operations with both tactical fighter bombers and interceptor fighters, but the aircraft cannot operate out of range of land-based air defense fighters

[2419] The ability for more sustained air operations in Norwegian airspace and over the sea well west of Troms will nevertheless increase in line with the introduction of aircraft with longer ranges

[2420] New aircraft- and ship-based cruise missiles in principle increase the ability to attack targets at long distances

[2421] However, the ability to utilize the range effectively against well-defended targets such as aircraft carrier groups is limited, as one is dependent on target guidance from a platform in direct contact with the target

[2422] It becomes easier to bypass strong defenses through extensive use of airmobile units and helicopters of all types

[2423] This could reduce the advantage that our difficult terrain has given us so far

[2424] However, tank divisions, heavy armored vehicles, heavier artillery and larger supply transports will still depend on the road network for movement

[2426] The strategic context in the Nordic Swedish area is believed to have limited strategic intrinsic value

[2427] The greatest threat to Sweden seems to lie in the fact that Swedish territory and airspace could serve as a transit area in the event of a westward advance

[2428] The northernmost parts of Sweden, and the southernmost areas towards the straits and belts, have often been perceived as particularly vulnerable

[2429] The entire Swedish airspace may be subject to overflights by combat and transport aircraft, and by cruise missiles

[2430] Swedish territory provides coverage along our entire long common border

[2431] Coverage is of utmost importance to our own defense capabilities

[2432] According to Swedish assessment, the Northern European and North Atlantic area has gained greater military strategic importance in recent years, with an increased risk of hostilities within the Nordic area already in the initial phases of a great power conflict

[2433] Swedish defense planning is based on the assumption that an attack on Sweden could occur as part of a conflict between the great power alliances

[2434] This means that an attacker could reasonably only use limited parts of his resources against Sweden

[2435] In the Swedish view, the intention could be to utilize the country as a transit and base area against targets in the Swedish vicinity

[2436] The size and scope of the Swedish defense force has been reduced in recent decades

[2437] In Sweden's view, however, it is within the country's economic and technical capabilities to maintain an effective defense in the years ahead

[2438] This defense should have such strength, composition and readiness that an attack on Sweden requires such great forces and resources, and takes so long, that the advantages that the attacker could gain are not in any reasonable proportion to the effort

[2439] Finnish territory, like northern Sweden, constitutes a possible strategic transit area in the event of an attack on our country

[2440] In both Sweden and Finland, it is felt that the northern parts of the countries have become more vulnerable, and a number of defense measures have therefore been taken in the area

[2441] Finnish defense will be able to provide significant resistance in the event of an attack

[2442] This must be assumed to create uncertainty among a potential attacker and have a deterrent effect

[2443] The Danish defense, together with West German forces, forms a forward defense of Norway in the south

[2444] Despite weaknesses, Denmark's defense can, in the Danish view, be considered credible and reasonably effective

[2445] If the conditions for effective defense of the Baltic Sea outlets fail, our own defense faces very difficult challenges
