[2447] a special role in alliance defense

[2448] Due to Norway's dependence on sea-borne reinforcements and supplies, the defense of Iceland has direct and crucial importance for the defense of Norway

[2449] The main task of the Armed Forces is to prevent an armed attack against Norway, and to defend Norwegian territory if the country is nevertheless attacked

[2450] The country's geographical size, topography, and climate pose significant obstacles to an attacker

[2451] This can be exploited to our advantage

[2452] On the other hand, a large area of land must be defended by a relatively small population

[2453] This places great demands on the defense's mobility and ability to quickly redeploy

[2454] Our defense is clearly defensive in nature

[2455] The buildup must nevertheless be such that after the country is attacked, we can strike back and turn the tide of the conflict

[2456] The Armed Forces must be able to quickly mobilize the available resources

[2457] This depends on warning and correct and timely political and military decisions

[2458] Of particular importance is the decision to request Allied reinforcements

[2459] If handled correctly, this will act as a deterrent to attacks

[2460] Reinforcement plans must be designed and practiced in such a way that they appear credible

[2461] This is believed to contribute to deterrence

[2462] The Soviet Union's military forces in our immediate area have a capacity that provides several deployment options

[2463] Attacks on Norwegian territory could be one of them

[2464] In defense planning, we must emphasize the physical possibilities that exist and contain them

[2465] As the possible options are many, we face significant uncertainties

[2466] This means that we must consider a broad spectrum of attack possibilities and alternative courses of action

[2467] Norway on its own has no ability to balance the military force that can be deployed against the country

[2468] Our defense must be seen in light of NATO's overall military strength and war prevention capability

[2469] Our defense planning assumes that an attack on Norway triggers solidarity obligations in NATO

[2470] Similarly, Norway's defense is also part of the total NATO defense

[2471] It is still likely that the central section will be the decisive area in a possible major war in Europe

[2472] Both alliances will probably prioritize their resources based on the overall consideration of influencing the development of the conflict in this area

[2473] NATO's primary mission is to deter attacks

[2474] Although it is difficult to imagine armed conflict in our continent as long as the Alliance maintains its credibility, conflicts can arise as a result of crises that the parties have failed to control

[2475] It is important that our defense is structured based on consideration of the challenges that it may face in a comprehensive conflict

[2476] These can be very demanding

[2477] But only by defending the country in such contexts does the defense fulfill its task, while at the same time fulfilling our obligations to the Alliance

[2478] However, we must at all times assess which conflict situations we may be directly confronted with, and which should therefore be of dimension to the Norwegian Armed Forces based on the possibilities that Norwegian defense efforts have to influence the outcome

[2479] A major nuclear war is an extreme point where the effect of Norwegian efforts will be small

[2480] Such a conflict cannot be won by either party

[2481] Everyone would be a loser

[2482] It is therefore so important that such a war is never fought

[2483] The Soviet Union has long been a distinct land power

[2484] A far-reaching need to secure one's own territory has traditionally been an important part of the country's foreign and security policy

[2485] This seems to continue

[2486] The development of weapons technology may have led to greater demands on control over one's own land area and adjacent "buffer zones" than before

[2487] The Soviet maritime buildup may have been motivated in part by the desire to control the adjacent sea and land areas, thereby increasing the protection of the homeland

[2488] But the composition of the Northern Fleet indicates that it has tasks beyond this

[2489] This has led to a deterioration of Norway's strategic situation

[2490] Allied defense cooperation is therefore of increasing importance to us

[2491] For deterrence purposes, Allied reinforcement plans for the country are an important signal that the defense of Norwegian territory is both formally and actually part of the Alliance's overall commitments

[2492] The ability to observe and interpret military activity in our immediate areas is important in order to make correct and timely decisions

[2493] The significance of this is reinforced by the imbalance that exists initially between Norwegian national defense capabilities and the Soviet military forces in the area

[2494] The work carried out by Norwegian intelligence and surveillance, and NATO's airborne radar warning, helps to enable appropriately tailored responses both from Norwegian authorities and from the Alliance as a whole

[2495] Modern intelligence tools provide an overview of unusual activity and improve the possibilities for early warning

[2496] Seen in the context of the changes in the security policy climate that could precede military dispositions, this provides a basis for interpreting both military and political signals so that concrete measures can be taken

[2497] However, such signals will often be very ambiguous and surrounded by great uncertainty

[2498] History has many examples of how unexpected events are hidden and covered up by "normal" businesses, and only become clear when it is too late

[2499] This emphasizes the importance of a good intelligence service, of a preparedness that does not require constant adjustments in line with minor changes in the environment, as well as the ability to respond repeatedly to alerts, without thereby depleting our departments' readiness for action

[2500] Conflict situations and regional priorities

[2501] Norway flanks the outlets to the world's oceans for two of the Soviet Union's four fleets

[2502] The control of the outlets is of essential importance to the Soviet Union

[2503] For NATO, our northernmost and southernmost parts of the country form a forward area from which NATO can monitor and influence the sailings

[2504] Southern Norway also has an important flank position in operations on the Central European section

[2505] It is difficult to imagine an isolated attack on Norway

[2506] However, both Northern Norway and Southern Norway could conceivably be attacked as part of operations against Western Europe, especially if control over Norwegian territory is considered important for the final outcome of the conflict

[2507] The country could also be exposed to attacks to create new movement if a war centered in Central Europe were to become entrenched

[2508] Strategically important areas and objects across the country could conceivably be neutralized without direct physical occupation

[2509] This could happen through assault, sabotage or raid-like operations, or through air and missile attacks

[2510] What is common to these types of operations is that they can be implemented without any prior notice

[2511] Our own force buildup is heavily dependent on the time it takes to get units up and in place

[2512] The forces need time for mobilization, preparation and transportation to the deployment areas

[2513] The bulk of Allied reinforcements would come from the North American continent

[2514] These forces may have different areas of deployment

[2515] It will be the current situation that determines where they will be deployed

[2516] A realistic view of what national and allied reinforcements can be expected, and when they can be in place, are important elements in assessing our capabilities to meet the challenges that the defense may face

[2517] Since reinforcements play such a large role in the defense of Norway in general, and for Northern Norway in particular, an attack would be least resource-intensive at an early stage in a conflict

[2518] Assessments of the effectiveness of the Norwegian and allied reinforcement apparatus will largely determine the strategic goals an attacker can set

[2519] If it were possible to neutralize the ports and airports that are central in this regard, our defense could soon find itself in a critical situation

[2520] A number of factors indicate that Northern Norway would be of particularly great strategic importance in a possible conflict

[2521] One of the Northern Fleet's most important tasks is probably to protect the Soviet strategic submarine capability and its base areas on the Kola Peninsula

[2522] With this goal in mind, Northern Norway could be at risk

[2523] The region flanks the entire northern Norwegian Sea

[2524] Possession of northern Norwegian ports and airports could provide significant strategic advantages through the expanded possibilities for controlling the sea areas and supporting the Northern Fleet's operations

[2525] For NATO, Northern Norway plays an important role in the defense of the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic

[2526] In a naval strategic context, the Alliance faces serious challenges due to Soviet maritime development

[2527] Factors related to both military-strategic assessments and the desire to promote Norwegian interests in allied defense cooperation provide important justifications for prioritizing our defense efforts in Northern Norway

[2528] Through a strong national defense of the region, we prevent the area from being threatened with a modest military effort

[2529] By prioritizing Northern Norway, we take advantage of being able to build up forces that can counteract or avert a threat to the region more quickly and effectively than our allies

[2530] For national reasons, it will also be essential to ensure that we have the greatest possible control over military development in the most vulnerable area of our country

[2531] In addition, a national prioritization of Northern Norway - within a framework that reconciles security considerations with reassurance - will help reduce uncertainty in a sensitive area

[2532] It is assumed that the Soviet forces in the north have, in principle, sufficient capacity to carry out an isolated and limited attack against the northeasternmost parts of Norway, without us being able to count on preparation time of any practical significance

[2533] Such an operation could hardly be launched without being prepared that the attack could trigger extensive hostilities beyond the attacked parts of Northern Norway

[2534] As long as NATO remains a credible alliance, the risks of a limited operation would hardly be proportionate to the possible strategic gains

[2535] A more extensive attack in the north that goes deeper into Norwegian territory requires larger combat-ready forces than those stationed on the Kola Peninsula

[2536] It is difficult to imagine such an operation being carried out without triggering a major conflict between the alliances

[2537] The attack could come at the same time as hostilities on other fronts, but a time shift is also conceivable

[2538] The build-up of forces can hardly take place in secret

[2539] Other war adaptation measures would probably also be recorded

[2540] This could provide strategic warning

[2541] Northern Norway's defense potential is limited

[2542] This makes it necessary to establish a defense threshold in the region with standing and locally rapidly mobilizable forces

[2543] The threshold must be high enough to prevent the area from being threatened by modest forces

[2544] It should also be sufficient to limit an attacker's freedom of action

[2706] Introduction The structure and activities of the Armed Forces depend on the tasks assigned to it and the financial and personnel frameworks that are established

[2707] The framework conditions must be seen in the context of the country's economy and the other societal tasks that must be solved

[2708] This section deals with the financial and personnel framework conditions for the Armed Forces' activities during the period

[2709] A description of the country's current economic situation and a perspective sketch of developments up to the mid-1990s are provided

[2710] Furthermore, a distribution of the financial framework between the main sectors of operations and investment has been suggested

[2711] Where appropriate, a comparison has been made with the Defence Commission's proposals

[2712] The defense budget and the economy In addition to military and security policy considerations, an assessment of the country's economy will be an important factor when the Government determines the framework for the annual defense budgets, and when guidelines are to be drawn up and plans are prepared for several years to come

[2713] Since this announcement concerns the last five-year period of the Defence Commission's 15-year perspective plan, a brief discussion will be given below of the deliberations the Defence Commission made about the country's economy when it drew up its proposal and of the changes to the Commission's plan that have subsequently been made

[2719] According to the commission's plan, defense spending would take up a decreasing portion of the country's economy and public consumption

[2725] With this time perspective, uncertainty also increased, and it had to be assumed that circumstances would arise that the ongoing planning would have to monitor and assess, in order to possibly adjust the set course

[2727] The country's economic situation has deteriorated significantly since then, and this must be reflected in the main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities in the period

[2736] The economic perspectives The Norwegian economy is currently facing major and serious challenges

[2737] There has become a large gap between what is used and what is produced in Norway

[2738] There is still strong underlying cost pressure in the economy, and the number of profitable companies in competitive industries outside the oil industry is too small

[2739] The foreign trade deficit is worrying and will become an unmanageable problem in the long term if the trend continues

[2740] In St report no. 4 for

[2741] Perspectives and reforms in economic policy, the Government has outlined a strategy for restoring balance in the Norwegian economy

[2742] The strategy has two main elements

[2743] Domestic demand must continue to be restrained in order to alleviate pressure on the economy, reduce deficits in the foreign economy and create room for growth in the competitive part of Norwegian business

[2744] We must work systematically to increase the growth potential of the economy and promote more balanced industrial development by curbing the growth in costs and stimulating increased restructuring, innovation and increased productivity

[2745] In Report to the Parliament no. 4, a macroeconomic projection for 1991 and 1995 is presented, illustrating what must be achieved in order to achieve a reasonably satisfactory development in the Norwegian economy even if petroleum prices remain low in the years ahead

[2746] There is a great deal of uncertainty surrounding the economic outlook

[2747] The uncertainty makes it very difficult to estimate how long it may take to correct the imbalances in the economy

[2748] If any of the assumptions fail, economic development could be significantly weaker than projected

[2749] In Report No. 4 to the Parliament, a growth in the gross domestic product of Norway's trading partners of 2.5 percent was assumed

[2750] There is a risk that growth could become weaker

[2751] Weaker international growth will make it more challenging to restore balance in the Norwegian economy

[2752] The assumptions about petroleum prices in Report No. 4 to the Parliament were considered cautious

[2753] A slight increase in oil prices from 1986 is assumed

[2754] These estimates must now be considered more realistic than when Report No. 4 was presented to the Parliament

[2755] The likelihood of reducing the gap between what is produced and what is consumed using petroleum revenues has diminished

[2756] But it must be emphasized that the uncertainty associated with petroleum prices is great

[2757] The economic plan and projections are based on cost growth in Norway coming down to the same level as our trading partners over the course of

[2758] This will be crucial for restoring the imbalances in the economy

[2759] The rapid cost growth of recent years cannot therefore continue

[2792] This will also have consequences for the planning of the Armed Forces' activities in the coming years

[2793] The general security and defense policy situation requires a credible and balanced national defense

[2794] The government is actively working to improve conditions for allied reinforcements, but a strong national defense is the cornerstone of Norway's defense

[2795] Maintaining and improving national defense will entail costly renewals

[2796] On the material side, there is a need to replace obsolete material, and in the construction sector there are also several measures that will result in increased expenses

[2797] The Armed Forces thus face significant challenges in adapting their operations to changes in resource availability (lower growth in appropriations and reduction in man-year consumption) while maintaining their defense capabilities

[2798] Measures will therefore be taken to curb operational growth and secure necessary investments for our future defense

[2799] To accomplish such a task, measures of varying nature must be taken

[2800] Overarching systems such as planning systems, budget systems, personnel management systems, etc. must be changed and adapted to a management by objectives form

[2801] Information and training in new systems must be strengthened and attitudes influenced

[2802] Emphasis will be placed on providing clear priorities for structure and activities within alternative resource frameworks

[2803] Flexibility in the use of resources should be increased and unnecessary constraints should be loosened

[2804] This will increase freedom of action, and necessary concrete measures will be more easily implemented

[2805] As described earlier in the report, the current security policy situation, and the basis for assessing future developments, indicate that the defense capability will be maintained

[2806] Through the main guidelines in this announcement, the Government is creating the conditions for this to be possible

[2807] On the other hand, the Government finds it right that the Armed Forces also contribute to the necessary restructuring in the period 1989-93 to remedy the unusually difficult economic situation for the country

[2808] Although great emphasis will be placed on increasing flexibility, constraints in the defense budget mean that there are clear limitations to this flexibility in the next five-year period

[2809] The government's goal is to provide the Armed Forces with an average real growth of two percent per year

[2810] However, a general reservation must be made regarding the uncertainty inherent in the prospects for economic development, both for the period as a whole and for individual years in the period

[2811] Growth can thus vary from year to year, and as mentioned, will have to be seen in relation to economic development

[2812] Defence capability will be maintained both by deploying financial resources and by means of significant productivity-enhancing measures

[2813] Defense capabilities will have to be continuously assessed in relation to security policy developments and the demands they impose, especially in our immediate areas

[2814] The lack of balance between ambition level and access to resources in the Armed Forces is, as demonstrated in the

[2815] no. 230 (1983-84) p. 11, the result of several circumstances going back many years

[2816] A particularly important reason is that neither the budget level nor structural objectives were adjusted in connection with the cessation of arms aid at the end of the sixties

[2817] In the period 1950-68, this had on average corresponded to about 20 percent of the defense budget

[2818] Secondly, efforts to restore balance through rationalization and efficiency have not yielded sufficient results

[2819] The peacetime organization is too large and the operating methods too expensive

[2820] Therefore, operating expenses become so high that the investment level becomes too low

[2821] A fundamental review is now needed

[2822] In addition, the Armed Forces have been given expanded tasks without the framework having been significantly changed

[2823] This is a problem that has not only arisen in recent years

[2824] It has been recurring

[2825] It is of course the political authorities who determine the tasks and their priorities

DEFENCE STRUCTURAL GOALS** **10.1 Basis** The goal of the defence structure is to maintain a defence organisation and force composition that enables the Defence to carry out its war prevention and deterrence tasks

[2937] The term defense capability refers to an assessment of our expected ability to solve defense tasks

[2938] Defence capability depends on the economic framework conditions, the personnel and material resources that society makes available, and the way in which these resources are utilized

[2939] This forms the basis for the structural composition and for the combat capability that our national forces can produce

[2940] Our country is also part of a defense alliance

[2941] The scope and value of one's own defense efforts must therefore be assessed in the context of the alliance

[2942] Defense capability must be assessed on the basis of a realistic perception of the challenges the Armed Forces may face in war

[2943] This means that defense capability must be assessed in relation to the forces that may be deployed against our country, which in turn is determined by the course of events and trade-offs that are necessarily very uncertain

[2944] It is not possible to guard against every conceivable eventuality

[2945] Choices must be made

[2946] The worst-case scenario cannot be used as a benchmark for the defense tasks of a small country

[2947] Efforts must be concentrated on areas where they can influence the outcome of a conflict

[2948] It is also necessary to guard against several conceivable situations, as it is not possible to assess the likelihood that any of these will occur

[2949] For a country that is a member of an alliance, it must also be assumed that an adversary cannot focus the bulk of its forces against this country alone, or bet everything on one situation, as this would weaken opportunities elsewhere and increase vulnerability to countermeasures from the Alliance

[2950] It is thus not possible to “calculate” what defense capability is required, and the concept of “relative defense capability” is very difficult to give concrete meaning

[2951] However, a professional and then a political judgment must be exercised regarding the defense capability that should be strived for

[2952] The main task of the Armed Forces - to prevent and, if necessary, repel an attack against our country - will be decisive for the structure of the Armed Forces

[2953] The Armed Forces are also tasked with smaller-scale, or lower-priority, missions

[2954] The structure that is determined must also be able to capture these missions to the extent possible

[2955] The organization, scope and activities of the Armed Forces have remained largely unchanged for several decades

[2956] In the 1980s, rapidly rising costs for both operations and investment became noticeable

[2957] This is expected to continue in the years to come

[2958] At the same time, the economic framework conditions are becoming tighter

[2959] The resource availability will not satisfy all needs

[2960] This requires stricter prioritization of tasks and resource consumption, a critical assessment of the level of ambition for the various activities, and a reassessment of routines and work arrangements

[2961] The structural objective is based on governing assumptions of a security and defense policy nature, and on the economic and personnel framework conditions

[2962] These are determined by the political authorities

[2963] The detailed design of the armed forces' organization, composition and equipment will be based primarily on professional military assessments

[2964] The operational requirements contribute to the basis for the design of the defense structure

[2965] Every area of the country must be defended

[2966] This creates a need for a decentralized organization

[2967] At the same time, the Armed Forces must be able to mobilize effective resources in the most vulnerable areas to achieve the necessary combat capability

[2968] The entire society must be organized with the aim of being able to provide effective support for the defense effort

[2969] We are based on a total defense concept, where one of the fundamental pillars is that civilian society's resources in war should be able to be used to provide overall support for the armed forces

[2970] The conscription system constitutes the second fundamental pillar

[2971] It provides the opportunity to mobilize sufficient forces to establish a defense across our vast country

[2973] Upon mobilization, the number increases to well over 300,000, meaning that it includes slightly over 8% of the country's population

[2976] But a professional defense force will not be able to provide a sufficient numerical basis for the war organization

[2977] With those tasks

[3330] ORGANIZATION, PERSONNEL, TRAINING AND EXERCISES

[3331] The assessment of the Armed Forces' organization is a continuous process

[3332] A main goal in peacetime is to establish organizational and responsibility relationships that can be maintained as much as possible even in times of crisis and war, and to eliminate weaknesses in preparedness during a transition from peace to war

[3333] For the planning period 1989-1993, the Ministry does not see that there will be a significant need to change the main structure of the Armed Forces organization

[3334] However, there will be a need for changes and adaptations to the organization, partly due to changing technology, weapons systems and management styles

[3335] Changes in financial and personnel framework conditions will also lead to organizational changes

[3336] By restructuring the peacetime organization, it should be possible to reduce the manyear consumption by an average of one percent per year

[3337] The level of man-year consumption will be reduced from approximately 27,500 in 1988 to approximately 26,150 in

[3338] or by

[3339] Emphasis will be placed on implementing the closure/restructuring/reduction of activities that are of less importance in terms of preparedness

[3340] The introduction of new equipment may also require organizational changes

[3341] The many organizational restructurings and organizational studies that have been carried out in the Armed Forces over the years have provided a broad base of experience that will be utilized in further work on the organization of the Armed Forces

[3342] In line with the developments taking place in society, the Norwegian Armed Forces will also undergo a decentralization of tasks and a corresponding shift of resources

[3343] This will be implemented in such a way that quality and efficiency are ensured in the primary functions of preparedness and force production

[3344] The emergency response arrangements will be reviewed with the aim of finding cost-effective solutions

[3347] Act no. 230 for 1983-84, point 11.5, on what it considered to be an oversized staff structure in the Armed Forces

[3349] In this regard, the division of labor between the various levels of the organization will be considered

[3350] Restructuring, rationalization and streamlining of the peacetime organization will result in activities being closed down, reduced or relocated

[3744] Length of service The Ministry of Defence assumes that the length of service will be maintained unchanged in the upcoming planning period

[3745] The Army, coastal and air defense artillery formations except the Navy battalion have a 12-month service period, while the other parts of the Navy and Air Force including the Navy battalion have 15 months

[3746] Fair conscription For conscription to be perceived as fair, it is very important that the burdens are fairly distributed

[3747] What is fair, however, often depends on the eyes that see and the standard that is used

[3748] The Armed Forces are a diverse organization that has a myriad of different service tasks with a wide geographical spread and under varying climatic conditions

[3749] Equal service for all consequently becomes an impossibility

[3750] The overall goal will therefore be that all conscripts will receive service conditions that are within the framework of the rules and regulations that have been established, and that the rules safeguard the conscripts' legitimate demands for fair treatment

[3751] For reasons of fairness, it is important that all conscripts are given equal status, and that no one is given special advantages due to education and professional experience acquired before their initial service

[3752] Until now, academic groups (priests, doctors, dentists, etc.) have been able to perform their first service as commanders

[3753] The same applies to a number of others with special training, such as Mates, engineers, etc

[3754] Such a status upgrade is difficult if it cannot be justified by the functional needs of the Armed Forces

[3755] On the other hand, these personnel groups have increasingly been at a disadvantage compared to other conscripts in terms of finances, as they do not benefit from the benefit schemes that apply to regular personnel

[3756] The Armed Forces have regulations that regulate the service load for those subject to conscription

[3757] Nevertheless, working time arrangements for other personnel groups are practiced differently from place to place

[3758] This applies in particular to shift and rotation schemes, which are often perceived to be very unfair

[3759] It is therefore important to find better rules in this area

[3760] A separate working group in the ministry has for some time worked on these and other issues concerning the service conditions of conscripts

[3761] This work will continue

[3762] The goal is to create the greatest possible fairness and equal treatment when performing military service

[3763] The Trusteeship Scheme The TMO has consolidated its position as a valuable and necessary institution in the Armed Forces

[3764] But even a well-established organization requires follow-up, further development and guidance

[3765] Therefore, the Ministry expects that there will be a need for a reassessment and review of the regulations with a view to improvements during the planning period

[3766] The main responsibility for TMO must still lie with the ministry

[3767] The training of trustees will be strengthened

[3768] The same applies to control and follow-up of provisions regarding elections, meeting frequencies at department level, etc

[3769] There is a particular need to assess the officer training academy students' connection to TMO with a view to improving the quality of training on TMO during basic officer training

[3770] The Ministry believes that TMO contributes to strengthening the Armed Forces and rooting it in sound democratic grounds

[3771] It contributes to maintaining the good will to defend Norway

[3772] As a collaborative arrangement, TMO is adapted to the unique nature of the Armed Forces and requires the participation of all parties

[3773] The Armed Forces must be built on cooperation and interaction between all levels of a comprehensive and highly complex organization

[3774] Commanders and privates do not, and must not, stand in any conflict with each other

[3775] They will solve tasks that are so important and demanding that they can only be solved together

[3776] The Ministry therefore views positively the increased attention that the TMO has paid in recent years to issues related to the content of the service, increased efficiency and meaningful utilization of educational time

[3777] Other issues that concern conscripts are the transition to civilian status after completing their service and fairness in the distribution of burdens within the conscript population and in relation to the youth group in general

[3778] Parts of these areas are addressed elsewhere in the report

[3779] On the basis of Section 109 of the Constitution, the Gender Equality Act, and general social developments, conscripts have on several occasions raised the proposal to investigate different models for compulsory community service within or outside the framework of total defense for the entire youth cohort

[3780] The part of the youth cohort that is burdened by conscription experiences this as an additional burden (in terms of finances, education, seniority, loss of professional experience, etc.) compared to groups that, for various reasons, do not serve conscription

[3781] The demands to raise the status of conscription have been raised against this background

[3782] Status" does not primarily refer to financial conditions related to initial service and conscription, but to all measures that raise the conscript's reputation and value in society

[3783] The burden of military service largely falls on those who serve their first term of service and are then called up for mobilization

[3784] Compared to youth in general, this group is disadvantaged in terms of education, professional experience and income opportunities

[3785] It is important to find measures that can offset this difference

[3786] A number of specific measures have been highlighted

[3787] salary seniority in the private sector, improved points systems for admission to higher education, pension points, measures to create awareness among employers and society in general about the importance of conscription and the resource that conscripts represent, etc

[3788] The situation upon graduation

[3789] Considerable efforts have been made to improve the position of conscripts upon discharge during the current planning period

[3790] Among the measures, it can be mentioned that the resources in Adult Education in the Armed Forces have been directed more consciously towards competence and vocational-oriented course offerings to strengthen the individual's opportunities in relation to the labor market and further education after completing initial service

[3791] Cooperation with the labour market agency centrally and locally has been strengthened, and programs for information about the labour market, career guidance and study guidance have been improved

[3792] An independent research institution, commissioned by the Ministry of Defense, has conducted a survey of unemployment among conscripted soldiers upon discharge

[3793] The survey has mapped the extent and duration of unemployment among the leavers, evaluated existing measures and recommended possible new measures

[3794] The report was handed over to the Ministry of Defense in July

[3795] The survey documents the particular problems faced by recently discharged personnel, and that young people who are performing their military service are more vulnerable to unemployment than young people in general

[3796] This applies regardless of the unemployment level in general

[3797] The report confirms that unemployment among discharged soldiers is a social problem that must be taken seriously

[3798] The registered unemployment among soldiers is according to the report

[3799] –10 times higher than general unemployment and 4–5 times higher than registered unemployment among youth

[3800] Dismissal creates an acute employment problem in the first months after completing initial service

[3801] The study shows that the early discharge scheme is an effective measure that alleviates some of the unemployment problems for soldiers

[3802] At the same time, it is clear that early discharge creates emergency preparedness and operational problems for the Armed Forces

[3803] The Ministry has decided that the scheme will be continued, but that certain aspects of its practice will be further assessed

[3804] A significant part of the unemployment problem is created by the lack of correspondence between the start of school and the completion of initial service

[3805] The Ministry will consider whether it is possible to mitigate the problem by changing the call times

[3806] Economic and social conditions of conscripts

[3807] The conscripts, totaling approximately 25,000, represent a significant group of personnel and constitute approximately half of the total number of personnel on permanent duty in the Armed Forces

[3808] However, only 85% and 72% of male youth begin and complete their first military service, respectively

[3809] Against this background, it is natural that finances and well-being are key issues for conscripts

[3810] Economic conditions and other comparisons between those who perform their compulsory service and those who are exempted for various reasons are constantly on the agenda

[3811] The question of whether the current arrangements for financial compensation cover the anticipated needs, and whether they are fair and reasonable in relation to the idea that military service should be as equal a burden for everyone as possible, has been raised from several quarters

[3812] Financial compensation is traditionally regulated based on salary settlements for state employees

[3813] Particular attention is paid to wage developments for low-paid workers in the state

[3814] The compensation system contains some biases

[3815] It is different for the initial service, the refresher training and the HV service

[3816] For example, the initial service provides means-tested housing benefit based on actual housing costs

[3817] Repetition soldiers receive a fixed housing allowance per day regardless of the size of their housing expenses, while HV soldiers receive no housing allowance at all

[3818] This differential treatment seems clearly unreasonable, and leads to negative attitudes towards the Armed Forces and our conscription system

[3819] In the fall of 1987, a committee was appointed with the task of assessing the compensation system for conscripts

[3820] The committee will address all aspects of the current compensation system for crews during initial duty, refresher exercises and HV exercises

[3821] A key question is whether current schemes cover the anticipated needs, and whether the benefits provide reasonable compensation for the burdens and demands that the conscription scheme imposes on the individual

[3822] The Ministry of Defense assumes that it will be appropriate to return to this important issue during the planning period

[3823] The welfare service in the Armed Forces is of great value in personnel care and environmental work at the departments and is a fundamental element in the development of civil-military cultural cooperation locally

[3824] During the current planning period, the welfare service has had certain difficulties in fully carrying out the tasks it has been assigned to perform

[3825] This is partly due to the fact that the Armed Forces have had a strong increase in social and benefit cases, which has reduced the opportunities for conducting general welfare, cultural and environmental work

[4006] Operation and maintenance of equipment

[4007] The need for operating assets to keep the fleet in proper condition is determined by, among other things, the types and quantities of equipment, the condition, age and method of use of the equipment, material consumption and the competence of the maintenance personnel

[4008] Operating expenses include, among other things, the replacement of ammunition, fuel and spare parts that are consumed, so that our emergency stocks are always at a reasonable level

[4009] Furthermore, operating expenses include the replacement of worn-out equipment such as vehicles, communications and engineering equipment, smaller vessels, various types of quartermaster equipment, daily inspections and maintenance

[4010] The size of the operating budget is assessed based on previous experience and planned activity in the period

[4011] Emphasis has been placed on keeping the increase in operating expenses as low as possible, partly in order to increase provisions for investments

[4012] In addition, the funds for operation and maintenance will be used for salaries of employees at the Armed Forces' workshops and to cover expenses for the work carried out by civilian workshops

[4013] Disposal and disposal of materials

[4014] In the coming years, the Armed Forces will receive large amounts of new equipment

[4015] Resupply and maintenance of this equipment will require an increasingly large share of maintenance capacity, while it will become more difficult to obtain spare parts and more expensive to maintain older equipment

[4016] Introducing new equipment in addition to the old also results in an increased need for personnel and storage space

[4017] Due to resource scarcity, disposal will occur on a much larger scale than before

[4018] Equipment that is replaced should normally be discontinued

[4019] If this is not desirable for special reasons, sober analyses of the costs of maintenance, storage requirements, personnel and spare parts during the period in which the equipment is expected to be retained must be presented

[4020] The Armed Forces currently have a branch-specific material management system where the key tasks are handled by the respective supply commands

[4021] The army also has regional supply commands with a smaller staff and with regional warehouses and workshops

[4022] The Air Force has supply group commanders at the main air stations with responsibility for material management within their geographical area

[4023] For the Navy, there is a similar arrangement

[4024] An estimated 85% of the operating funds are used locally, while the remainder is used regionally and centrally

[4025] In following up on the many proposals that emerged during the workshop survey in the Armed Forces, the Ministry will particularly look at the organization and framework conditions for the units that are to centrally handle materiel maintenance, and at the financial management of this activity

[4026] The Ministry will consider the distribution of positions between civilians and military personnel to ensure continuity and good career opportunities for employees at the workshops, including advancement to management positions

[4027] The many proposals that have not yet been implemented include changes to rules and routines, environmental measures, interpersonal relationships, structural and material improvements, etc

[4028] Through specific action plans and prioritized follow-up, the Ministry will ensure that measures are implemented and benefits are reaped as soon as practically possible

[4029] Everything indicates that the review of equipment maintenance that the workshop survey entailed will enable the Armed Forces to maintain the growing and increasingly complex fleet of equipment with significantly lower operational growth than would otherwise be possible

[4030] The increased knowledge of all aspects of material maintenance, material use and material dependency that the survey provided will contribute to this

[4031] The same applies in general to increased cost awareness, recognition that managers should be more involved in material maintenance, and the increased understanding of the importance of and opportunities for changed operating arrangements

[4032] Need for qualified personnel

[4033] Much of the equipment that the Armed Forces receive is technologically very advanced

[4034] In order to act as an expert purchaser of defense equipment and to be able to maintain the equipment in a fully satisfactory manner, there is a need for personnel with high technical expertise

[4035] These are professional groups that are particularly in demand in the civilian market

[4036] This makes it difficult for the Armed Forces to meet its needs

[4037] A separate committee has assessed the situation and proposed a number of measures to recruit and retain qualified personnel

[4038] Work is underway to implement the measures

[4039] Research and development

[4040] As is clear from previous sections, technological developments affect our country's strategic situation, the threat and the design of our defense

[4041] A good understanding of technological development and the longer-term defense consequences is therefore of great importance for the further development of the Armed Forces

[4042] This requires separate research and development activities

[4043] Through such activities, which in a small country cannot cover all areas of technology, if the quality is good enough, we create a basis for good intervention and exchange of information with the far broader research and development activity in leading allied countries

[4044] Our country's size and industrial capacity set clear limits on what kind of defense equipment can be developed and produced domestically

[4045] A large part of our material needs will be covered by procurement from other countries

[4046] But there are also several reasons why we should develop and produce materials ourselves in important sectors

[4047] Foreign industry cannot be expected to take special account of our special climatic and topographical conditions and the fact that our defense is made up of smaller units than in other countries and partly has different needs

[4048] By concentrating our resources, we have over the years produced a number of types of equipment that have provided very useful and economical solutions for the Armed Forces

[4049] This activity has also significantly contributed to the further development and innovation of leading technological industries in our country

[4050] It is a clear national task to maintain the technological environments that exist within Norwegian development and production of defense equipment and to create conditions for the formation of new industries

[4051] High-level national development and production expertise, at least in certain sectors, is also a prerequisite for Norwegian industry to be able to take on international system responsibility in the increasing international cooperation on defence materiel (see Chapter 12.9), and not just assignments as a raw material and component supplier

[4052] The Armed Forces' material procurement and updates are determined based on defense needs and available resources

[4053] Perhaps especially in a small country with limited resources, it is important to find materials with performance, complexity and price so that a good balance between quantity and quality is achieved

[4054] This is a demanding task because modern defense equipment is complex

[4055] It must work under many different conditions and against future threats, and it can rarely be acquired as a ready-made off-the-shelf product

[4056] Decisions about procurement must largely be made before the development work is completed

[4057] In order to find the materiel that provides the best cost-effectiveness ratio, in addition to solid specialist military knowledge, good insight into cutting-edge technological areas and extensive trade-off analyses between competing materiel solutions are often necessary

[4058] The Armed Forces' own research and development capacity is gathered in the Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI), which also plays an important role in the extensive analysis work in connection with the Armed Forces' long-term planning, and in technical investigations and trade-off analyses in connection with major material procurements

[4059] A significant portion of the Armed Forces' development work is outsourced to industry under contract from one of the supply commands, from FFI or in collaboration between a supply command and FFI

[4060] Because our bodies are small by international standards, development work can be organized with simple and direct lines between the parties and thus carried out at lower costs

[4061] The scope and focus of research and development activities in the Armed Forces must be adapted to both technological developments and the defense challenges that result from this, as well as our future material needs

[4062] In the period up to the turn of the century, the Armed Forces will face an increasing need to carry out large and important material projects

[4063] This indicates a certain increase in our total effort

[4064] Successful implementation of development and production projects in the years ahead requires that all parties involved, including the Armed Forces, development agencies and industry, feel responsible for using modern technology to provide cost-effective defense equipment rather than opting for the most sophisticated technological solutions

[4065] Procurement policy and Norwegian industry

[4066] In the upcoming planning period, the Ministry of Defence will continue to develop contacts with Norwegian industry to increase the industry's opportunities for deliveries to the Armed Forces from its own production, or in collaboration with foreign suppliers

[4067] In order to increase Norwegian industry's share of defense deliveries, the system for industry's access to the Armed Forces' future materiel plans must be further developed

[4068] Furthermore, the defense authorities must place greater emphasis on early identification of industry that has realistic opportunities for constructive engagement in the project

[4069] Depending on the nature of the new material and the industry's qualifications and prerequisites, the engagement may be in the nature of independent development and production, development in collaboration with FFI with subsequent production, or production only

[4070] Projects in areas where industry has little experience and which involve significant industrial expertise often result in cost uncertainty and increased costs for the Armed Forces

[4071] The costs of development contracts in such areas should be shared between the company and the authorities

[4072] Norwegian industry's opportunities should also be strengthened through increased participation in multinational materiel projects that will lead to materiel that satisfies Norwegian operational needs and cost limits

[4073] To improve conditions, the Ministry has entered into framework agreements (so-called Memorandum of Understanding - MOU) with a number of countries

[4074] This aspect of international cooperation is discussed further in the next section on International materiel cooperation

[4075] To utilize the Armed Forces' purchases of equipment in other countries to create employment and further develop Norwegian industry, buyback agreements are used

[4076] Such agreements have been entered into on a relatively large scale

[4077] The value of the contracts has varied from NOK 20-30 million to NOK 2-3 billion

[4078] Experience suggests that in the future, greater emphasis should be placed on including in the agreements technological products that can contribute to further developing and increasing our industry's international competitiveness

[4079] The possibilities will vary from project to project

[4080] Aircraft, vessels and equipment for land defense offer various opportunities, and one can usually achieve more in both volume and quality when a large industrial group is the counterparty than if it is a smaller company with a limited product spectrum

[4081] In collaboration with industry, a number of areas should be selected that will provide us with opportunities for the above-mentioned industrial or further development and where we have realistic opportunities to make a difference in international cooperation

[4082] In negotiations about material procurement and repurchases, our representatives must show the flexible firmness needed so that the repurchase agreements can also contribute to the desired industrial development

[4083] As discussed in section

[4084] we will be dependent on acquiring a significant portion of our defense equipment from other countries

[4085] This also applies to an increasing extent to other and larger countries

[4086] For understandable reasons, many larger countries want to be as self-sufficient as possible in defense equipment, and to utilize the cutting-edge expertise and activity that the development and production of defense equipment provides for their own industrial development

[4087] However, the cost development for defense equipment has been so great that these countries are also increasingly trying to establish cooperation across borders to increase production series sizes and reduce unit prices

[4088] Another reason for efforts for increased material cooperation, especially in Europe, is the Americans' long-standing dominant position in the development and production of advanced and large defense systems

[4089] Individually, even the larger European countries cannot develop new technology to the same depth and breadth as the Americans, and they do not have nearly as large defense needs of their own

[4090] But with better utilization of the combined development and production resources in joint materiel projects where several countries are purchasers of the materiel, it is possible to create a far better balance

[4091] A third factor is the need to strengthen the Alliance's conventional defenses

[4092] The primary goal on the military side is interoperability and increased standardization across national borders

[4093] Joint material projects between several countries will contribute to this goal

[4094] Furthermore, it should lead to cheaper defense equipment in both procurement and operation, thereby contributing to more defense for available resources

[4095] Within NATO, work has been underway on these difficult problems for many years

[4096] A strategy for coordinated material planning has now been adopted at ministerial level, which will contribute to the initiation of several specific collaborative projects

[4097] One aspect of this strategy focuses specifically on new technology and the possibilities of exploiting it to give the West a qualitative advantage in the conventional field

[4098] Within the IEPG - which consists of the 13 European NATO countries - concrete measures have been implemented, following an initiative from the defense ministers, to increase the number of multinational materiel projects and, as a new measure ahead of materiel projects, joint projects for the development and maturation of new technology for later exploitation

[4099] At the first ministerial meeting within the IEPG in 1984, it was decided to conduct a thorough study of the European defense industry with a view to strengthening it

[4100] The starting point was the problems of unnecessary use of resources in the form of duplicate development, lack of standardization and interoperability within Western Europe, and a desire for a stronger technological/industrial position vis-à-vis the United States

[4101] The study concludes that a reorganization of the defense industry into stronger units across national borders would have several benefits

[4102] It will be easier to obtain standardized products, it will be easier to operate in collaboration with American industry on advanced projects, and it will be easier to gain a foothold with Western European products in the United States and other countries

[4103] Jobs in the defense industry will thereby become more stable

[4104] Traditionally, nations have opposed any form of supranationalism when it comes to security and defense

[4105] Both to protect their own defense industry and to secure jobs, individual nations have largely acquired defense equipment from their own industry

[4106] For its part, the industry considers defense technology to be an essential factor in its own general further development and is afraid to share its knowledge with others for competitive reasons

[4107] Although a number of joint material projects have been successfully implemented, progress has not been that great

[4108] In several of the projects that have been completed, the cost reductions that were expected have not been achieved

[4109] The reasons for this are partly that multinational materiel projects have tended to be very heavily driven by both government and industry

[4110] There is still much to learn regarding effective organization and division of labor in such projects

[4111] Part of the reason is that it has proven difficult to agree on rational operational requirements for the new equipment

[4112] To some extent, the operational requirements for materiel in joint projects have become the sum of the requirements of the individual participating countries

[4113] This has led to unnecessarily expensive materials

[4114] Norway supports and actively participates on both government and industry levels in efforts within NATO and the IEPG to increase materiel cooperation

[4115] As more rational forms are developed on both the government, defense and industry sides, cooperation will lead to better utilization of resources and more defense of the funds made available

[4116] Cooperation on defense equipment will also help Norwegian industry find its place in the growing European industrial cooperation and allow the Norwegian defense industry to benefit from larger series

[4117] However, cooperation on defense equipment with countries that are significantly larger than ours involves problems that must be resolved

[4118] The larger and more resource-rich countries enter the projects with a heavier development and production apparatus

[4119] They will be the purchasers of a larger proportion of the produced material and will often be responsible for project management and all technically and systemically more demanding and developmental tasks

[4120] Smaller countries often become subcontractors of relatively simple, routine components

[4121] This would not benefit our country and Norwegian industry, even if it would lead to cheaper defense equipment

[4122] To maintain our place as an advanced industrial nation, albeit in limited technological areas, it is important that we concentrate in our material cooperation on projects and technological areas where we have realistic opportunities to play a significant role

[4123] Furthermore, it is important that we take on responsibility for more demanding tasks that can provide our industry with a basis for further technological development and experience in industrial collaboration, also when it comes to the design and management of larger projects

[4124] One factor that must also be given importance in cooperation on the production of defense equipment is the export regulations in the individual countries

[4125] Different rules may in certain cases limit the possibilities for joint production

[4126] This is a cost that countries like Norway must be prepared to bear in order to pursue a responsible and consistent policy for the export of defense equipment
