[4400] DEFENSE

[4401] AND CIVIL SOCIETY IN INSTITUTION

[4402] S. No. 230 for 1983-84 pt

[4403] On 11.6.4, the Defence Committee expressed a number of views on the relationship between the Defence Forces and civil society

[4404] The Government builds on these views in the following

[4405] The activities of the Armed Forces will primarily be concentrated on managing the resources made available by society in accordance with the defense policy goals that the Storting has endorsed

[4406] The defense appropriations will therefore be used primarily with a view to maintaining a strong national defense that contributes to preventing war, and to protecting our freedom of action and ability to assert Norwegian rights and interests

[4407] The Government believes that in peacetime, the Armed Forces should perform or support civilian tasks where this is natural and can be combined with the Armed Forces' activities

[4408] Furthermore, the Government considers it natural that the Armed Forces continue to provide support in connection with disasters, major accidents and major national events

[4409] Traditionally, the Armed Forces provide grants to civilian organizations that work actively to support and disseminate knowledge about the Armed Forces' activities or that otherwise contribute to strengthening the country's defense will and capability

[4410] At the local level, there are also a number of collaborative projects between the Armed Forces and civil society, which mainly concern support for cultural cooperation, sports facilities, community centers, joint development of roads, shooting ranges and measures to integrate conscripts into local community life

[4411] The most important and most extensive impacts on society, however, come as a result of the Armed Forces' ordinary activities

[4412] To carry out its main tasks, the Armed Forces are dependent on civil society services and assistance in terms of manpower, materiel, buildings, facilities, maintenance services, etc

[4413] This means that a large portion of the funds that the Armed Forces receive are returned to civil society through salaries to employees and purchases of goods and services

[4414] As the Armed Forces' branches are spread over large parts of the country, this has a regional political effect with positive effects for a number of municipalities, companies and individuals

[4415] When designing the Armed Forces' activities, it is therefore reasonable to take certain regional, industrial, and employment policy considerations into account, but military priorities will always have to weigh most heavily

[4416] The Norwegian Armed Forces are one of the country's largest employers with approximately 25,000 employees, nearly half of whom are recruited from the local civilian labor market, and nearly 25,000 conscripts

[4417] The business is often located in areas with a modest economic base

[4418] The military therefore plays an important role in regional economic development

[4419] Through its jobs, the armed forces contribute to a stable tax base for a number of municipalities

[4420] This in turn means that municipalities can, among other things, maintain a level of education and service that they would otherwise likely find difficult

[4421] Furthermore, the Armed Forces' permanent personnel and those subject to conscription use a significant portion of their disposable income to demand goods and services on the local market

[4422] This contributes to increased activity and securing the economic base and settlement in some disadvantaged areas of the country

[4423] As a result of the geographical prioritization of the Armed Forces' activities, this is primarily evident in Northern Norway

[4424] A typical example is Indre Troms, where the Armed Forces have had significant operations for 30-35 years

[4425] When it comes to the Armed Forces' own procurement of goods and services, from a preparedness perspective it is important to have a varied business sector, also in Northern Norway

[4426] It will therefore be in the Armed Forces' interest to contribute to strengthening the business community in Northern Norway to the greatest extent possible through procurement at the local level

[4427] An example of this is that spare parts, food, office supplies, maintenance, etc. will be sought from local retailers

[4428] However, the military is more dependent than ever on keeping operating expenses down

[4429] Local procurement must therefore not compromise sound financial operations

[4430] Vessel maintenance will be carried out at a regional level as far as possible

[4431] This means that maintenance takes place close to the areas where the vessels operate

[4432] Coast guard vessels, landing craft and minelayers are maintained in Northern Norway

[4433] Maintenance of equipment that has previously been carried out abroad will, where possible and economically justifiable, be sought to be carried out in Norway

[4434] When it comes to the actual procurement of materials, a large part of this still takes place abroad

[4435] However, there are significant national industrial and employment policy opportunities associated with these procurements

[4436] There has long been active work to develop Norwegian industry's involvement in this area, both from political authorities and industry bodies

[4437] The acquisition of the F-16 aircraft and the SIDEWINDER air-to-air missile system has added value to Norwegian industry over the past decade

[4438] technological expertise and significant assignments in the form of sub-production

[4439] Negotiations are underway regarding Norwegian participation in the research, development and production of next-generation air-to-air missile systems (ASRAAM/AMRAAM

[4440] In the years to come, this project will be of great importance for maintaining and further developing the high-tech environment in parts of Norwegian industry

[4441] Where it is not possible or appropriate for direct Norwegian participation in the production of equipment purchased abroad, so-called buyback agreements are often entered into

[4442] From 1984 to 1987, contracts worth over NOK 4,300 million were entered into in connection with 24 repurchase agreements

[4443] The value of the repurchase agreements is approximately NOK 3,000 million

[4444] In the upcoming planning period, the government will continue its work to expand contacts with Norwegian industry, especially with a view to providing the industry with high-tech expertise

[4445] For further details regarding this, please refer to the section on procurement policy - Norwegian industry

[4446] To ensure material maintenance, accommodate and care for crews, expand and improve combat and defensive positions, etc., large construction and civil engineering investments are required annually

[4447] In addition to national funds, Norway also receives significant amounts through NATO's infrastructure programs

[4448] This greatly benefits districts with a weak and one-sided economic base

[4449] The activity created in the local community is not limited to just the construction phase

[4450] The military's large and partly obsolete building stock requires extensive maintenance that provides the local community with permanent jobs

[4451] Some of the Armed Forces' facilities also benefit civil society in other ways

[4452] Practically all military airports, which are also funded through NATO infrastructure programs, are open to civil aviation

[4453] Similar civilian use of military installations also applies within the telecommunications area

[4454] The Armed Forces' educational activities are another area with significant bonus effects for civil society

[4455] Through initial service, several thousand conscripts receive annual training in many different subjects and disciplines that benefit society and the individual after completing their initial service

[4456] This applies to both the training provided in daily service and the adult education courses during free time

[4457] The Armed Forces' schools and courses have been established to train operational and administrative leaders and technical commanders for the various service fields

[4458] But this training also provides good skills for a number of functions in civilian working life

[4459] This is not least reflected in the great demand for military-trained personnel in the civilian labor market

[4460] Personnel with management training, pilot training, technical-mercantile and IT education are particularly sought after

[4461] To the extent that there is a reasonable balance between the entry and exit of officers at the various grade levels, it must be seen as an advantage that well-trained military personnel also transition to civilian activities

[4462] This is valuable for society as a whole

[4463] It contributes to mutual understanding between military and civilian activities and to spreading knowledge about the Armed Forces

[4464] OF THE GOVERNMENT'S RENEWAL PROGRAM

[4465] RATIONALIZATION 15.1 The Government's Renewal Program

[4466] Implementation of the Government's renewal program in the Armed Forces will primarily focus on the following areas of focus: - targeted use of information technology - financial management and results orientation - personnel policy and management development

[4467] A steering group has been established consisting of representatives from the Ministry of Defence, the Defence Rationalisation Service and the Defence High Command

[4468] The steering group will lead and coordinate the Ministry of Defence's work on the implementation of the renewal program in the Armed Forces

[4469] An action plan that is structured point by point for each of the main areas above will highlight the status, progress plans, time horizons and cost estimates for the various measures that are expected to be implemented

[4470] A separate working group has been established to implement the renewal program with a view to modernizing the internal operations of the Ministry of Defence. The goal of introducing new information technology is to streamline the Armed Forces' operations in war and peace

[4471] This shall be achieved by creating conditions for increased, appropriate use of EDB, particularly at the local level in the organization, including by - utilizing the organization and size of the Armed Forces for common computer systems that provide sufficient innovation and that contribute to economically advantageous solutions - establishing clear responsibilities and authority with regard to overall management, professional activities, procurement activities and functional responsibility for the application - implementing appropriate standards for hardware and software equipment - establishing norms for economic assessments of EDB use - creating conditions for simpler and faster exchange of data and services by establishing distributed EDB systems - creating conditions for greater collaboration on the development of common user systems - increasing training opportunities for personnel at all levels **15.1.2 Financial management and results orientation** Greater emphasis will be placed in the Armed Forces on goals and results than on detailed management through budget items

[4472] This reorientation will include - active follow-up of the opportunities for increased freedom that the budget reform of 1986 provides - that all levels of the Armed Forces will be given clearer signals about which goals are being aimed at, and that stronger requirements will be placed on documentation of the results achieved

[4473] The Ministry of Defense has initiated several measures to implement budget reform in the Armed Forces

[4474] The main intentions behind the budget reform are that the results of individual government activities should come into greater focus and that the overall management of the activities should take place through the setting of goals and resource frameworks, as well as performance monitoring

[4475] The Armed Forces' units will be given increased freedom in the disposal of allocated funds, while greater responsibility will be assigned to the individual organization in planning the utilization of resources

[4476] By preparing business plans in which the goals for the activities are described, it will become clear which tasks must be carried/prioritized to achieve the goals

[4477] In this way, more efficient use of resources and productivity growth will be sought

[4478] The main elements of the budget reform in the state are management by objectives using targeted business plans with subsequent performance monitoring

[4479] The Norwegian Armed Forces, with its extensive structure and relatively centralized system, are facing quite extensive restructuring in order to implement results-oriented performance management of their operations

[4480] In order to achieve the goals of increased political control of the Armed Forces' activities and productivity growth through more efficient resource consumption and greater local freedom of action, an action plan has been prepared for the implementation of the budget reform in the Armed Forces

[4481] The action plan is expected to be implemented gradually and without the establishment of a separate project organization to manage the reform

[4482] It is planned to implement pilot projects at various selected units in the Armed Forces to test key elements of the budget reform within the Armed Forces' most important areas

[4483] The budget reform effort will necessitate changes to the financial management function in the Armed Forces

[4484] In this context, greater emphasis will need to be placed on the introduction of new technology, such as computer-based budget control systems

[4485] As part of the budget reform work, measures have already been taken to restructure the budget routines in the Armed Forces

[4486] Extensive restructuring of the budget proposal will be carried out so that this document can become both a central political management tool and a better source of information

[4487] This work will continue during the planning period

[4488] In addition, the budget proposals prepared in the Armed Forces' agencies should be more strategically designed, stating goals for the activities and describing the results achieved

[4489] The introduction of business planning with the preparation of target structures for each business will be central to this work

[4490] Greater local freedom of action in the Armed Forces is a prerequisite for practicing management by objectives and business planning

[4491] To qualify the units to carry out the reform work, efforts will be made to train personnel, acquire and train suitable control and information systems, and undertake extensive work to introduce new budget and financial management routines

[4492] Implementation of the budget reform in the Armed Forces will take place gradually and in line with the organization's ability to absorb and utilize the new management system in a satisfactory manner. The leadership concept in the Armed Forces has been taken up for assessment in connection with the follow-up of measures following the avalanche accident in Vassdalen on March

[4493] No. 68 (1986-87) on the accident, which was presented on 5 June 1987 and discussed in the Storting on 29 February 1988, states, among other things, that factors related to leadership and organizational structure may have influenced the course of events prior to the accident

[4494] This was particularly addressed by organizational researchers from the University of Bergen in a consultation statement to the investigation commission's report (NOU 1986:20 issued on 7 July

[4495] The researchers pointed out, among other things, that there was a mismatch between how the organization is expected to function and how the leaders are expected to behave, and what actually happened as expressed through the investigation commission's description of the accident

[4496] The Armed Forces have initiated a number of measures to evaluate and improve their leadership

[4497] In the Ministry's opinion, the spotlight must be focused on the leadership forms in the Armed Forces, as these must be adapted to both developments in society and the constant demands imposed by the Armed Forces' special tasks

[4498] Well-being and performance depend on good leadership at all levels

[4499] Good leadership will unleash creativity and commitment throughout the Armed Forces

[4500] Leadership work will receive increased attention during the planning period and organizations will be actively involved in the work

[4501] As part of the work, the ministry has engaged researchers at the Department of Administration and Organizational Sciences at the University of Bergen in a larger project to investigate leadership and organizational conditions in the Armed Forces

[4502] The project spans 3 years and is part of the so-called LOS research program (Leadership, Organization and Governance

[4503] As is well known, LOS research has been designated as one of the main areas of focus in Norwegian research and the work is coordinated by the Norwegian Council for Applied Social Research (NORAS

[4504] To follow up on this research work, as well as measures that the defense branches themselves have initiated, a coordination council has been appointed in the ministry with representation from the Armed Forces High Command and the Institute of Administration and Organizational Sciences

[4505] At the conclusion of the project in 1989, the Council will present its recommendations regarding any changes to the Armed Forces' leadership concept based on the material that has emerged

[4506] The military duty of obedience and the conditions for refusing to carry out orders were addressed in the St.meld

[4507] No. 68 and commented on during the consideration thereof

[4508] The Armed Forces generally cannot allow personnel to develop a relaxed attitude towards the requirement of obedience, and the criteria for refusing to carry out orders must therefore be strict

[4509] The Advocate General has discussed the duty of obedience in an opinion, where the starting point is that only lawful orders are subject to obedience

[4510] When obviously incorrect orders are given, or local circumstances indicate that they should not be followed because life and health may be at stake, it is the duty of every commander to prevent the orders from being carried out

[4511] Such an action cannot be considered a refusal to comply with an order

[4512] However, it must be acknowledged that the military duty of obedience and the conditions for refusing to carry out orders is an area full of gray areas

[4513] It can be difficult to determine when a situation is so dangerous that a given order must be deviated from

[4514] It is therefore important that the Armed Forces train its personnel to take the responsibility inherent in such decisions. Simplification of rules is an important part of the efficiency improvement work in the Armed Forces

[4515] The overall goal is to have a regulatory framework in the Armed Forces that is at all times best adapted to current and future needs and requirements

[4516] More specifically, the goal is - to have rules that are no longer needed removed from force - to have rules that are simple, easy to understand and possible to comply with - to establish purposeful and framework-like regulations to achieve, among other things, the intention of management by objectives (instead of rule management), decentralization, greater local freedom of action, and the removal of unnecessary double processing - to look at routines for rule production and adapt these goals in the Government's renewal program

[4517] In the regulatory simplification work in the Armed Forces, measures will be initiated both centrally and locally during the planning period

[4518] The central measures will address specific areas/overarching systems, while local measures will be aimed at regulatory simplification in general

[4519] It is assumed that regulatory simplification will also be carried out on one's own initiative, both locally and centrally

[4520] Productivity growth Productivity refers to the relationship between the product that is produced and the consumption of resources to make the product

[4521] Efforts to achieve increased productivity will be carried out in line with the Government's public administration renewal program

[4522] Productivity growth in the Armed Forces must be related to defense capability, which is the product that the Armed Forces produce

[4523] Productivity growth will therefore be the result of measures that make it possible to increase or maintain defense capability with the same or less resource use

[4524] In order to achieve the desired productivity growth in the Armed Forces of one to two percent per year, measures will be initiated during the planning period that will include

[4525] reorganizations - better coordination and organization of activities - reduction and closure of activities that contribute least to maintaining defense capabilities - delegation of authority to simplify case processing and stimulate greater effort - better economization of resources - productivity-enhancing investments in new technology - simplification of regulations

[4526] By means of such productivity-enhancing measures as listed above, the goal is to increase productivity growth per year by one to two percent of the defense budget

[4527] All budgeting units in the Armed Forces must create annual results-oriented business plans

[4528] Before the start of a year, a unit should outline the work goals it will achieve during the year and what resources are expected to be used to achieve these work goals

[4529] During the year, achieved goals and resources used to achieve the goals are recorded

[4530] At the end of the year, deviations between what was planned and what was realized are assessed

[4531] This is again the basis for setting new goals

[4532] An important prerequisite for getting the full benefit of business planning is that the unit is given the necessary freedom of action within the operating budget and regulations

[4533] Such business plans shall be prepared during 1990 for all units

[4534] The business plans will be a tool for measuring productivity growth at the individual unit

[4535] The business plans will include both goals to increase the value of the product and goals to reduce resource consumption

[4536] Savings targets will therefore be included as part of the productivity work and the business plan

[4537] It will be difficult to measure total productivity growth in the Armed Forces, but certain indications can be given

[4538] However, savings targets will be set for the total activities of the Armed Forces

[4539] The savings targets per year in personnel and other resources will be quantified in the annual budgets

[4540] These savings targets should be achieved both as part of the activities of the individual unit and through significant project rationalization

[4541] The measures involved will be explained elsewhere in the report

[4542] Reference is made in particular to chap

[4543] on the Armed Forces' structural objectives, chap

[4544] on Organization, personnel, education and exercises and section 16.3 on main points in the efficiency improvement work

[4545] The Ministry will carry out pilot projects to test the impact of these reforms

[4546] These projects will be planned in 1988 and implemented in 1989 at individual units

[4547] Savings** The Chief of Defence's directive for rationalisation and efficiency, cf. section 15.3.2, requires that each department prepare a plan for efficiency measures for the individual year

[4548] This plan can be seen as part of the business plan

[4549] The efficiency improvement plan must include specific savings targets related to the measures to be implemented in the year in question

[4550] It is assumed that operational savings can be used for investment purposes or for higher priority operational goals, similar to the schemes that have already been established for certain management companies in the state

[4551] Salary expenses and other personnel-related expenses constitute the largest share of the operating budget

[4552] In a cost-saving process, personnel cannot be exempted

[4553] However, it may also be profitable to increase personnel levels, for example in areas where in-house work is significantly cheaper than outsourced work, when restructuring the organization and to maintain a reasonable standard in professional environments

[4554] It is the overall economy that should guide the measures

[4555] A significant amount of investment must be made in the implementation of the measures, especially on the building side

[4556] Experience from recent years shows that the investments for most measures can be earned over less than five years

[4557] However, it will take a few years before the intended personnel savings and the full effect of the new arrangements are achieved

[4558] The Ministry of Defense has considered various measures and savings opportunities and has consulted with other agencies and other countries' defense forces

[4559] The goals set seem realistic, but require strong effort and management

[4560] However, the changes are a prerequisite for us to be able to maintain an effective defense with the assumed access to resources

[4561] The various operational growth factors must be kept under control and the ability to restructure and wind down lower-priority activities must be strengthened

[4562] Based on this, the annual savings targets are set at one percent of the gross budget

[4563] To achieve this goal, among other things, personnel use must be reduced by an average of approximately 275 man-years per year or, accumulated over the five-year period, by just over 4,000 man-years. The measures that must be implemented to create the productivity growth necessary to achieve the goal of maintaining defense capability will be expressed in specific action plans within the Armed Forces' system for long-term planning

[4564] The specific measures will be reflected in the annual budget proposals to the Storting. **15.2.4 Productivity work as part of daily operations** It is important that improvement measures are developed continuously in line with needs and opportunities

[4565] The Armed Forces will build on the good experiences from such activities in the Armed Forces

[4566] Very extensive efficiency improvement work is carried out annually at departments, specialist authorities, and central staffs and institutions

[4567] The measures described above will further strengthen the work

[4568] Experience from the productivity program in workshop operations shows that many measures depend on additional resources being made available to the unit in question

[4569] This applies partly to equipment procurement, but to a greater extent to implementing measures on the construction and civil engineering side

[4570] The Ministry of Defense will ensure that the necessary funds are allocated so that such measures can be implemented quickly

[4571] In any large and complex organization, there will always be a need for innovation and room for efficiency improvements

[4572] The military is no exception

[4573] There is also a tendency in such large organizations to stiffen in familiar forms and to resist new operating methods and routines

[4574] The Armed Forces are no exception here either

[4575] The military uses large amounts of public funds

[4576] This requires a great emphasis on economization, on getting the most “defense” out of the resources society makes available

[4577] Society also imposes on young men service in the defense of the country

[4578] Military service obliges us to make the service as efficient as possible

[4579] The defense of our country is a fundamental societal task

[4580] Those assigned to safeguard it are obliged to do so in a way that makes optimal use of resources

[4581] The credibility of the Armed Forces, both internally and externally, depends on a good reputation for high productivity

[4582] Productivity in the Armed Forces requires commitment and shared responsibility at all levels of the organization

[4583] It cannot be secured by orders and central decisions

[4584] It requires an organization with good two-way communication

[4585] Consequently, great emphasis will be placed on involving employees in the work of improving efficiency in the Armed Forces

[4586] A program will be prepared that requires meetings to be held at all service locations and pilot schemes to be initiated with measures aimed at increasing efficiency

[4587] Organizations must be given an important role in this work

[4588] To ensure effective interaction and cooperation on productivity work, the Ministry of Defence, in collaboration with the Armed Forces High Command and the organisations, aims to carry out a series of assessments of specific issues regarding the efficiency of the Armed Forces' organisation and operational methods

[4589] The productivity growth aimed for in the period assumes reduced growth in operating expenses compared to previous years

[4590] This cannot be achieved without significant changes to the operations and organization of the Armed Forces

[4591] The Ministry has no doubt that such changes are possible and necessary

[4592] However, they require extensive commitment throughout the Armed Forces

[4593] The Ministry of Defense will prepare for this

[4594] General** The Ministry will outline several goals, methods and guidelines for the rationalization work below

[4595] For the Armed Forces, it is of essential importance to keep the growth in the operating budget within a set target and that the rationalization work contributes to achieving this target

[4596] Rationalization could help create a necessary renewal process

[4597] The Ministry considers it essential to accelerate this process

[4598] The change process has so far proceeded late in the Armed Forces' extensive organization, and it is often difficult to implement the measures required to realize the savings opportunities

[4599] Changed management form Stronger management by objectives in the Armed Forces' activities involves significant restructuring of current systems

[4600] The central authorities must provide a greater degree of framework and goals for the activities and handle individual cases to a lesser extent

[4601] Extensive delegation of authority becomes necessary

[4602] Management by objectives also means that there must be greater alignment within the organization between clients and resource allocators

[4603] These principles deviate somewhat from current practice, but are in line with the intentions of the Government's renewal program

[4604] The principles require some changes in budget procedures and some adjustments in the central organization

[4605] The supply commands will have to settle their services to a greater extent

[4606] For a changed form of governance to have the necessary effect, there must also be a real change in attitude through training and practical performance of the service

[4607] Changes in the framework conditions could provide better motivation

[4608] In this regard, it is crucial that the departments themselves have control over some of the savings so that they can invest the funds where they are needed most

[4609] The Chief of Defence's directive for efficiency and rationalisation, which was issued in 1987, is based on this assumption

[4610] It is also crucial that the management style practiced at all levels motivates employees to actively participate in change processes

[4611] The changed form of governance is intended to make the Armed Forces more adaptable to new situations

[4612] Changed organization** The Ministry aims to ensure that the Armed Forces conduct continuous organizational development

[4613] This development requires, among other things, that the organization be changed so that it can have a more results-oriented business form

[4614] More flexible organizational forms will also be important

[4615] The aim is therefore to counteract excessive fragmentation in the organization, and the Ministry of Defence will reduce the number of departments and offices in the internal organization

[4616] The Ministry's resource-intensive organization will thus become more results-oriented

[4617] Decentralization of tasks and delegation of authority will also entail organizational changes in the Armed Forces

[4618] The capacity for planning and directive-giving must be increased at the expense of case processing

[4619] Self-rationalization** In 1987, the Chief of Defence issued directives on how efficiency and simplification work should be practiced at all Defence units

[4620] Extensive self-rationalization is necessary to achieve the goals set

[4621] Decentralized, local rationalization activities are nothing new

[4622] The new feature is that self-rationalization will become more systematic and comprehensive, that the framework conditions will be changed to promote development, and that the results achieved will benefit the units more directly

[4623] Being able to use some of what you save for prioritized initiatives in your own department is an important motivational factor and source of attitude change

[4624] Self-rationalization means that the individual unit clarifies the goals, the prioritization between them, and actively measures results and resource consumption

[4625] Budgeting and accounting follow-up become important in this context

[4626] In the coming years, more emphasis will be placed on training in efficiency and management at the Armed Forces' schools and courses

[4627] The training will include, among other things, principles of management by objectives

[4628] There will also be other ways to emphasize working on attitudes towards rationalization

[4629] Seeing change as a positive challenge rather than a threat is one of the most important factors in improving productivity. **15.3.5 Project areas for the years 1989-93** The administration and professional bodies are continuously working to streamline operations within their areas of responsibility

[4630] In the following, the Ministry will discuss certain areas where it will particularly focus on rationalization efforts

[4631] The areas that have been selected are either functions that are of great importance or are costly

[4632] What they have in common is that it will be possible to achieve, in some cases, significant productivity growth

[4633] The Armed Forces' Force Production** Expenditure on force production constitutes approximately 80 percent of the total operating budget

[4634] If the Armed Forces are to achieve the goal of limiting the growth in operating expenses, savings must be achieved within the force production sector

[4635] General measures have now been implemented that provide incentives for greater cost awareness and sobriety in resource consumption

[4636] An example of this is greater economic freedom for the force-producing units

[4637] The idea generation competence at the individual unit shall be utilized so that the path between idea, decision and implementation is as short as possible. Personnel management systems Personnel management includes a number of vital key functions that directly affect the personnel's position, working conditions, productivity, welfare, well-being, etc

[4638] For some of these key functions, there has been a registered need for adjustments and adaptations that affect the individual employee

[4639] This field requires broad commitment from within the Armed Forces, from the employees themselves, personnel organizations, and collaboration with civilian and public research environments and universities

[4640] Materiel maintenance** In the years 1985-1987, the Armed Forces carried out a comprehensive and thorough productivity analysis of the workshop operations in the Armed Forces, with the involvement of a civilian consulting firm as project manager

[4641] The purpose was to achieve better planning and management of materiel maintenance and to implement measures that would increase productivity and improve defense capabilities

[4642] Through the involvement of approximately 1,500 people from the Armed Forces and around 20 consultants, a total of approximately 8,000 ideas emerged that were coordinated into approximately 2,000 proposals

[4643] Of these, approximately 40 percent have been completed or are under implementation

[4644] Approximately 10 percent of the proposals have been rejected, while approximately 1,000 proposals are still being processed by regional and central agencies in the Armed Forces

[4645] The Ministry, in consultation with the Armed Forces High Command and the supply commands, will ensure that as many of these proposals as possible are implemented as soon as is practically possible

[4646] The consulting firm has estimated the total savings potential of the aforementioned proposals at NOK 350 million

[4647] It is realistic to believe that we will be able to recover approximately 50 percent of this

[4648] These are annual amounts, where the accumulation effect will increase as measures are implemented

[4649] The experiences that the project provided with regard to, among other things, work methodology and co-influence through broad involvement of employees in an idea creation process, have been established as a permanent arrangement through directives for rationalization and efficiency

[4650] Building operation and maintenance A study with participants from the central, regional and local levels, all branches of defense and the Armed Forces Building Service will include

[4651] systems for planning and management

[4652] resource utilization - possible operational reductions, including in the cleaning and heating sectors **15.3.5.5 Catering services** A study shall shed light on - the possibilities for stronger coordination/integration of catering functions locally and regionally, also across branches of defense - alternative forms of catering (cash catering, canteen operations, etc.) - personnel needs/resource use

[4653] The study will be conducted with the involvement of the Armed Forces Quartermaster Board, the administrations, users, personnel organizations and the National Association for Nutrition and Health

[4654] Experience from the Swedish Defence will be taken into account. **15.3.5.6 Transport Service** The Defence spends significant amounts annually on the transport of personnel and materiel

[4655] In particular, travel expenses for conscripts are showing a sharp increase

[4656] In a study, the Ministry wishes to look more closely at the possibilities for, among other things: - limiting the scope of transport/travel for both personnel and material - coordinating transport activities for units within limited geographical areas - more economical utilization of available means of transport For this study, the professional expertise within the individual branches of defense will be utilized together with civilian expertise, but coordinated and managed in a holistic defense perspective

[4657] DEFENCE'S LONG-TERM PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE MAIN GUIDELINES

[4658] FOR DEFENSE ACTIVITIES

[4659] DURING THE PERIOD 1989-93 16.1 Main problems in the Armed Forces' long-term planning

[4660] This report outlines the main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities in the five-year period

[4661] In a planning context, this is a short period for such a large and complex organization as the Armed Forces

[4662] The planning activity within the Armed Forces therefore has a significantly longer perspective

[4663] Over a long period of time, the Armed Forces have worked based on long-term strength goals and development plans that have been higher than has been economically feasible to realize

[4664] The problem has been exacerbated over time

[4665] It is now no longer possible to push it forward

[4666] The organization and activities of the Armed Forces on the one hand must be brought into balance with the availability of resources on the other

[4667] In light of the economic outlook for the upcoming five-year period, it is very important that the imbalance is not carried forward

[4668] The Norwegian Armed Forces' equipment and defense facilities are of such a scale that even if approximately 35 percent of the defense budget is spent annually on such purposes, significant structural or geographical changes will necessarily take many years

[4669] After any decisions have been made to reduce or terminate the Armed Forces' activities within a sector, it may in practice take several years to reduce personnel levels so that any closures have a significant impact in terms of freeing up necessary resources for the remaining defence

[4670] However, restoring weapons after a possible closure, or creating new weapons that will be necessary to meet the threat Norway may face, will take much longer

[4671] Procurement of necessary materials and construction of permanent installations will take several years

[4672] It may take even longer to build up the educational apparatus and reach the necessary operational and technical level of insight and experience

[4673] As far as possible, it is therefore desirable to make firm and concrete plans for the Armed Forces' further development for periods significantly longer than 5 years

[4674] It will provide the best assurance for good utilization of available resources, it will be a good motivational factor within the Armed Forces, and it will send a clear signal to other countries about Norway's willingness to contribute to stability in our region and assert our national independence

[4675] On the other hand, there are significant uncertainties surrounding a number of factors and conditions that will influence the development of our defense over the next 15-20 years

[4676] The military threat is subject to some of the same types of constraints against rapid change as our own defense

[4677] Nevertheless, the threat cannot be predicted with great certainty in such a long term

[4678] It can change and new technological possibilities can give it new dimensions

[4679] And although it is not currently reasonable to assume that the agreement to eliminate intermediate-range missiles will also lead to reductions in conventional forces, this cannot be ruled out

[4680] NATO countries advocate such reductions through an approach aimed at increasing stability

[4681] The results of such negotiations could also set new framework conditions for our defense

[4682] NATO has been a mainstay in the defense of Western democracies for decades and will undoubtedly continue to be so for as long as we can see

[4683] But within NATO, changes may occur for both political and economic reasons that could affect the possibilities for defending our region

[4684] There are also uncertainties regarding national conditions and dispositions that have consequences for the Armed Forces

[4685] As long as we have had reasonable growth in the country's economy, it has been possible to predict budget developments with relatively good certainty

[4686] We are now facing a period of low growth in the national product

[4687] How long it will take before the country once again has a healthy economic growth is difficult to predict

[4688] During this period, the growth in the defense budget cannot continue unchanged

[4689] There are also uncertainties associated with larger material and construction projects that often extend over several years

[4690] Before contracts are signed, it is often not possible to estimate the costs of the project with great accuracy

[4691] And it often takes a few years from the time the structural proposals for the Armed Forces are designed until this stage is reached in larger projects

[4692] Even if it was clear how large the defense budget would be for several years to come, there would still be some uncertainty about what acquisitions and what kind of activity there would be room for

[4693] The Armed Forces are also facing uncertainties on the personnel side

[4694] Should the strong competition continue in the years ahead, the Armed Forces may have difficulty recruiting and retaining personnel for key civilian and military positions, and thus realizing its goals

[4695] A main task in long-term planning in the Armed Forces is therefore to find a working method and proposals for long-term plans that can capture uncertainties and at the same time provide the long-term perspective in decisions and dispositions that is a prerequisite for good utilization of available resources

[4696] Planning under uncertainty

[4697] Long-term planning in the Armed Forces must be a continuous process that is carried out in appropriate periods

[4698] Each period consists in principle of three main phases

[4699] The first is the examination of alternative plans for developing the composition of the Armed Forces in the long term, assessing the ability of the alternatives to satisfy our defense needs, and calculating the total costs of implementing the plans

[4700] The second phase is the overall military and political choice of the main alternative to be pursued until the next major review and rollout of the long-term planning basis

[4701] The third and final phase is the preparation of more detailed action and implementation plans for the preferred alternative for the upcoming planning period

[4702] The purpose of the first phase, investigation of the alternatives, is to formulate good proposals for alternative development lines, and to clarify the consequences of choosing one or another of them

[4703] Since, as mentioned above, there are significant uncertainties surrounding many of the factors and conditions that will affect our defense in the years ahead, it is particularly important to clarify how the ability of alternative defense structures to meet the country's defense needs is affected by these uncertainties

[4704] In designing the alternatives, the goal must be to find development plans for our defense that provide a defense capability that is insensitive, or as robust as possible, to changes in uncertain conditions

[4705] It is particularly important to design development plans that are well adapted to other economic development lines for the Armed Forces

[4706] The Defense Commission chose a 15-year planning period, 1989-2003, for its work, and considered three different frameworks

[4707] A "high" framework of just over five percent annual growth, a "medium" framework of just over three percent, and a "low" framework of approximately one percent

[4708] The three percent option was recommended as a guideline, and addressed in the report in the form of a 15-year plan

[4709] The growth assumptions for each of the three five-year periods were distributed with four percent for the period 1979-83, three percent for the period 1984-88 and two percent for the period

[4710] The Ministry's internal guidelines for long-term planning, which now run for a corresponding 15-year period, also provide three different financial framework profiles

[4711] However, with the economic development that can be expected in the coming years, the Ministry has found that there is no basis to go beyond a plan that, in accumulated terms, corresponds to an average growth of two percent per year in the period

[4712] However, a lower alternative of 1-1.5 percent will also be investigated

[4713] The table shows the average percentages for the three framework profiles and the increase in the accumulated annual budgets relative to zero growth

[4715] Overall growth

[4716] Behind the low profile lies the need to see which choices of different defense structures will be necessary to make with a lower budget development than that behind today's defense

[4717] The framework limits for the other two profiles are determined more by socio-economic considerations

[4718] They are unlikely to have such an impact on the development of the defense that the structures will have to undergo fundamental changes

[4719] The Ministry considers these assumptions to be preliminary guidelines, and would also like to emphasize that the plans should be prepared with a degree of flexibility that makes it possible to adapt the business to varying growth in individual years

[4720] This planning will help to highlight those parts of the business that are at the limit of the value of the use of the money at any given time

[4721] In this way, planning will also be more strongly linked to productivity increases and rationalization

[4722] In the figure below, which shows the planning profiles, an imaginary budget curve has also been drawn that includes the "middle alternative" allocation profile plus the effect of a one percent productivity improvement

[4725] Studies will also be conducted with frameworks that are significantly lower and higher than those illustrated in the figure

[4726] Using games, simulations and analyses, an attempt will be made to find defense structures that will be adapted to other main assumptions that can cover a greater degree of uncertainty about the future

[4727] Furthermore, an attempt is made to form a picture of how different defense structures can be expected to solve defense tasks in imagined future crisis and war situations

[4728] The time perspective for this work should be 15-20 years

[4732] The main problem in the second phase, the political and military authorities' choice of development alternatives for the immediate planning period, is the decision on how much risk one is willing to accept that the Armed Forces will not be able to solve its various tasks, and which uncertainties should be emphasized

[4733] The overall security risk that must be accepted is highly dependent on the availability of resources to the Armed Forces

[4734] The choice of economic framework assumptions is therefore a particularly important decision as a basis for further planning work

[4735] For this given financial framework, a decision must then be made about which defense tasks and regions of the country should be prioritized and where the greatest security risks should be accepted

[4736] The purpose of the third phase is to develop a sufficiently concrete and detailed plan for the implementation of the chosen development alternative

[4737] This implementation plan is only prepared for the first part of the long-term planning period

[4738] Six years is considered to be an appropriate choice based on considerations of frequency in the roll-over of the long-term plans

[4739] This also corresponds to the time horizon NATO uses in its planning

[4740] The key problem in this third phase is to find the right balance between flexibility to capture the consequences of uncertainties as they materialize, and firmness and long-termism to avoid too frequent and extensive changes in the projects and activities that are initiated

[4741] For the immediate future, the plan must necessarily provide specific instructions on what will happen, while for the somewhat more distant future it is important to keep the possibilities open within the framework of the strategies that follow from the planning decision in phase two

[4742] Unnecessarily early decisions about, for example, the choice of a weapon system and the scope of a procurement project, reduce the opportunities to take unforeseen factors and conditions into account in the planning work

[4743] It is important that the implementation plan identifies as precisely as possible which decisions must be made and at what time, so that the necessary decision-making documentation can be completed in a timely manner

[4744] When specific decisions are made about, for example, the selection and procurement of equipment, it is extremely important to clarify whether and to what extent the choice depends on uncertain factors such as access to resources

[4745] This is done based on the alternative long-term plans prepared in phase

[4746] If, for example, the plan adapted to a lower resource level implies a very different solution to the impending decision problem, this indicates a strong sensitivity to variations in the resource framework

[4747] When such conditions are identified, it is crucial to be able to maintain the highest possible degree of adaptability

[4748] This can, for example, happen through a step-by-step decision in connection with options in, for example, material procurement

[4749] The main idea of ​​this planning concept is to take into account the consequences of the fact that the future contains many important uncertainties

[4750] But it is not possible with such a large and complex apparatus as the Armed Forces to only make short-term decisions and thus keep all options open

[4751] Decisions for major material projects and dispositions concerning the recruitment and training of personnel have long-term consequences

[4752] The overall assessments that lead to the selection of a master plan in phase two must set a long-term main course for future development

[4753] They must indicate the range of variation for the most important uncertainties that must be taken into account in the further and more detailed work on realizing the main course in the period until the next review of the long-term development plans

[4754] The scope of work required to carry out such planning is so great that it cannot be done too often

[4755] On the other hand, the pace of general development outside the Armed Forces indicates that the interval should not be too long

[4756] Five years seems to be a reasonable compromise when it comes to rolling out long-term plans

[4757] However, there is insufficient capacity to conduct thorough studies of a broad spectrum of alternative plans every five years

[4758] Such a major review of the planning basis should be carried out every ten years

[4759] In the efficiency improvement effort, an effort will be made to achieve productivity growth that corresponds to an average annual real growth in the defense budget of one to two percent

[4760] This is justified both by the desire to mitigate expectations regarding the financial resources the State will have at its disposal in the years ahead and by the need to bring about a better match between goals and means

[4761] A strong rationalization effort will stimulate a faster transition to an increasingly cost-effective defense that produces an up-to-date, future-oriented defense capability

[4762] The following main points will be the basis for the work

[4763] A more rigorous operational assessment and critical review of the defense capability created through various activities, acquisition programs, etc

[4764] A more thorough clarification of the cooperation of the various defense elements in solving defense tasks

[4765] The air defense sector is mentioned as an example

[4766] Reduction of operating costs through extensive use of various forms of simulators

[4767] Training can be provided much more cheaply and often better in this way than by using expensive ammunition and high mileage or walking hour costs

[4768] Training through cadre exercises, war games, etc. will be increased

[4769] A continuation of the mobilization and peacetime organization's structural adaptation

[4770] A stronger effort to remove irrational overlaps between different parts of the Armed Forces' peacetime activities

[4771] An assessment and implementation of measures to coordinate the work of the central administrative agencies is the first goal

[4772] In this regard, measures to ensure better coverage of qualified personnel will be a key point

[4773] Overall planning of larger programs where, for example, significant material procurements are to be combined with construction and civil engineering measures, personnel access and training

[4774] Binding of material projects to governing cost frameworks, from the preparation of requirements, through the development phase to procurement, if necessary with a possible reduction in quantity as the final consequence

[4775] To achieve this, freedom of action will be ensured through the use of step-by-step decisions and options

[4776] Consistently exploiting the service life potential of existing weapons platforms by implementing renewal programs instead of choosing completely new programs

[4777] Coordination of national and allied planning

[4778] The design and further development of our defense is a national task

[4779] It is primarily our own deliberations and assessments that form the basis for decisions about the further development of the Armed Forces

[4780] But long-term planning work and decisions are naturally also influenced by current NATO guidelines for the development of collective defense

[4781] At regular intervals, NATO conducts a reassessment of the challenges and of defence needs as a basis for coordinating national defence plans in light of the needs of the common defence

[4782] The time perspective for this planning work in NATO has so far been considerably shorter than what we have been working on in this country for a long time, but long-term force goals and long-term needs have now also been introduced into NATO planning

[4783] Although there is extensive coordination of national plans with NATO's proposed force goals, the degree of alignment varies

[4784] It is not always possible to fully meet NATO's strength goals, which either require resources in addition to national plans or for national plans to be adjusted to fit the Alliance's strength goals

[4785] Deciding which plans and force objectives to implement is in all cases a national responsibility, but consideration for alliance defense and our dependence on allied reinforcements dictates that NATO's force objectives, as far as possible, be incorporated into our own plans

[4786] Division of responsibility and work in long-term planning Long-term planning is organized in accordance with the responsibilities of the Minister of Defence and the Chief of Defence in this area

[4787] The Minister of Defence has overall responsibility for long-term planning

[4788] This includes the formulation of politically determined main guidelines for the planning work, such as budgetary frameworks, personnel guidelines and security policy guidelines and framework conditions

[4789] Furthermore, he is responsible for submitting to the Storting for consideration and approval the guidelines, framework conditions and general goals that will apply to the Armed Forces' ongoing long-term planning

[4790] The resource guidelines are mainly formulated on the basis of the Government's long-term program, while the Ministry of Foreign Affairs participates in security policy issues

[4791] The Chief of Defence is responsible for formulating and presenting proposals for a long-term plan for the further development of the Armed Forces, and for assessing the extent to which the proposals address the defence challenges that the country may face

[4792] He is thus responsible for the practical implementation of ongoing planning in the Armed Forces as this process is described above

[4793] This involves coordinating necessary studies, designing alternative long-term development plans, and preparing more short-term implementation plans within the chosen major

[4794] In this work, the Chief of Defence and his Joint Staff draw on the inspectors general, the operational commanders and the supply commands

[4795] The scope and nature of most of the investigation and impact analysis work that will be done as a basis for long-term planning work is of such a nature that it can hardly be carried out within the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces High Command

[4796] A significant investigative capacity is needed with a high degree of continuity and good insight into security policy, military, technological and cost-related issues

[4797] The Norwegian Defence Research Institute is an important focal point for such analyses as a basis for long-term planning

[4798] In order for these analyses to be based on a sufficiently good foundation of operational insight, it is of crucial importance that the Armed Forces assign officers to continuously participate in these analyses at FFI

[4799] In addition, special expertise is drawn from staffs, school departments and administrative bodies in the Armed Forces

[4800] Control of cost developments for major investment projects

[4801] Already in the design of the alternative development lines in the first phase of the planning process, future material and construction projects are described and assessed

[4802] Based on the knowledge one then has about the characteristics and costs of the projects, proposals for development plans and force structures are designed and coordinated

[4803] As mentioned in section 16.5, this work is carried out primarily by the Chief of Defence and his Joint Staff with support from investigative and analytical bodies

[4804] After a development plan has been selected in phase two of the process and the plan is to be implemented, the main actors are often the respective inspectors general, supply commands, the Armed Forces Building Service, etc

[4805] Military operational requirements for the equipment or facility are prepared, followed by technical specifications and then procurement is carried out

[4806] Very few of the larger acquisitions are pure purchases of finished off-the-shelf goods

[4807] Most often, it involves a certain degree of further development and/or assembly of individual finished elements into systems

[4808] These are extensive and time-consuming processes

[4809] The work is carried out by others than those who prepared the structural proposal and at the later stages of the process more is known about the material than was done in the first phase

[4810] There is therefore a certain risk that the procurement will not sufficiently fall within the cost and other frameworks that the structural proposal assumed

[4811] If that happens, it could easily have consequences for the balance of the entire structure

[4812] To safeguard against such eventualities, the Ministry will establish ad hoc groups of 2-3 people for the largest projects whose task is to stay informed about the project's development and ensure that the defense leadership is informed of significant cost-related or other deviations in the project from the structural plan

[4813] The group will include people who are well familiar with the structural plan and its assumptions on the one hand, and the practical work of implementing the project on the other

[4814] Contact between the Storting and the Ministry of Defence in the planning process

[4815] It is important to have good contact in the planning process between the ministry and the Storting

[4816] This can be done in several ways

[4817] Appointment of political defence commissions has been made only twice after the war, in

[4818] Questions may be raised about how often and how defense commissions should be used

[4819] But regardless of the scope and nature of commission investigations, they should be timed so that they can serve as a useful aid in long-term planning

[4820] When preparing five-year plans, parliamentary contact committees have sometimes been used with representatives appointed by parties represented in the Storting

[4821] Some of the representatives were members of the defense committee

[4822] Parliamentary contact committees have had no constitutional status and have not taken a position on behalf of the parties

[4823] The views that have emerged have nevertheless been important in the preparation of the long-term plans

[4824] In Sweden, a defense commission is appointed by the political parties to prepare and present a new five-year plan

[4825] There is close cooperation between this commission and the Riksdag's Standing Defense Committee (the so-called Defense Committee

[4826] The commission normally works for about three years, presents its proposal to the Government and is dissolved

[4827] This form provides a good basis for a dialogue between a cross-political grouping and the administration

[4828] The consequences of proposed measures are assessed from both a defense and societal perspective and contribute to defense planning being carried out on an economically realistic basis

[4829] The Government wishes to discuss with the Storting suitable future forms of broader political participation in long-term planning for the Armed Forces

[4830] This could be done through a representatively composed liaison body, or through defense commissions when the situation warrants it

[4831] Any new defense commission should be composed with mixed political and military participation, as was the case with the two previous defense commissions after the Second World War

[4832] Developments in the security, military and economic areas in the coming years may make it natural to initiate a comprehensive review, by such a cross-political body, of the planning basis for and design of the Armed Forces towards the 21st century and into the next century

[4833] Preparation for work on the next long-term plan

[4834] A significant part of the analytical basis for the Armed Forces' long-term planning over the past ten years was laid in the latter half of the 1970s, including through the studies carried out in connection with the Defence Commission

[4835] This planning basis must now be reworked in light of changed conditions

[4836] The study should be completed by the end of the upcoming planning period, and should form the basis for a major review of the Armed Forces' long-term plans with a time horizon of

[4837] The aim is to analyze defense branches and an overall integrative defense analysis

[4838] Main guidelines for the activities of the Armed Forces in the period 1989-93 are sent to the Storting

[4839] The Chief of Defence's principled view of the Armed Forces' needs and development 1. Purpose 1.1 In this appendix, the Chief of Defence (FSJ) gives his view of the situation of the Armed Forces and the defence needs in the period 1989-93 and assesses the consequences and effects on defence capability under different economic frameworks and assumptions

[4840] Possible consequences in a longer-term perspective are also assessed

[4841] The appendix builds on the studies conducted through the 1985 Defense Study (FS

[4842] FS 85 has been the basis for the Armed Forces' planning from 1985 to the present, and the Armed Forces' long-term structure has been based on the study's resource-adapted structure (3 percent annual real growth

[4843] FS 85 did not include the consequences of lower resource limits than those applicable to the current period

[4844] Given the current economic uncertainty, FS 85 finds it necessary to also use examples to illustrate the consequences of lower annual growth rates than 3 percent

[4845] The appendix also discusses other key assumptions and elements that affect the structure and activities of the Armed Forces and thereby also defense and combat capability

[4846] The strategic situation and the threat

[4847] Norway's strategic situation is primarily determined by our geographical location between East and West and by weapons technology development

[4848] Section 2.1 Chapter 2 highlights the strategic importance of the High North

[4849] Northern Norway and Southern Norway flank the outlets of two of the Soviet Union's most important maritime bases, both crucial to the Soviet Union in both defensive and offensive contexts

[4850] NATO will have to view these outlets with adjacent sea areas as a forward line of defense in an attempt to stop a possible Soviet attack

[4851] Norway's central location in this strategic area of tension makes us very vulnerable in a possible East-West conflict

[4852] We must assume that the Soviet Union considers Norwegian territory important for advanced defense in the north and in the Baltic Sea area

[4853] In a possible East-West conflict, the area is of significant importance for force deployment in the Norwegian Sea and the Atlantic Ocean and as a flank position to Central Europe

[4854] Trajectories for intercontinental missiles between the Soviet Union and the United States pass over Norwegian territory

[4855] Norway is of great importance as a platform for strategic monitoring and warning

[4856] The Soviet Northern Fleet's combat power has increased significantly over the past fifteen years and has enabled Soviet naval forces to gradually operate further south in the Norwegian Sea

[4857] The developments that have taken place on the vessel and aircraft side have increased the risk that Northern Norway could be isolated for shorter or longer periods

[4858] Although there has been an increased understanding of the necessity of highlighting allied presence in these areas, there is uncertainty about where Western naval units will be located and where they will be deployed in a crisis situation

[4859] The Soviet army and naval infantry forces in the north have also been modernized and have received increased capacity, including increased helicopter capacity, increased fire support and improved mobility

[4860] It must be established that the balance of power in the highlands - also in the context of alliances - is in our disfavor

[4861] The Soviet standing forces in the north, together with reinforcements that can be set up and brought forward very quickly, have sufficient capacity to carry out an isolated and limited attack against parts of northern Norway

[4862] This can be done without us gaining preparation time of practical significance

[4863] However, an attack targeting the Troms area must be assumed to require larger forces than the Soviets have on Kola

[4901] The commission based its assessments on a number of analyses, including the combined efforts of land forces, naval forces and air forces in an invasion defense of the country under several operational alternatives

[4902] This was later summarized in a cross-sectional analysis, called the Defense Analysis

[4904] At the time, FSJ pointed to the need for an increase in the framework that had been given with the aim of increasing defense capabilities in a number of important, specified areas, but otherwise agreed in principle with the commission's recommendation

[5148] Although the combat capability of our own departments has increased and is increasing, our relative combat capability is decreasing

[5149] We are therefore becoming increasingly dependent on allied support

[5150] In FS 85, the FSJ pointed out what, based on a professional military assessment, was necessary to achieve adequate national defense within the framework of the alliance defense

[5151] up to the year

[5152] The adapted structure in FS 85 is based on an assumed annual growth of just over 3 percent

[5153] FSJ considers this to be a minimum structure that should not be undercut or eroded

[5154] With this structure, a satisfactory and balanced national defense can only be built up in parts of the country

[5155] up to the year

[5156] This structure has a number of serious weaknesses that should be corrected

[5157] This will only be possible with annual real budget growth exceeding 3 percent

[5158] To point out the impact on defense capability of a possible lower growth assumption than 3 percent, the FSJ has chosen to illustrate the consequences of a 2 percent framework through examples

[5159] When assessing the consequences, FSJ has considered the strained budget situation at the start of the planning period due to cost developments, new orders and lack of compensation

[5160] Main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities in the period 1989-93 and the effects of lower budget limits

[5161] Both for the upcoming 5-year period and for structural development in the long term, this will lead to a downsizing of the Armed Forces

[5162] Both the peace and war structures must be reduced

[5163] Our ability to prepare and receive allied assistance effectively will be reduced, while our need for such support is increasing

[5164] For the optimization of resources and rational management towards a balanced defense, FSI will point out the importance of the Armed Forces having long-term goals and the most stable frameworks and conditions possible

[5165] For the annual growth to be real, it is important to arrive at a satisfactory calculation methodology for wage and price compensation

[5166] Regardless of the resource framework, FSJ requires a comprehensive effort for rationalization and efficiency in order to limit the growth in operating expenses as much as possible

[5167] Operating expenses are determined by the level of activity to be maintained and the extent of the structure to be developed

[5168] Should the Armed Forces be imposed operating limits that are significantly lower than 1.5 percent growth per year, this will lead to the closure of activities, reduced training activities, poorer maintenance and reduced readiness stocks

[5169] Closing down lower-priority businesses has often proven difficult and time-consuming

[5170] Such measures and organizational changes often meet resistance both among those affected in the Armed Forces and in the local community, and require political will and the ability to make decisions

[5171] MoD considers it essential for future work on rationalization and efficiency that it be possible to close down activities that provide little or no defense capability

[5172] The personnel situation in the Armed Forces is very strained, and further reductions in personnel levels are unlikely to occur without closing departments and reducing activities

[5173] Such measures of any magnitude will also have to lead to a reduction in the total war structure

[5174] FSJ would finally like to emphasize that based on a military assessment of our strategic situation and the military forces that can be deployed against us, there is still a need to improve our defense capabilities

[5175] Our dependence on allied support and allied reinforcements is increasing, but our allies' capacity is also limited in relation to the need

[5176] Strong individual efforts are therefore necessary, both because our security primarily rests on our own will and ability to defend ourselves, and because this is the basis for allied support

[5177] FSJ therefore warns against a development that could, in the long term, reduce our ability for military defense

[5331] The revised command structure (RBO

[5332] The revised command structure (RBO) was adopted by the Storting on 8 June 1983, cf. St prp no. 76 (1982-83), Innss S no. 270 (1982-83), and implemented by the Ministry of Defence from 1 November

[5333] In connection with the RBO, a job analysis was conducted to clarify the need for officers within the individual categories, industries, educational levels and degree levels

[5334] The analysis thus indicated the ideal structure of the professional officer corps

[5335] Changes in the Armed Forces' organization, failing recruitment and a large number of unforeseen departures of professional officers during the period have led to the personnel structure within certain categories of officers deviating significantly from the structure that the position analysis indicated as the ideal one

[5336] There is therefore a need for a re-examination of the job analysis

[5337] This review has been initiated

[5339] The scheme seems to work well, but has been in operation for too short a time for any firm conclusion to be drawn

[5341] However, the scheme places a significantly greater burden on personnel management

[5721] The financial framework for operation and maintenance has experienced real growth of an average of 3 percent during the period

[5724] The workshop survey The activities of the Armed Forces must be run as efficiently, rationally and economically as possible

[5725] One of the measures in this regard is the so-called workshop survey that has been carried out at the Norwegian Armed Forces workshops

[5726] The main purpose is to find a common structure and common main guidelines for the organization and operation of the Armed Forces' maintenance service

[5727] The purpose is thus to achieve better planning and management of operations, better utilization of resources, stronger incentives for profitable operations, better balance between own activities and the purchase of services, etc

[5728] A private company has conducted the investigation in close collaboration with the defense branches' own maintenance personnel

[5729] The investigation has so far resulted in the implementation of a number of measures, primarily in local communities, and a number of proposals for efficiency improvements/simplification

[5730] Proposals for more extensive changes require, among other things, greater dynamism in the workshop organizations

[5731] This indicates greater flexibility in the personnel sector both in terms of the remuneration system and mobility between and across the different agreement areas

[5732] This is being worked on regionally and centrally

[5733] The investigation has also led to stronger coordination and utilization of maintenance resources within defined geographical areas between the defense branches

[5734] In sum, the workshop survey already represents a significant contribution to curbing the growth of operations for the maintenance of a fleet of equipment that is growing rapidly in both scope and complexity

[5735] In general, the maintenance of the armed forces' equipment has been well taken care of, although there are areas in need of improvement and rationalization

[5736] The workshop survey, which seeks to coordinate the workshop capacity of the defense branches within the same area, is part of this

[5737] The maintenance of equipment that is in daily use has been carried out according to a set plan and otherwise when special needs have arisen

[5738] Equipment that is stored for the long term is preserved in advance so that maintenance is largely limited to inspections

[5739] Maintenance of new equipment largely requires people with high-quality technical education

[5740] Today, there is a high demand for such personnel in the civilian market

[5741] This has led to a shortage of people with technical education and maintenance experience

[5742] The Armed Forces have therefore had to purchase maintenance capacity on the civilian market

[5743] Introduction of EDB
