[5745] In this regard, discount agreements have been entered into with suppliers of microcomputers (PCs) that provide the Armed Forces with discounts on purchases and ensure training and spare parts

[5746] The introduction of EDB is a process that will continue in the next period

[5747] Specially qualified personnel

[5748] It has been a problem for the Armed Forces to retain particularly qualified personnel

[5749] The situation has at times been so critical that the progress of certain projects has been threatened, and in many cases it has been necessary to hire consulting services to get the projects completed

[5750] To try to correct this, it has been necessary to increasingly use the State's b regulations

[5751] It has also been necessary to create several time-limited (four-year) project positions

[5752] There has also been a need to strengthen the mercantile side of the supply commands

[5753] Thus, the Army Supply Command has recently used officers from the Naval Academy's Quartermaster Course

[5754] Securing the defense's ammunition and weapons stores

[5755] Securing the Armed Forces' warehouses includes security against ammunition explosions and security against burglary

[5756] In recent years, it has been necessary to grant exemptions from safety distances around ammunition depots, mainly due to new regulations

[5757] To obtain a proper assessment of the risk at ammunition storage facilities, a risk assessment of each individual storage facility is necessary

[5758] When choosing an analysis model, a Swiss-type has been chosen that has also been used by Sweden and West Germany

[5759] It is expected that the review of the stocks will take four to five years

[5760] For emergency preparedness reasons, it is desirable to have the Armed Forces' ammunition and weapons stocks dispersed

[5761] This makes supervision difficult

[5762] To secure the warehouses against burglary, immediate measures have been taken, such as the acquisition of steel boxes and steel cabinets, the installation of alarms and structural measures in the warehouses that are believed to be most vulnerable

[5763] Work on more long-term measures is in full swing

[5764] First of all, the future level of security will be determined and the different technical and economic consequences of different alternatives will be clarified

[5765] Advance storage for allied forces

[5766] Due to military developments in the High North, it has become increasingly important to pre-stock equipment for the Allied forces that are planned to be deployed in Norway in the event of a crisis or war

[5767] The storage has been mentioned in a number of parliamentary documents, including St meld no. 74 for

[5768] The countries that currently have pre-stocked materials in Norway include the USA, the UK, Canada, West Germany and the Netherlands

[5769] As a result of the storage agreements that have been introduced, large quantities of material and fuel have been received and pre-stored, especially in recent years, the vast majority from the United States

[5770] Deliveries began in the early 1980s, and according to current plans will be completed in

[5771] The equipment being pre-stocked is artillery, transport vehicles, special vehicles, equipment for bridge building and other engineering equipment, communications equipment, field hospitals, equipment for smaller medical units, fuel, ammunition, spare parts, provisions, ground equipment for aircraft and general supplies

[5772] The value can be estimated at close to 30 billion kroner, of which 85% is financed by the United States

[5773] Norway is responsible for the maintenance of the equipment, but the expenses are reimbursed

[5774] The pre-stocked material includes only part of the heavier equipment that is expected to be included in the Allied reinforcements

[5775] In the event of a crisis/war, the deployed forces will bring with them large weapons systems such as aircraft, missiles, radar equipment, etc

[5776] This applies primarily to the American units

[5777] The English and Dutch will bring with them practically their entire fleet of equipment

[5778] The planned deployment forces are equipped with a large number of fighter jets, helicopters, reconnaissance aircraft, artillery, missiles, tanks, field hospitals, personal weapons, etc

[5779] The value of the equipment coming with the forces is estimated at approximately NOK 60 billion

[5780] The total value of the material that is being pre-stored and that which is being brought along will thus amount to 90 billion kroner

[5781] As a consequence of the decision to store American MEB equipment in Trøndelag, it was decided that heavier equipment for a Norwegian brigade should be advance stored in Northern Norway

[5782] The brigade's area of operations is Northern Norway, but the equipment has been stored in Southern Norway

[5783] The equipment to be stored is primarily heavier equipment such as tracked vehicles, artillery and anti-aircraft guns, as well as ammunition and fuel

[5784] The lighter equipment will continue to be stored in Southern Norway

[5785] Procurement policy and Norwegian industry

[5786] The Norwegian Armed Forces' procurement programs and other material activities offer significant industrial policy opportunities

[5787] This particularly applies to the restructuring of the industry from being a heavy raw material-based business to the fast-growing knowledge-based industries with international development opportunities

[5788] The use of the Armed Forces' procurement in the context of industrial, employment and regional policy has been actively followed up by the political authorities, by industrial bodies and individual companies

[5789] The work to strengthen industry has been continued during this period, based on Parliamentary Report No. 94 (1978-79) and the Defence Commission's report, which discussed the four main possibilities available for developing industrial involvement

[5790] National research and development contracts and production

[5791] Examples of this form of cooperation include the TADKOM communications system, the PENGUIN missile for the navy and air force, and the command and weapons control system for ULA-class submarines

[5792] Research and development contracts for Norwegian businesses obtained through international agreements

[5793] An example of this form of cooperation during the planning period is the ASRAAM/AMRAAM air-to-air missile systems

[5794] Norwegian production, possibly partial production, achieved through international agreements

[5795] These will be projects where Norwegian industry participates in co-production

[5796] Examples include air-to-air

[5797] the SIDEWINDER missile system and the cooperation between five countries on the production of the F

[5798] This form of co-production can result in increased product costs due to parallel production lines

[5799] This form of cooperation is based on the Armed Forces' procurements abroad, to which separate repurchase agreements are attached

[5800] Examples of agreements entered into in connection with the Armed Forces' procurement during the period include

[5801] ROBOT 70, IHAWK fire control, sonars, tracked vehicles, M 113 armored personnel carriers, cargo trucks and helicopter

[5802] From 1984 to 1987, contracts worth over NOK 4,300 million were signed, which included 24 repurchase agreements with 19 foreign companies

[5803] The value of the repurchase agreements is approximately NOK 3,000 million or approximately 69%

[5804] During the period, cooperation between the Ministry of Industry and the Ministry of Defence has been strengthened to better safeguard the industrial policy aspects of the Defence Procurement

[5805] A coordination group has been established with representatives from both ministries

[5806] An example of the Ministry of Industry's involvement is its participation together with the Ministry of Defence with research and development funds for Norwegian industry as part of the financing of the ASRAAM project in the definition phase

[5807] During the period, the industrial aspects of the Armed Forces' procurements have been given greater importance by both the authorities and the industry and its bodies in light of the goal of restructuring, developing and internationalizing Norwegian industry

[5808] This has in turn meant that the Norwegian Armed Forces' procurements are receiving greater attention and are receiving greater interest from industry

[5809] A large part of the equipment that the Armed Forces currently have at their disposal was acquired during the arms aid programs in the 1950s and 1960s

[5810] Much of this equipment has now reached the end of its technical and economic lifespan

[5811] Military technology has developed significantly in recent years

[5812] Greater performance and efficiency must be paid for with increased prices

[5813] The trade-off between quality and quantity has become an increasingly pressing issue

[5814] During the current planning period, there has been a growing recognition of the need to strengthen international cooperation in the materiel sector

[5815] The main goal of this is that through joint procurement, more favorable prices for the equipment can be achieved and an increased degree of standardization can be achieved

[5816] This ensures interoperability, reduced operating expenses and training costs

[5817] Resupply will also be easier

[5818] Cooperation takes place both bilaterally through separate agreements with individual countries and multilaterally through cooperation bodies in NATO and within the Independent European Programme Group (IEPG

[5819] During the planning period, bilateral cooperation agreements have been signed with the United Kingdom and Sweden

[5820] Similar agreements have previously been signed with the United States, Canada, Germany and France

[5821] As envisaged in Parliamentary Report No. 74 for 1982-83, these agreements are more comprehensive than pure compensation agreements, as emphasis is also placed on cooperation within research and development and on utilizing the expertise that each country already possesses

[5822] The purpose is primarily to provide Norwegian industry with new expertise and thereby opportunities to compete in a larger market

[5823] In connection with procurements from abroad, the Ministry of Defence has also entered into repurchase agreements

[5824] The negotiations for repurchase have taken place within the framework of the general agreement with the country in question, and are arranged in the form of industrial agreements between the supplier and the Ministry of Defense

[5825] The agreements primarily emphasize cooperation between foreign suppliers and Norwegian industry within high-technology areas, and that the repurchases will primarily take place from the Norwegian defense industry

[5826] The result of this work is that large parts of the material investments lead to assignments for Norwegian industry, even if the contracts go to foreign suppliers

[5827] Within NATO, a strategy was adopted in 1985 for coordinated materiel planning and the introduction and use of new technology to better utilize common resources

[5828] The strategy involves the initiation of both specific materiel projects and various studies of defense planning

[5829] Norway is participating in a project within advanced data/communications technology

[5830] This concerns data processing of images in connection with missiles

[5831] FFI plays a central role in the work together with relevant Norwegian industry that has been involved

[5832] Within NATO, there is a separate organization, the NATO Materiel Supply Agency (NAMSA), where resupply of materiel is coordinated and which is widely used by several NATO countries

[5833] This ensures better and more affordable access to spare parts, and that any modernizations are carried out jointly

[5834] Within the IEPG which consists of 13 NATO countries

[5835] At the initiative of the Ministers of Defense, material and development projects have been launched

[5836] Norway actively participates in several of these, both from the government and industry perspective

[5837] In terms of specific projects, we are participating in the development of a future surface-to-air missile that will replace the HAWK missile

[5838] The pure research and development projects are led by FFI in collaboration with competent Norwegian industry

[6047] The Planning and Building Act of 14 June 1985 No. 77, which, among other things, gives municipalities the opportunity to self-approve their municipal plans, has led to a need to strengthen and restructure the Armed Forces' building service and work routines in relation to municipal planning

[6048] The Ministry has thereby sought to safeguard the interests and participation of the Armed Forces in municipal, county and conservation planning contexts

[6049] During the planning period, the Ministry has continued to work on establishing new shooting and training ranges in line with the Armed Forces' needs

[6050] In this context, efforts have been made to expand and lease existing training areas, as well as to transfer training areas rented on short-term contracts to more permanent arrangements

[6051] In St. prp no. 86 for 1979-80, the Storting was informed of the Armed Forces' need for larger regional training areas

[6052] In this context, it was determined that the Armed Forces need 3 regional shooting ranges, 1 in Northern Norway, 1 in Trøndelag and 1 in Eastern Norway

[6053] Development of regional fields

[6054] Northern Norway is expected to be continued by connecting the existing shooting ranges

[6055] Mauken and Blåtind

[6056] In Trøndelag, the field is thought to be located in Nordfosen

[6057] Regional fields for Eastern Norway are still under investigation

[6058] With regard to the clause of security zones, the Ministry has found it necessary to adopt a restrictive stance with regard to exempting such zones around ammunition depots

[6059] There is therefore reason to expect increased costs for this in the future

[6060] Furthermore, the civil planning authorities have become more restrictive regarding noise protection

[6061] In addition, land acquisition costs will depend on the pace of construction and the materials sector

[6062] Jointly financed construction and civil engineering works

[6063] In the period 1984-88, the allocations to the jointly financed infrastructure program were as follows (in million kroner

[6064] Year / Allocation incl. VAT / National costs / Norway's contribution to NATO / Net grants / Allocations as a percentage of the 1984 defense budget

[6065] The NATO infrastructure program has experienced a strong increase over the past 10 years

[6066] In the five-year period 1974-79, the total allocation was NOK 10.4 billion for distribution among the participating countries

[6067] The next five-year plan, 1980-85, increased this amount to 24.5 billion kroner and the current NATO long-term plan 1985-90 has a framework of 64.4 billion kroner, based on the exchange rate in

[6068] In the financial settlement for infrastructure, the reference unit used is the IAU (Infrastructure Accounting Unit), which is calculated based on the exchange rate of the member countries' currencies in relation to Belgian francs

[6069] A devaluation/revaluation of the Norwegian krone will primarily result in Norway's contribution to the total program in the member states increasing or decreasing

[6070] This has meant that the total programme for the period 1985-90, which was approximately 64.4 billion in 1985 kroner, has increased to approximately 80 billion (1988 kroner) due to the exchange rate development between the Norwegian kroner and the currencies of the other member states, and Norway's contribution will therefore increase by just over 400 million kroner

[6071] NATO's long-term programme for 1985-90 was adopted by NATO's Defence Planning Committee in December 1984 and now comprises a rolling six-year programme, compared to the previous five-year fixed programme

[6072] At the same time, it was decided that Norway's contribution would increase from 3.14% to 3.17%

[6073] In connection with the consideration of the new long-term program, it was also decided to introduce new procedures, which will improve the utilization of the funds made available by the participating countries

[6074] In order to facilitate the participating countries' budget estimates for their share of the common expenses, it was decided at the same Council meeting that an upper limit for the participating countries' contributions to the following annual budget should be set at least one year in advance

[6075] For Norway, these costs constitute 3.17% of the total expenditure on all buildings and facilities in all member states and appear in the table above as Norway's contribution to NATO

[6076] Three annual programs have been approved by the Storting of NATO's new long-term plan

[6077] This applies to part 36 (St prp no. 90 for 1984-85), part 37 (St prp no. 70 for 1985-86) and part 38 (St prp no. 68 for

[6078] It normally takes five to eight years to complete work on a part of the infrastructure program and Norway's contribution will be distributed over the same period

[6079] The facilities that can be financed through the jointly financed building and construction program must fall under the approved project categories

[6080] The distribution of all projects in Norway between the different categories has been as follows

[6081] Project Category / Pct

[6082] Various smaller facilities

[6083] National expenses related to jointly financed buildings and facilities, such as land acquisitions, road, water and electricity supply, as well as value added tax, etc., are added

[6084] It is estimated that these expenses constitute approximately 25% of the amount financed by NATO

[6085] The annual jointly financed construction budgets contain a significant material component that includes projects related to communications facilities, command, control and information systems, and warning systems

[6086] During the period, the material share totaled approximately NOK 1.3 billion, distributed as follows

[6087] Percentage of the defense budget

[6088] Avg

[6089] The most important project in the period 1984-88 is the advance storage in Trøndelag for an American marine infantry brigade

[6090] The project includes the construction of three equipment depots, three ammunition depots and improvements to Værnes and Ørland airports

[6091] A total of five municipalities are affected by the project that is currently underway

[6092] In connection with the agreement with the US government on advance storage of equipment for a US naval expeditionary brigade in Trøndelag, it was decided to establish storage for another Norwegian brigade in Northern Norway

[6093] These warehouses have now been approved by NATO for joint financing and are expected to commence during the current period

[6094] During this period, warehouses were built in northern Norway for a Canadian infantry battalion group and a Dutch/British amphibious force

[6095] The following projects have been initiated and are expected to be completed during the period

[6096] development of war headquarters at Kolsås, Reitan and Jåtta - development of Ørland main air station for operating the NATO airborne early warning system (NAEW

[6097] At the same time, significant improvement and expansion work is underway at our airports, especially Andøya, Bardufoss, Bodø and Evenes, so that they can receive allied air reinforcements in a crisis situation

[6098] The construction of three new early warning radars is in the final stages

[6099] This applies to silo radars on Skykula, Vågsøy and Vestvågsøy

[6100] These are all built according to a new concept in that they can be lowered into the mountain when there is a risk of them being destroyed

[6101] They represent a new generation of radars and are the first of their kind in NATO

[6102] In addition to the pure infrastructure projects, some projects have been implemented on a bilateral basis

[6103] In collaboration with Canada, a 200-person shelter has been built on Andøya

[6104] The base is used by Canada during exercises, and by Norway the rest of the year

[6105] For the Americans, storage halls for aircraft ground equipment have been built at all COB airports, warehouses for two American field hospitals in Trøndelag and Northern Norway, respectively, and equipment for repairing damaged runways at airports

[6106] According to bilateral agreements, the facilities are Norwegian property

[6107] Building maintenance includes maintenance of the entire building stock, i.e. nationally and jointly financed buildings and facilities

[6108] The maintenance allocation has been given a slight increase throughout the period

[6109] Requirements for raising standards, increasing the number of buildings and the fact that the Armed Forces still has a number of older establishments are putting pressure on the allocation

[6110] Funds have been allocated annually for energy saving (ENØK) measures

[6111] The ENØK measures essentially aim to improve buildings' insulation, automatically manage energy consumption, and facilitate the use of alternative energy sources such as oil, electricity, and district heating

[6112] The annual allocations for energy efficiency measures have increased from approximately six to nine million kroner during the planning period

[6113] The intention is that the costs of ENØK measures will be saved through reduced operating costs over a three-year period

[6114] In 1986, a program began to improve the standard of older crew accommodations

[6115] The estimated cost over a four-year period was approximately NOK 94 million, which was covered by annual allocations of approximately NOK 16 million under the maintenance budget and approximately NOK 10 million under the investment budget

[6116] The program will be substantially completed during the planning period

[6117] The following has been allocated for the maintenance of buildings and facilities during the period (in million NOK

[6118] In the budget proposals for the period, the ministry has been authorized to enter into agreements of up to five years' duration for the maintenance of buildings and structures and housing

[6119] Construction and construction operations

[6120] Operation of buildings and facilities includes operating expenses for both nationally and jointly financed buildings and facilities

[6121] Fees for public services, rental costs, electricity, fuel and expenses for cleaning agencies and security companies, etc. are included in operating expenses

[6122] The appropriations to cover operating expenses for buildings and structures have increased somewhat during the period and have amounted to (in million kroner

[6123] The implemented energy-saving measures, discussed in more detail under maintenance, have a beneficial effect on operating costs

[6124] Construction for the Coast Guard

[6125] The construction and civil engineering works for the Coast Guard at Sortland, Ramsund, Andøya and Bardufoss have been completed during the planning period

[6126] The most important development has taken place at Sortland, including a quay, administration building, workshop, warehouses, accommodation with halls and housing

[6127] Hangars, housing and accommodation have been built at Bardufoss and Andøya, and warehouses and offices have been built in Ramsund

[6128] The total costs for construction and facilities for the Coast Guard amount to approximately NOK 192 million

[6129] In addition, a quay facility and offices have been built at Haakonsvern for approximately NOK 10 million

[6130] Relatively small amounts have been allocated for the operation and maintenance of buildings and facilities during the period
